ARTICLE 1. INCORPORATION, FORM OF GOVERNMENT, POWERS, GENERAL ELECTIONS
§ 1-101 INCORPORATION.
   The City of Lexington, Oklahoma, within the corporate limits as now
established or as hereafter may be established, shall continue to be a
municipal body politic and corporate in perpetuity under the name of the “City
of Lexington, Oklahoma.” It shall succeed to and possess all the property,
rights, privileges, franchises, powers and immunities now belonging to the
corporation known as the City of Lexington, Oklahoma, and shall be liable for
all debts and other obligations for which the corporation is now legally bound.
§ 1-102 FORM OF GOVERNMENT.
   The municipal government provided by this code shall be known as the “City
Council form of government.” All powers of the city shall be exercised in the
manner as the Council may prescribe by ordinance; provided, that this code and
other ordinances which may be enacted are not repugnant to the Constitution and
laws of the state.
§ 1-103 GENERAL POWERS OF CITY.
   (A)   The city shall have all powers, functions, rights, privileges,
franchises and immunities granted to cities by the State Constitution and state
law and all the implied powers necessary to carry into execution all the powers
granted. Except as prohibited by the State Constitution and state law, the city
shall have all municipal powers, functions, rights, privileges, franchises and
immunities of every name and nature whatsoever.
   (B)   The city shall have power to adopt a corporate seal and to alter it at
pleasure, to sue and to be sued and to make contracts. It shall have power to
acquire property within or without its corporate limits for any city purpose
(including public utilities, works and ways) in fee simple; or any lesser
interest or estate, by purchase, gift, devise, lease, condemnation or other
legal means; and to hold, maintain, improve, enlarge, manage, control, operate,
lease, sell, convey or otherwise dispose of such property as its interest may
require (including public utilities, works and ways). It shall have power to
issue bonds in the manner and within the limitations prescribed by the State
Constitution and state law. It shall have power, within the limits prescribed
by the State Constitution and state law, to accept and administer federal and
state grants in aid and to do everything necessary to accomplish the purpose or
purposes for which such grants may be made. It shall have power to ordain and
to enforce local legislation, consistent with the State Constitution and state
law, for the proper organization and functioning of the city government, for
the preservation and enforcement of good government and order, for the
protection of health, life, morals and property, for the promotion of the
common welfare. It shall have power to grant, extend and renew franchises in
accordance with the State Constitution and state law. It shall have the power
to make all contracts and do all other acts in relation to the property and
affairs of the city necessary to the good government of the city.
   (C)   The enumeration of particular powers by this code shall not be deemed
to be exclusive or limiting; in addition to the powers enumerated herein or
implied hereby, the city shall have all powers which, under the State
Constitution and state law, it would be competent for this code specifically to
enumerate.
§ 1-104 GENERAL ELECTION.
   General elections shall be held on the first Tuesday in April 1995, and each
two years thereafter.
ARTICLE 2. CITY COUNCIL
§ 1-201 COUNCIL MEMBERS; NUMBER, ELECTION, OFFICERS, TERMS, COMPENSATION.
   (A)   The City Council shall be composed of five members. The Council
members shall be residents and registered voters of the city. The Council
members from wards shall be actual residents of their respective wards at the
time of their candidacy and election; but removal of a Council member from one
ward to another within the city after his or her election, or a change in ward
boundaries, shall not disqualify him or her from completing the term for which
he or she was elected.
   (B)   Commencing on the first Tuesday in April 1995, Council members 1, 3
and 5 shall be elected for terms of four years; at the general election on the
first Tuesday in April, 1997, Council members of Wards 2 and 4 shall be elected
for terms of four years. The terms of officials elected under this section
shall begin at 12:00 p.m. on the second Monday following their election, and
they shall serve until their successors are elected and qualified.
   (C)   Each elected Council member shall be compensated as follows: $150 per
month.
(Ord. 2021-04, passed 5-4-2021)
§ 1-202 CITY COUNCIL POWERS.
   Except as otherwise provided in this code, all powers of the city, including
the determination of all matters of policy, shall be vested in the Council.
Without limitation of the foregoing, the City Council shall have the following
powers granted by the Constitution and statutes of the state:
   (A)   To have a common seal and alter the same;
   (B)   To purchase, hold, sell or convey any estate, real or personal, for
the use of the city, so far as such purchase may be necessary to carry out the
objects contemplated;
   (C)   To organize fire companies and the like and govern their activities;
   (D)   To declare what constitutes a nuisance and to take whatever measures
are necessary to remove, abate and prevent the same, and such other measures as
they deem necessary for preservation of public health;
   (E)   To restrain any animals from running at large;
   (F)   To restrain and prohibit gambling and other disorderly conduct; to
suppress and prohibit keeping houses of ill fame; and to authorize the seizure
and destruction of gambling apparatus;
   (G)   To establish and regulate markets and build market houses; to direct
the location of slaughterhouses;
   (H)   To lay out, open, grade and otherwise improve the streets, alleys,
sewers, sidewalks and crossings and to keep them in repair;
   (I)   To appoint Street Commissioners and Fire Wardens, not exceeding three;
   (J)   To prohibit encumbrance of the sidewalks, and riding or driving
thereon, except to cross the same;
   (K)   To provide means for keeping and preserving the peace and quietness by
appointment of a City Marshal and/or other means;
   (L)   To ensure the public property of the city;
   (M)   To purchase, lay out and regulate cemeteries;
   (N)   To plant trees upon public grounds and along the streets, provide for
their culture and preservation, and to enclose any public square or public
grounds within the city;
   (O)   To provide for annual taxes;
   (P)   To make and establish such bylaws, ordinances and regulations not
repugnant to the laws of this state, as may be necessary to carry into effect
the provisions of this code, and to repeal, alter or amend the same as they
shall seem to the Council to require; but every bylaw, ordinance or regulation,
unless in case of emergency, shall be published in a newspaper of the city, if
one be printed therein, or posted in five public places, at least ten days
before the same shall take effect;
   (Q)   To enact fines, penalties and forfeitures for violation of this code,
or of any bylaw or ordinance by them established, which fine may be recovered
by action in the name of the city; but such Council may remit the whole or any
part of the fine, penalty or forfeiture; and
   (R)   To authorize the construction and maintenance of streets, water mains,
water pipes, gas mains and pipes, electric lines and telephone wire along or
through the streets and alleys within the corporate limits, and to grant rights
and franchises to persons, associations or corporations for such purpose, under
the provisions of Article 18, §§ 5a and 5b of the State Constitution; but no
exclusive right shall be granted for any such purpose. The use of streets may
be granted on the same terms to all desiring to compete with each other in the
business of furnishing gas, electricity, telephone accommodations or water, and
all shall be subject to reasonable regulations by ordinance, which ordinance
may be changed at the pleasure of the City Council.
§ 1-203 CITY COUNCIL; OTHER POWERS.
   (A)   The Council may levy and collect a license tax on auctioneers,
contractors, druggists, hawkers, peddlers, brokers, bankers, pawnbrokers,
merchants of all kinds, grocers, confectioners, restaurants, butchers, taverns,
public counseling houses, billiard and pool tables, bowling alleys, carts,
wagons and all other vehicles used in the city or village for pay; hay scales,
lumber dealers, furniture dealers, saddle and harness dealers, jewelers, real
estate agents, express companies or agencies, shows, theaters, all exhibitions
for pay, doctors, dentists, blacksmiths, all manufacturing establishments,
cotton gins, mills and elevators and plumbers; provided, however, that all
scientific or literary lecturers and entertainments shall be exempt from
taxation, and also all concerts and musical or other entertainments given
exclusively by citizens of the city. The tax so levied and collected therefrom
shall be applied for the use and benefit of the city as may be directed by the
City Council of Council members thereof.
   (B)   The Council may establish or adopt a pension, retirement and/or Social
Security system or systems for any or all groups of the officers and employees
in the service of the city, either alone or in cooperation with the state or
federal government, or both.
§ 1-204 CITY COUNCIL; APPROPRIATION OF MONIES.
   All monies, however derived, belonging to the city, shall only be
appropriated for such objects and defraying such expenses as accrue or
necessarily arise in the exercises of powers granted the Council members by
this code.
§ 1-205 CITY COUNCIL; INDUCTION INTO OFFICE, MEETINGS.
   (A)   On the second Tuesday following their election, the Council members
shall initiate their terms of office by taking and subscribing, before a person
of authority to administer the same, the usual oath or affirmation for the
faithful performance of their duties.
   (B)   The Council shall meet regularly at least once monthly at such times
as it may prescribe by ordinance or resolution. Special meetings may be called
by the Council members. All meetings shall be open to the public and the
journal of its proceedings shall be given to public inspection.
§ 1-206 CITY COUNCIL; REMOVAL OF MEMBERS.
   The Mayor or any other member may be removed from office for any cause
specified by applicable state law for the removal of officers, and by the
method or method prescribed thereby.
§ 1-207 CITY COUNCIL; VACANCIES.
   The Council, by majority vote of its remaining members, shall fill vacancies
in its own membership for the unexpired term.
§ 1-208 CITY COUNCIL; QUORUM, RULES, YEAS, NAYS.
   A majority of all the members of the Council shall constitute a quorum to do
business, but a smaller number may adjourn from day to day. The Council shall
determine its own rules and may compel the attendance of absent members in the
manner and under penalties as the Council may prescribe. On the demand of any
member, the vote on any question shall be by yeas and nays and shall be entered
in the minutes. An abstention shall be a no vote.
§ 1-209 ORDINANCES; ENACTING CLAUSE.
   The enacting clause of all ordinances passed by the Council shall be “Be it
Ordained by the Council of the City of Lexington, Oklahoma,” and of all
ordinances proposed by the voters under their power of initiative “Be it
Ordained by the People of the City of Lexington, Oklahoma.”
§ 1-210 ORDINANCES; PASSAGE, WHEN IN EFFECT.
   Every proposed ordinance shall be read and a vote of a majority of all the
Council members shall be required for the final passage of an ordinance. The
vote on final passage of every ordinance shall be by yeas and nays and shall be
entered in the journal. The Mayor shall have no power to veto. Every ordinance,
except an emergency ordinance, shall be published in full or by title when such
is allowed by the statutes of the state, within 15 days after its passage, in a
legal newspaper of general circulation within the city. Every ordinance except
an emergency ordinance shall become effective 30 days after its final passage
unless it specifies a later time.
§ 1-211 ORDINANCES; EMERGENCY.
   An emergency ordinance is an ordinance which, in the judgment of the
Council, is necessary for the immediate preservation of peace, health or
safety, and which should become effective prior to the time when an ordinary
ordinance would become effective. Every such ordinance shall contain, as part
of its title, the words “and declaring an emergency,” and in a separate section
herein called the emergency section shall declare the emergency. The Council
shall vote on the emergency section separately and must adopt the section by a
vote of at least three-fourths of all the members of the Council, which vote
shall be by yeas or nays and be entered in the journal. An emergency ordinance
shall take effect upon passage unless it specifies a later time.
§ 1-212 ORDINANCES; ADOPTION BY REFERENCE.
   The Council, by ordinance, may adopt by reference codes, ordinances and
standards relating to building, plumbing, electrical installations, milk and
milk products and other matters which it has power to regulate otherwise. Such
a code, ordinance or standard so adopted need not be enrolled in the book of
ordinances; one copy shall be filed and kept in the office of the City Clerk.
The City Clerk shall keep copies of every such code, ordinance or standard in
force for distribution or sale at their approximate cost.
§ 1-213 ORDINANCES; CODIFICATION OF MUNICIPAL ORDINANCES AND PENAL ORDINANCES,
PUBLICATION, FILING.
   (A)   The City Council or a Council member may, from time to time, authorize
a codification of its ordinances. Such a code may be kept up to date by use of
a loose leaf system and the process of amendment.
   (B)   At least three copies of this code shall be kept in the office of the
City Clerk for public use, inspection and examination. The City Clerk shall
keep copies of the code for distribution or sale at a reasonable price.
   (C)   Notice of the publication of the code shall be in the manner provided
for publication by title of certain codes and ordinances by 11 O.S. § 14-107
(A).
   (D)   (1)   Penal ordinances of the city shall be compiled and published in
a permanent form, either printed or typed, periodically, but not less than once
every ten years. The city shall also publish biennial supplements to the
permanent volume of compiled penal ordinances. No municipal ordinance shall be
enforced if it is not reflected in such a permanent volume or supplement if the
ordinance was adopted before the latest compilation or supplement. A
codification of municipal ordinances which includes all penal ordinances is
sufficient for complying with these compilation requirements if the code is
issued as a permanent volume with biennial supplements and if the procedure for
filing and notice, as outlined below have been complied with.
      (2)   Provided, further, the ten-year codification requirement shall be
satisfied if the code complies with the compilation requirement and the
biennial supplements are made a part of the permanent volumes which are
maintained in permanent form either bound or in a loose leaf form.
   (E)   (1)   When the city has compiled and published its permanent volume or
biennial supplement of penal ordinances, the City Council shall adopt a
resolution notifying the public of the publication. A copy of the resolution
shall be filed in the office of County Clerk. At least one copy of the
permanent volume and each biennial supplement shall be deposited free of cost
by the municipality in the County Law Library.
      (2)   The permanent volume or biennial supplement of compiled penal
ordinances shall be available for purchase by the public at a reasonable price.
ARTICLE 3. OFFICERS AND EMPLOYEES
§ 1-301 MAYOR.
   (A)   The Council shall elect one of its members as Mayor. The Mayor shall
be elected in each odd-numbered year at the first Council meeting held after
member terms begin or as soon thereafter as practicable. The Mayor shall serve
until his or her successor has been elected and qualified.
   (B)   The Mayor shall preside over meetings of the Council and may call
special meetings thereof. He or she shall sign all warrants properly and
legally drawn upon the City Treasurer.
   (C)   The Mayor shall certify to the correct enrollment of all ordinances
and resolutions passed by the Council. He or she shall be recognized as the
head of the city government for all ceremonial purposes and by the Governor for
the purposes of military law. He or she shall sign such written obligations of
the city as the Council may require.
   (D)   The Mayor shall have all the powers, rights, privileges, duties and
responsibilities of a member, including the right to vote on questions.
   (E)   During the absence, disability or suspension of the Mayor, the Council
shall elect from among its members an acting Mayor. When a vacancy occurs in
the office of Mayor, the Council shall elect another Mayor from among its
members to serve for the duration of the unexpired term.
   (F)   The Mayor shall perform all other duties prescribed by law or
ordinance.
§ 1-302 CITY CLERK.
   (A)   The City Clerk shall be an officer of the city and shall have custody
of the records, books and papers of the City Council and shall attend all
meetings and record the proceedings of said Council to include all bills and
warrants as to name, amount and claim number.
   (B)   The City Clerk shall be custodian of the seal of the city and shall
attest and affix the seal to documents when required in accordance with the
applicable law or ordinance.
   (C)   The City Clerk shall keep a condensed summary of all ordinances passed
which shall be filed in the office of the City Clerk and kept there for public
use and inspection and examination.
   (D)   The City Clerk shall make the records of the city available to the
public in accordance with the provisions of the State Open Records Act, being
51 O.S. § 24A.1, and have custody of the archives, documents and records of the
city.
   (E)   The City Clerk is authorized and empowered to issue a second or
duplicate warrant or voucher that has been lost or destroyed; but not until
after an affidavit setting forth the facts as to the loss or destruction of
said original warrant or voucher has been filed with the City Clerk together
with an indemnifying bond, running to the City Treasurer, in the amount of such
lost or destroyed warrant or voucher.
   (F)   The City Clerk shall have such other duties as prescribed by law,
ordinance or the City Manager. The salary for the City Clerk shall be set by
the City Council.
§ 1-303 CITY TREASURER.
   (A)   The City Treasurer shall be an officer of the city and shall deposit
daily funds received for the city in depositories as the City Manager may
designate.
   (B)   (1)   The salary for the City Treasurer shall be set by the City
Council. The City Treasurer may be required to perform certain other duties
which shall be described by the City Manager.
      (2)   The pay for such additional duties shall also be set by the City
Council.
   (C)   The books and accounts of the City Treasurer shall be subject at all
times to examination by the City Manager.
   (D)   The same person may hold both the office of the City Treasurer and the
office of the City Clerk.
(Ord. 23-015, passed 12-5-2023)
§ 1-304 CITY ATTORNEY.
   (A)   The City Attorney shall be appointed by the City Manager. He or she
shall be of good moral character, licensed to practice law in the state and
shall be subject to removal at the request of the City Manager.
   (B)   It shall be the duty of the City Attorney to give legal advice on
questions submitted to him or her by the City Manager (or other city officials)
when the subject matter concerns their powers or the performance of their
duties. Additionally, he or she shall draw such ordinances, resolutions,
notices, forms, leases, deeds, papers or other documents as may be required of
him or her by the City Manager.
§ 1-305 CHIEF OF POLICE.
   (A)   The Chief of Police shall be appointed by the City Manager. The Chief
of Police may appoint police officers as he or she deems necessary, subject to
the approval and confirmation of the City Manager.
   (B)   The Chief of Police and police officers shall possess the powers and
be subject to the liabilities possessed and conferred by law in executing their
orders or enforcing the code of ordinances of the city.
   (C)   It shall be the duty of the Police Department, Chief of Police and/or
police officers to bring justice to all violators of city ordinances, federal
and state laws, and to turn such violators over to the proper authorities. The
Chief of Police shall serve all warrants, writs, executions and other process
properly directed and delivered to him or her.
   (D)   The Chief of Police and each police officer shall be paid such
compensation as the City Manager may prescribe.
   (E)   The Chief of Police shall perform all other duties prescribed by law
or ordinance.
   (F)   (1)   All personal property which comes into the possession of any
police officer, which has been found or stolen or taken off the person or out
of the possession of any prisoner or person suspected of or charged with being
a criminal, and which is not known to belong to some person laying claim
thereto, shall be, by the officer securing possession thereof, delivered into
the charge of the Chief of Police.
      (2)   The Chief of Police shall, in a permanent record book kept for that
purpose, make a record sufficient to identify the property, with the date and
circumstances of the receipt thereof, the name of the person from whom it was
taken or the place where it was found, and the record shall also disclose the
subsequent disposal thereof, giving the date of sale, name and address of the
purchaser and the amount for which it was sold. (Sales shall be conducted in
accordance with the provisions of 11 O.S. § 34-104.)
§ 1-306 MUNICIPAL JUDGE AND ALTERNATE AND ACTING JUDGES.
   (A)   There shall be one judge of the court, and he or she shall be
appointed by the Mayor with the consent of the City Council. The City Council
may decide upon a proposed appointment by a majority vote at a quorum present
and acting. The Mayor may be designated as judge upon approval of the City
Council.
   (B)   The Judge shall be at least 21 years of age, and, if he or she is not
an attorney, a resident of the city or a suitable person residing within 20
miles of the boundaries of the city. A judge who is a licensed attorney may be
a nonresident, but he or she must reside in the county or an adjacent county or
maintain a permanent office in the municipality. He or she may engage in the
practice of law in other courts, but he or she shall not accept employment
inconsistent with his or her duties as a judge, or arising out of facts which
give rise to or are connected with cases within the jurisdiction of the court,
pending therein, or which might become the subject of proceedings therein. A
resident of the municipality need not be an attorney licensed to practice law.
   (C)   If the Judge of the Municipal Court is not a licensed attorney, the
trial shall be to the court and the court may not impose a fine and costs
which, taken together, exceed $50, and may not order the defendant imprisoned,
except for the nonpayment of fines or costs.
   (D)   The official term of the Judge shall be two years expiring on the
second Monday of January, in each odd-numbered year. The Judge, unless sooner
removed by majority vote of the Council, shall serve until his or her successor
is appointed and qualified.
   (E)   The Judge of the Court shall receive a salary as prescribed by the
City Council, paid in the same manner as the salaries of other officials of the
city.
   (F)   The Judge may prescribe rules, consistent with the laws of the state
and with the ordinances of the city, for the proper conduct of the business of
the courts.
   (G)   There may be appointed an alternate judge of the court possessed of
the same qualifications as the Judge. His or her appointment shall be for the
same term and made in the same manner as the Judge. He or she shall sit as
acting judge of the court in any case if the Judge is absent from the court,
unable to act as judge or disqualified from acting as judge in any case. If at
any time there is no judge or alternate judge duly appointed and qualified
available to sit as judge, the Mayor shall appoint some third person possessing
the qualifications required by this chapter for the Judge, who shall preside as
acting judge over the court in the disposition of pending matters until such
time as a judge or alternate judge shall be available.
   (H)   An alternate judge or an acting judge shall be paid as prescribed by
the City Council for each day devoted to the performance of his or her duties,
except that, for any month, the total payments so calculated shall not exceed
the salary of the Judge in whose stead he or she sits. An alternate or acting
judge who sits for an entire month shall receive the amount specified in this
chapter as the salary of the Judge in whose stead he or she sits.
   (I)   Judges shall be subject to removal from office by the City Council for
the causes prescribed by the Constitution and laws of the state for the removal
of public officers.
   (J)   A vacancy in the office of judge shall occur if the incumbent dies,
resigns, ceases to possess the qualifications for the office, or is removed and
the removal proceedings have been affirmed finally in judicial proceedings, or
are no longer subject to judicial review. Upon the occurrence of a vacancy in
the office of judge, the City Council shall appoint a successor to complete the
unexpired term upon the same procedure as an original appointment is made.
§ 1-307 CITY BOARD OF HEALTH.
   (A)   The City Council may constitute a Board of Health which shall perform
all the duties provided or required by law.
   (B)   The Board of Health shall be under the supervision of the County
Department of Health and the State Department of Health.
   (C)   It shall be the general duty of the Board of Health to examine and
consider all measures necessary for the preservation of the public health of
the city to see that all ordinances and regulations in relation thereto are
observed.
   (D)   To assist in carrying out the provisions of this section, the Board of
Health may appoint a Health Officer to serve the city.
§ 1-308 FIRE DEPARTMENT COMPOSITION.
   The Fire Department shall consist of the Fire Chief, the Fire Marshal, the
assistant Fire Chief and other such officers (investigators, inspectors,
training, mechanical shop and firefighters) as may be designated from time to
time by the City Manager, with the approval of the City Council.
(Ord. 24-011, passed 7-2-2024)
§ 1-309 FIRE CHIEF.
   (A)   Office created. There is hereby created the office of Chief of the
Fire Department. The Fire Chief shall have general supervision over all
property and employees of the Fire Department and shall see that each employee
does his or her duty. The Fire Chief shall designate which position and what
employment each employee shall take in the Department. The Fire Chief shall
have the power to suspend any employee of the Department, subject to the
approval of the City Manager and shall be responsible for all duties contained
within division (B) below. Within 30 days of the vacancy of this position, the
Fire Department shall notify the members of the City Council and the City
Manager of the individual chosen by the Fire Department, according to their own
bylaws and/or such other internal regulations as they see fit, to serve in the
capacity of the Chief of the Fire Department. Such individual shall be
considered and may be appointed by the City Manager. He or she shall hold this
position until removed for the good of the service or until death, resignation
or incapacity.
   (B)   Duties.
      (1)   The Fire Chief shall be at the head of the Fire Department, subject
to the laws of the state and the provisions of this article and other
ordinances of the city. He or she shall diligently perform the duties imposed
upon him or her by law and by ordinance.
      (2)   The Chief shall be held responsible for the general condition and
efficient operation of the Department and the training of members.
      (3)   The Chief may inspect or cause to be inspected by members of the
Department, the fire hydrants, cisterns and other sources of water supply at
least twice each year.
      (4)   The Chief shall maintain a library file of publications on fire
prevention and fire protection and shall make use of it to the best advantage
of all members.
      (5)   The Chief shall make every effort to attend all fires and direct
the officers and members in the performance of their duties.
      (6)   The Chief shall see that the citizens are kept informed on fire
hazards in the community and on the activities of the Department.
      (7)   The Chief shall see that each fire is carefully investigated to
determine its cause and in the case of suspicion of incendiarism shall notify
proper authorities and secure and preserve all possible evidence for future use
in the case.
      (8)   The Chief shall file the appropriate fire loss reporting forms with
the State Fire Marshal in Oklahoma City each quarter of the calendar year in
those instances that include loss of life, personal injury or property damage
exceeding $15,000. The report shall include, but shall not be limited to,
notification of all fire related injuries and deaths, amount of property damage
and of firefighter injuries in the line of duty requiring the services of a
physician.
(Ord. 2021-01, passed 4-6-2021; Ord. 2022-005, passed 11-1-2022; Ord. 24-011,
passed 7-2-2024)
§ 1-310 ASSISTANT FIRE CHIEF.
   The assistant Fire Chief of the Fire Department shall be appointed by the
Fire Department. In the absence of the Chief, the assistant Fire Chief shall
command the Department and be held responsible therefore in all respects, with
the full powers and responsibilities of the Chief.
(Ord. 24-011, passed 7-2-2024)
§ 1-311 FIRE MARSHAL.
   (A)   There is hereby created the office of the Fire Marshal. The individual
holding the position of the Fire Chief and the Fire Marshal may be one and the
same. The Fire Marshal and all officer designated by the Fire Marshal, if any
shall be responsible for enforcing all ordinance requirements, for approving
equipment materials and installation relating to fire prevention and inspection
and correction of fire hazards and life safety regulations affecting or
relating to structures, processes and premises and safeguards from the hazard
of fire and explosion arising from the storage, handling or use of structures,
materials or devices; from conditions hazardous to life, property or public
welfare in the occupancy of structures or premises from fire hazards in the
structure or on the premises from occupancy or operation; and, matters related
to the construction, extension, repair, alteration or removal of fire
suppression and alarm systems.
   (B)   The Fire Marshal may, but shall not be required to, define fire
districts and boundaries thereof. For all fire districts so designated, if any,
or for the city as a whole, if no districts have been established the Fire
Marshal shall make an inspection of every building. It shall be the Fire
Marshal’s special duty to enforce a strict compliance with all the fire
provisions of the International Fire Code, as amended, published by
International Code Council, Inc., with certain amendments thereto and deletions
therefrom, and as may be further amended from time to time by resolution of
Council, and the same as so amended and changed is hereby adopted and
incorporated and considered as a part of this code.
(Ord. 24-011, passed 7-2-2024)
§ 1-312 FIRE DEPARTMENT; COMPANY OFFICERS.
   The officers of the Fire Department companies shall be selected upon their
ability to meet the following requirements:
   (A)   Their knowledge of firefighting;
   (B)   Their ability to lead people; and
   (C)   Their knowledge of firefighting equipment.
§ 1-313 FIRE DEPARTMENT; SECRETARY-TREASURER.
   One member elected by the Fire Department shall be Secretary-Treasurer. His
or her duties shall consist of the following:
   (A)   Calling the roll at the opening of each meeting;
   (B)   Keeping the minutes of each meeting; and
   (C)   Collecting any money due the Department by members.
§ 1-314 FIRE DEPARTMENT; NEW MEMBERS.
   All new members shall be on probation for one year after their appointment.
New volunteer members, upon completion of their probation period, must be
approved by the majority of the Fire Department.
§ 1-315 FIRE DEPARTMENT; BYLAWS.
   The bylaws of the Department shall include, but shall not be limited to, the
following.
   (A)   All volunteer firefighters are required to respond to alarms of fire
and other emergencies when notified.
   (B)   A volunteer firefighter is required to be present at all regular
meetings, call meetings and schools presented for the benefit of the
firefighters.
   (C)   There shall be at least one regular business meeting each month.
   (D)   Any volunteer firefighter having two unexcused absences in succession
or three unexcused absences in a period of three months will be expelled from
the Fire Department rolls.
   (E)   Volunteer firefighters leaving the municipality for an extended period
of time will be required to notify the Chief.
   (F)   Any volunteer firefighter refusing to attend training classes provided
for him or her will be expelled from the rolls.
   (G)   Any volunteer member of the Fire Department shall be expelled from the
rolls for the following offenses:
      (1)   Conduct unbecoming a firefighter;
      (2)   Any act of insubordination;
      (3)   Neglect of duty;
      (4)   Any violation of rules and regulations governing the Fire
Department; or
      (5)   Conviction of a felony.
   (H)   Volunteer members shall be paid $10 per fire per run.
   (I)   These bylaws hereby incorporate the provision of 11 O.S. §§ 49-103 et
seq. concerning volunteer Fire Departments.
§ 1-316 CITY PLANNING COMMISSION; CREATION, MEMBERSHIP.
   (A)   The City Planning Commission shall consist of not less than five
citizens, all of whom shall reside in the city.
   (B)   (1)   All members shall be nominated by the Mayor and confirmed by the
Council. The term of office shall be for three years; provided, however, that
in the first instance, one-third shall be for three years, one-third shall be
for two years and one-third shall be for one year.
      (2)   The members of said Planning Commission, having already been
nominated and confirmed, shall serve their abbreviated terms in accordance
herewith.
   (C)   The Mayor and City Engineer shall be ex officio members of the City
Planning Commission.
   (D)   The members of the City Planning Commission shall serve without
salary.
   (E)   Members may be removed by the City Council only for inefficiency,
neglect of duty or malefaction in office; vacancies occurring otherwise than
through the expiration of a term shall be filled only for the unexpired term by
the Mayor and confirmed by the Council.
   (F)   (1)   Within five days of the appointment and qualification of the
members of the City Planning Commission, the Commission shall meet and elect
one of its number as Chairperson, one as Vice Chairperson and one as secretary;
in addition, the Commission may create and fill such other offices as it may
deem necessary.
      (2)   The term of all such offices shall be one year, with eligibility
for reelection.
   (G)   The City Planning Commission shall have the power and duties as
prescribed for such a body by the statutes of the state.
§ 1-317 OFFICE OF STREET SUPERINTENDENT CREATED.
   (A)   The Street Superintendent shall be appointed at the beginning of each
fiscal year and shall serve until his or her successor shall be appointed and
qualified.
   (B)   The Street Superintendent shall be responsible for reporting to the
Council on all matters concerning the streets and alleys of the city or as the
Council may direct and at all times be under the supervision of the Council.
§ 1-318 CITY MANAGER.
   (A)   Appointment. The City Council is charged and empowered to appoint and
remove the City Manager as provided by law.
   (B)   Duties. The City Manager shall be the Chief Executive Officer and head
of the administrative branch of the city government. He or she shall execute
the laws and administer the government of the city and shall be responsible
therefor to the Council. He or she shall:
      (1)   Appoint and, when necessary for the good of the service, remove,
demote, lay off or suspend all heads of administrative departments and other
administrative officers and employees of the city except as otherwise provided
by law. The Manager or the Council, by ordinance, may authorize the head of a
department, office or agency to appoint and remove the subordinates in such
department, office or agency;
      (2)   Supervise and control all administrative departments, officers and
agencies;
      (3)   Prepare a budget annually and submit it to the Council and be
responsible for the administration of the budget after it goes into effect; and
recommend to the Council any changes in the budget which he or she deems
desirable;
      (4)   Submit to the Council a report after the end of the fiscal year on
the finances and administrative activities of the city for the preceding year;
      (5)   Keep the Council advised of the financial condition and future
needs of the city and make recommendations as he or she deems desirable; and
      (6)   Perform such other duties as may be prescribed by law or by
ordinance.
   (C)   Spending authority; emergency contracts.
      (1)   The City Manager and the General Manager of the City Public Works
Authority is hereby expressly authorized to enter into contracts and/or to make
purchases expending municipal funds as have been previously budgeted by the
City Council for purposes of the general running and management of the city
without prior approval of the City Council or the City Public Works Authority
without competitive bidding for contracts under $20,000.
      (2)   The amount herein designated may be change by the Council and LPWA
by resolution.
      (3)   Except as specified in division (C)(4) below, any expenditures,
whether by contracts or direct purchases, the City Manager and LPWA General
Manager seeks to make in excess of $20,000 must be submitted to the City
Council for approval by majority vote.
      (4)   (a)   If the City Manager in good faith determines that an
emergency exists such that inaction would be detrimental to the safety and
security of the city and its citizens, the City Manager shall be authorized
expend and/or enter into contracts for amounts not exceeding $100,000;
provided, however, that if the City Manager declares such an emergency, he or
she shall notify the City Council of such action within ten days.
         (b)   Such notification shall contain a statement of the reasons for
the action and the same shall thereafter be recorded in the official minutes of
the Council at the next regularly scheduled meeting.
(Ord. 24-010, passed 7-2-2024)
Statutory reference:
   Similar provisions, see 11 O.S. §§ 10-106(1) and 10-113
ARTICLE 4. NOMINATIONS AND ELECTIONS
§ 1-401 NOTICE OF MUNICIPAL ELECTIONS.
   (A)   Notice of a general municipal election or a special election shall be
given by publishing the resolution of the municipal governing body calling the
election. The resolution shall set forth:
      (1)   The date or dates of the election; and
      (2)   The offices to be filled or the questions to be voted upon at the
election.
   (B)   The resolution shall be published in a newspaper of general
circulation in the municipality at least ten days before the beginning of the
filing period for a general municipal election or at least ten days before the
date of a special election.
§ 1-402 GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTIONS, WHEN HELD.
   General municipal elections shall be held on the first Tuesday in April in
each odd-numbered year.
§ 1-403 CONDUCT OF GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTIONS.
   (A)   The laws applicable to general elections shall govern general
municipal elections, except as otherwise provided.
   (B)   Elected officials, including those from wards, as well as at large,
shall be elected at large by the registered votes of the entire city.
§ 1-404 WHAT CANDIDATE’S NAME MAY BE PLACED ON GENERAL ELECTION BALLOT.
   No candidate’s name shall be printed upon the official ballot for a general
municipal election unless such candidate shall have been nominated by some
political party at the primary election or unless his or her name is presented
as an independent candidate as provided in §
1-409 of this article.
§ 1-405 UNOPPOSED CANDIDATES IN GENERAL ELECTIONS.
   Any candidate who is unopposed for an office in a general municipal election
shall be deemed elected and certified; and his or her name shall not appear on
the general election ballot. If there is only one candidate for each of the
offices which are to be filled at the election, and no questions are to be
voted upon at the election, the general municipal election shall not be held.
§ 1-406 PRIMARY ELECTIONS, WHEN HELD.
   A primary election shall be held on the third Tuesday of March in each odd-
numbered year, at which time the several political parties shall nominate
candidates for offices which are to be elected at the upcoming general
municipal election.
§ 1-407 CONDUCT OF PRIMARY ELECTIONS.
   The general laws relating to primary elections shall govern municipal
primaries, except as otherwise provided. Party candidates for office, including
those from wards, as well as at large, shall be nominated at large by the
registered voters of the respective parties of the entire municipality.
§ 1-408 MANNER OF BECOMING PARTY CANDIDATE, DECLARATION OF CANDIDACY.
   Any registered voter who is an actual resident of the city or of the ward
where the office is from a ward, may become a candidate for a political party
nomination in the municipality’s primary election. To become a party candidate,
a declaration of candidacy must be filed with the County Election Council no
earlier than 8:00 a.m. on the first Monday in February, and no later than 5:00
p.m. on the next succeeding Wednesday.
§ 1-409 INDEPENDENT CANDIDATES.
   An independent candidate may have his or her name printed upon the general
municipal election ballot as candidate for any office to be filled at the
election. To become an independent candidate, a declaration of candidacy must
be filed with the County Election Council no earlier than 8:00 a.m. on the
first Monday in February, and no later than 5:00 p.m. on the next succeeding
Wednesday. An independent candidate must also be a registered voter and an
actual resident of the city or of the ward where the office is from a ward.
Filing as an independent candidate in an election or voting for such candidate
shall not affect one’s party affiliation or regularity.
§ 1-410 UNOPPOSED CANDIDATES IN PRIMARY ELECTION.
   Any candidate who is unopposed for an office in a primary election shall be
deemed nominated and so certified; and his or her name shall not appear on the
primary election ballot. If there are unopposed candidates for each of the
offices which are up for election, no primary election shall be held.
§ 1-411 SPECIAL ELECTIONS, QUESTIONS WHICH MAY BE SUBMITTED.
   When the Council shall deem it advisable, it may, by resolution or
ordinance, authorize the Mayor to call a special election for the purpose of
submitting to the registered voters of the city the question of issuing
municipal bonds, of granting any franchise or for any other purpose authorized
by law.
§ 1-412 SPECIAL ELECTION BALLOT PREPARATION AND ARRANGEMENT.
   The ballot for a special election shall be prepared by the secretary of the
County Election Council and shall set forth the proposition or propositions to
be voted upon, and if more than one proposition is submitted, they shall be
arranged so that each proposition may be voted upon separately.
§ 1-413 CONDUCT OF SPECIAL ELECTIONS HELD FOR ELECTING OFFICERS.
   (A)   When the office of a municipal elected official is to be filled at a
special election, the resolution or order of the Council calling the election
shall contain the following facts:
      (1)   A filing period of three days, on a Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday,
not less than ten days from the date of the resolution or order;
      (2)   The date of the special primary election, not less than 30 days
after the close of the filing period; and
      (3)   The date of the special general election, not less than 30 days
after the date of the primary election.
   (B)   A copy of the resolution or order shall be filed with the secretary of
the County Election Council. The election shall be conducted under the laws
applicable to general municipal elections.
§ 1-414 POLITICAL ACTIVITY OF OFFICERS AND EMPLOYEES.
   Municipal employees may attend and express their views at City Council
meetings or any other public meetings of the city. Any municipal employee may
actively participate in partisan and nonpartisan political activities;
provided, that the political activity in which the employee participates shall
be exercised only during off-duty hours and while not in uniform. Any federal
statutes restricting the political activities of certain municipal employees
shall supersede the provisions of this section as to such employees. No city
employee shall file as a candidate for public office while employed by the city
unless the Council, by majority vote, approves continued employment.
Statutory reference:
   Similar provisions, see 11 O.S. § 22.101.0
ARTICLE 5. MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS
§ 1-501 INITIATIVE AND REFERENDUM.
   The powers of the initiative and referendum are reserved to the people of
the city. In the exercise of these powers, the requirements of the State
Constitution and state law shall be observed.
Statutory reference:
   Similar provisions, see 11 O.S. §§ 15 et seq., 34 O.S. §§ 1 et seq. and
Article 18, §§ 4a through 4e of the State Constitution
§ 1-502 QUALIFICATIONS OF OFFICERS AND EMPLOYEES.
   Officers and employees of the city shall have the qualifications prescribed
by this code and such additional qualifications as the Council may prescribe by
ordinance; the Council shall not prescribe additional qualifications for
Council members.
Statutory reference:
   Similar provisions, see 11 O.S. § 8-101
§ 1-503 NEPOTISM; COMPATIBILITY OF OFFICES.
   (A)   No member of the City Council nor any other authority of the city
government may appoint or vote for the appointment of any person related to
himself or herself by affinity or consanguinity within the third degree, to any
office or position of profit in the city government. The provisions of this
section shall not prohibit an officer or employee already in the service of the
city from continuing in such service or from promotion therein.
   (B)   Except as may be otherwise provided by ordinance, the same person may
hold more than one office or position in the same city government; provided,
however, that a member of the Council shall not receive compensation for
service in any municipal office or position other than his or her elected
office.
Statutory reference:
   Similar provisions, see 11 O.S. § 8-106
§ 1-504 OFFICERS TO GIVE BONDS.
   The Clerk, Treasurer and Chief of Police of the city shall each give bonds,
payable to the city, within ten days after their election or appointment in the
following amounts:
   (A)   City Clerk: $1,000;
   (B)   City Treasurer: $15,000; and
   (C)   Chief of Police: $1,000.
§ 1-505 COMPENSATION.
   (A)   The salary of the Police Chief, police officers, firefighters,
electricians, sanitation workers, clerical workers, Street Department and all
other employees shall be as set by the City Manager.
   (B)   The salary for the Municipal Judge shall be $200 per month. The salary
for the Civil Defense Director shall be $50 per month.
§ 1-506 CHANGE OF SALARIES.
   (A)   The salary or compensation of elected officers shall not be changed
after their appointment or election, or during their term of office.
   (B)   The Council may, from time to time, determine or regulate the number
and class of officers and employees and determine or change their compensation
by motion or resolution, except as to elected officers as set forth in division
(A) above.
§ 1-507 OATH OF OFFICE.
   (A)   Every officer of the city, before entering upon the duties of his or
her office, shall take and subscribe to the following oaths.
 
   I,                        , do solemnly swear (or affirm) that I will support, obey and defend the
Constitution of the United States and the Constitution of the State of Oklahoma, and that I will not
knowingly receive, directly or indirectly, any money or other valuable thing, for the performance or
nonperformance of any act or duty pertaining to my office, other than the compensation allowed by
law. I further swear (or affirm) that I will faithfully discharge my duties as
                        of the City of Lexington and of the Lexington Public Works authority to the
best of my ability.
 
   I,                                          , do solemnly swear (or affirm) that I will support, obey and defend the
Constitution of the United States, and the Constitution of the State of Oklahoma, and will discharge the duties of my
office with fidelity; that I have not paid, or contributed, either directly or indirectly, any money or other valuable
thing to procure my nomination or election (or appointment), except for necessary and proper expenses expressly
authorized by law; that I have not, knowingly, violated any election law of the State, or procured it to be done by
others in my behalf; that I will not knowingly receive, directly or indirectly, any money or other valuable thing, for
the performance or nonperformance of any act or duty pertaining to my office, other than the compensation allowed by law,
and I further swear (or affirm) that I will not receive, use or travel upon any free pass or on free transportation
during my term of office.
 
   (B)   The oath shall be filed and kept in the City Clerk’s office. The
officer shall take and subscribe to the oaths required by state law and the
State Constitution.
Statutory reference:
   Similar provisions, see 11 O.S. § 8-103 and Article 15, § 1 of the State
Constitution
§ 1-508 WHO MAY ADMINISTER OATHS.
   All officers authorized by federal or state law, the Mayor, the City Clerk,
the City Treasurer, the heads of all other administrative departments, the
Municipal Judge, the City Attorney and other officers as the Council may
authorize, may administer oaths.
§ 1-509 CITY MANAGER MAY LAY OFF, SUSPEND, DEMOTE AND REMOVE.
   The City Manager shall have direct supervision of all employees, including
office personnel, and may lay off, suspend, demote or remove any officer or
employee.
§ 1-510 ACTING OFFICERS AND EMPLOYEES.
   The City Manager may appoint or elect the successor of an officer or
employee during the temporary absence, disability or suspension of such officer
or employee, or in case of vacancy, until a successor is appointed.
§ 1-511 PUBLICITY OF RECORDS.
   All records and accounts of every office, department or agent of the city
government shall be open to public inspection if authorized and allowed by the
State Open Records Act.
Statutory reference:
   Similar provisions, see 51 O.S. §§ 24A.1 et seq.
§ 1-512 FILING OF MINUTES.
   It shall be the duty of the City Clerk to prepare and file at the City Hall
the tentative minutes of every regular and/or special meeting of the City
Council or the utilities authority. Such minutes shall be prepared and filed
within five days after such regular and/or special meeting.
§ 1-513 LOCATION OF RECORDS.
   All records of the city and the City Public Works Authority shall be
prepared, kept and maintained at the City Hall located at 121 East Broadway,
Lexington, Oklahoma, except that police, fire and ambulance records may be kept
and maintained at the office of the Police Department at 330 N. Main,
Lexington, Oklahoma. No person may remove any records from said offices, except
that rules for the removal of records may be promulgated by the City Council.
§ 1-514 STARTING SALARY FOR POLICE OFFICERS.
   The starting salary for certified police officers shall be as set by the
City Manager.
§ 1-515 HOLDING OF DUAL OFFICES.
   (A)   Any person holding an office or position, either as an employee or as
the head or assistant head of a department, of the municipality of the city
shall be prohibited from also holding elected office in the governing body of
the city at any point during the same period of time.
   (B)   This prohibition shall not apply to the following:
      (1)   Persons who are no longer employed by the city but receiving
government pensions or retirement due to previous employment, and persons who
are employees or hold offices outside of the city, whether other municipal,
county, state or federal;
      (2)   Any part-time employee of the city or volunteer of any city
department or agency, including, but not limited to, the City Volunteer Fire
Department, provided nothing in this article shall permit compensation in
violation of 11 O.S. § 8-106; and
      (3)   Any individual who, as of the date this article is passed, is
currently employed or holding any position prohibited by this article within
the city and also serving as an elected official, provided such exemption shall
only apply for the duration of such individual’s current elected term.
(Ord. 2022-06, passed 11-1-2022; Ord. 2023-001, passed 2-7-2023)
ARTICLE 6. SUCCESSION IN GOVERNMENT
§ 1-601 NEW CODE TO GO INTO EFFECT WHEN APPROVED BY COUNCIL.
   This code of ordinances shall go into effect 30 days from the date of
approval by the City Council unless an emergency is declared.
§ 1-602 ORDINANCES CONTINUED.
   All ordinances, insofar as they are not inconsistent with this code, shall
continue in effect until they are repealed or until they expire by their own
limitation.
§ 1-603 OFFICERS AND EMPLOYEES CONTINUED.
   All officers and employees of the city under all previous ordinances shall
continue in the offices and employments which they respectively hold after this
code goes into effect, until their services may be terminated in accordance
with the provisions of this code.
§ 1-604 BOOKS AND PROPERTY TO BE DELIVERED TO SUCCESSOR.
   All books, vouchers, monies or other property belonging to the city and in
charge or possession of any officer of the city shall be delivered to his or
her successor when qualified.
