ARTICLE 1. FEDERAL, STATE AND LOCAL LAW
§ 3-101 FEDERAL AND STATE LAW AND CONSTITUTIONS.
   (A)   Whereas, the state acts as the agent of the federal government when
acting in matters relating to the enforcement of federal law, regardless of
geographic boundaries of local government jurisdiction within the state; and
   (B)   Whereas, the city acts as the agent of the state in matters relating
to the enforcement of state law within the geographic boundaries of the city;
   (C)   Now, therefore, the City Council hereby acknowledges and incorporates
the State Civil and Penal Codes into the code of the city and hereby adopts,
ratifies and confirms the same as if set out in full herein.
§ 3-102 RELATIONSHIP OF STATE, FEDERAL AND LOCAL CODES DEFINED.
   All officers and employees of the city shall be required to swear or affirm
that the laws and Constitutions of the state and the United States will be
carried out and upheld to the best of their ability as well as the ordinances
and regulations of the city.
§ 3-103 ENUMERATION OF PROVISIONS.
   (A)   Provisions of the state law which affect the city because of its
general relationship to the state will not be enumerated herein but are
declared to be an inseparable part of this code.
   (B)   Provisions of the state law which prescribe specific actions or laws
for the city and its citizens may be included in this code for purposes of
clarity. Provisions of state law in matters of wider public concern which are
not enumerated herein but which affect the city and its citizens in a general
way may not be enumerated herein, but are nevertheless hereby made a part of
this code.
   (C)   (1)   All provisions of the city code shall be specifically enumerated
herein which are of purely local concern. Only the regulations, rules,
prohibitions, nuisances, offenses and other provisions which are of purely
local concern to the city as provided by state law and are specifically
enumerated herein in detail shall be enforced by the city.
      (2)   The city and its duly authorized officers and agents shall have all
power, duties and responsibilities necessary to enforce the same.
§ 3-104 HOW CODE DESIGNATED AND CITED.
   The ordinances embraced in this and all other chapters and sections shall
constitute and be designated the “Code of Ordinances, City of Lexington,
Oklahoma” and may be so cited. Such code may also be cited as the “Lexington
City Code or City Code of Lexington.”
§ 3-105 CATCHLINES OF SECTIONS.
   The catchlines of the several sections of this code are intended as mere
catchwords to indicate the contents of the section and shall not be deemed or
taken to be titles of such sections, nor as any part of the section, unless
expressly so provided.
ARTICLE 2. RULES OF CONSTRUCTION
§ 3-201 RULES OF CONSTRUCTION; DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   CITY, THE CITY or MUNICIPALITY. The City of Lexington, Cleveland County,
Oklahoma.
   CITY ATTORNEY or CORPORATION COUNSEL. The City Attorney for the City of
Lexington, Oklahoma.
   CITY COUNCIL. The City Council of the City of Lexington, Oklahoma.
   CITY TREASURER. The City Treasurer of the City of Lexington, Oklahoma.
   CLERK, CLERK OF THE MUNICIPALITY or CITY CLERK. The Clerk of the City of
Lexington, Oklahoma.
   CODE. The code of ordinances of the City of Lexington, Oklahoma.
   COMPUTATION OF TIME. Whenever a notice is required to be given or an act to
be done a certain length of time before any proceeding shall be had, the day on
which such notice is given or such act is done shall be excluded in computing
the time, but the day on which such proceeding is to be had shall be included.
   COUNTY. Cleveland County, Oklahoma.
   GENDER. A word imparting the masculine gender only shall extend and be
applied to females and to firms, partnerships and corporations as well as to
males.
   HEALTH OFFICER or HEALTH DEPARTMENT. The County Sanitarian or County Health
Department unless specific reference is made to the appointed Health Officer of
the city or state.
   HIGHWAY. Any street, alley, highway, avenue or public place or square,
bridge, viaduct, tunnel, underpass, overpass or causeway in the city dedicated
or devoted to public use.
   JOINT AUTHORITY. Words purporting to give authority to three or more
officers or other persons shall be construed as giving such authority to a
majority of such officers or other persons, unless it is otherwise declared.
   MAY. The act referred to is permissive.
   MONTH. A calendar month.
   NUMBER. Any word imparting the single number shall include the plural and
any word imparting the plural number shall include the singular, except where a
contrary intention plainly appears.
   OATH. Includes an affirmation in all cases in which, by law, an affirmation
may be substituted for an oath, and in such cases, the words SWEAR and SWORN
shall be equivalent to the words AFFIRM and AFFIRMED.
   OFFICERS, DEPARTMENTS AND THE LIKE. Whenever any officer, department, board,
commission or other agency is referred to by title alone, such reference shall
be construed as if followed by the words “of the City of Lexington, Oklahoma.”
   OR; AND. OR may be read AND, and AND may be read OR, if the sense requires
it.
   OWNER. Applied to a building or land, shall include any part owner, joint
owner, tenant in common, tenant in partnership, joint tenant or tenant by the
entirety of the whole or of a part of such building or land.
   PERSON. The word PERSON shall extend and be applied to associations,
corporations, firms, partnerships and bodies politic and corporate, as well as
to individuals. Whenever used with respect to any penalty, the word PERSON, as
applied to partnerships or associations, shall mean the partners or members
thereof; and as applied to corporations, the officers thereof.
   POLICE CHIEF or CHIEF OF POLICE. The City Marshal of the City of Lexington,
Oklahoma.
   POLICE OFFICER. The City Marshal or any deputy marshal or police officer of
the City of Lexington, Oklahoma.
   PRECEDING, FOLLOWING. Next before and next after, respectively.
   PRESIDENT OF THE CITY COUNCIL, CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER or MAYOR. The
President of the City Council of the City of Lexington, Oklahoma.
   ROADWAY. The portion of a street improved, designed or ordinarily used for
vehicular traffic.
   SHALL. The act referred to is mandatory.
   SIDEWALK. Any portion of the street between the curb, or the lateral line of
the roadway and the adjacent property line, intended for the use of
pedestrians.
   SIGNATURE or SUBSCRIPTION. Shall include a mark when a person cannot write.
   STATE. The State of Oklahoma.
   STATUTORY REFERENCES. Reference to the statutes of the State of Oklahoma
means the statutes as they now are or as they may be amended to be; a reference
to a particular year of statutes also means any amendments and the comparable
provision when included in future codifications or supplementation of the
statutes.
   STREET. Includes any highway, alley, street, avenue or public place, square,
bridge, viaduct, underpass, overpass, tunnel or causeway in the city, dedicated
or devoted to the public use.
   TENSE. Words used in the past or present tense include the future as well as
the past and present.
   WRITTEN or IN WRITING. Includes any representation of words, letters or
figures, whether by printing or otherwise.
   YEAR. Unless otherwise designated, a calendar year.
§ 3-202 AMENDMENTS OR ADDITIONS TO CODE.
   (A)   All ordinances passed subsequent to this code which amend, repeal or
in any way affect this code may be numbered in accordance with the numbering
system of this code and printed for inclusion therein. When subsequent
ordinances repeal any chapter, section or division, or any portion thereof,
such repealed portions may be excluded from this code by omission thereof from
reprinted pages. Such inclusion of ordinances passed subsequent to this code
which amend or add to this code (except in the case of repeal) shall be prima
facie evidence of such subsequent ordinances until such time that this code and
subsequent ordinances numbered or omitted are readopted as a new code by the
City Council.
   (B)   Amendments to any of the provisions of this code shall be made by
amending such provisions by specific reference to the section number of this
code in the following language: “That section of the code of ordinances, City
of Lexington, Oklahoma, is hereby amended to read as follows.” The new
provisions shall then be set out in full as desired.
   (C)   In the event a new section not heretofore existing in the code is to
be added, the following language or any language substantially similar of
conveying the same meaning shall be used: “That the Code of Ordinances, City of
Lexington, Oklahoma, is hereby amended by adding a section, to be numbered
which said section reads as follows:                              .” The new
section shall then be set out in full as desired.
   ARTICLE 3. MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS
§ 3-301 CERTAIN ORDINANCES NOT AFFECTED BY CODE.
   (A)   Nothing in this code or the ordinance adopting this code shall be
construed to repeal or otherwise affect the validity of any of the following:
      (1)   Any ordinance promising or guaranteeing the payment of money for
the city, or authorizing the issuance of any bonds of the city, or any evidence
of the city’s indebtedness;
      (2)   Any appropriation ordinance or ordinance providing for the levy of
taxes, for an annual budget or prescribing salaries for city officers and
employees;
      (3)   Any ordinance annexing territory to the city or excluding territory
as a part of the city or zoning any property;
      (4)   Any ordinance approving, authorizing or otherwise relating to any
contract, agreement, lease, deed or other instrument or granting any franchise;
      (5)   Any ordinance authorizing or otherwise relating to any special
public improvement; and/or
      (6)   Any temporary or special ordinance.
   (B)   All such ordinances are hereby recognized as continuing in full force
and effect to the same extent as if set out at length herein.
§ 3-302 CODE DOES NOT AFFECT PRIOR OFFENSES, RIGHTS.
   Nothing in this code or the ordinance adopting this code shall affect any
offense or act committed or done, or any penalty or forfeiture incurred, or any
contract or right established or accruing, before the effective date of this
code.
§ 3-303 CODE AND ORDINANCES EFFECTIVE OUTSIDE CITY ON PROPERTY OWNED OR
CONTROLLED BY CITY.
   All provisions of this code and other ordinances of the city now in effect
or adopted in the future are hereby extended to all real property belonging to,
or under the control of, the city, outside the corporate limits of the city,
and shall be in full force and effect thereon, insofar as they are applicable.
Any words in any such provision indicating that its effect is limited to the
corporate limits of the city shall be deemed to mean and include also such
outlying real property belonging to, or under the control of, the city, unless
the context clearly indicates otherwise.
§ 3-304 SEPARABILITY OF PARTS OF CODE.
   It is hereby declared to be the intention of the City Council that the
sections, paragraphs, sentences, clauses and phrases of this code are
separable, and if any phrase, clause, sentence, paragraph or section of this
code shall be declared invalid by the judgment or decree of any court of
competent jurisdiction, such invalidity shall not affect any of the remaining
phrases, clauses, sentences, paragraphs and sections of this code, since the
same would have been enacted by the City Council without the incorporation in
this code of any such invalid phrase, clause, sentence, paragraph or section.
§ 3-305 SALVAGE YARDS.
   It shall be unlawful and an offense for any person or corporation to own,
operate or maintain within the corporate limits of the city, a salvage yard for
the salvaging, wrecking or dismantling of vehicles, including, but not limited
to, automobiles, trucks, trailers of any kind or lawn mowers without a license
therefor. It shall further be unlawful and an offense to keep or place any of
the above said vehicles on any unlicensed lot or parcel within the corporate
limits of the city, when such are not in a usable condition. Each day such
violation occurs shall be deemed a separate offense and punishable under the
appropriate provisions of this code.
§ 3-306 CHARGE FOR RETURNED CHECKS.
   There shall be a $10 charge assessed to the maker thereof for all checks
returned to the city for insufficient funds, closed account or any other
reason.
§ 3-307 PURCHASING AGENT.
   (A)   The City Council, by motion, shall appoint a purchasing agent for the
city. The City Council shall also appoint any alternate purchasing agents
deemed necessary in its discretion. The purchasing agent shall have such
authority and shall follow such procedures as may be authorized by state law.
   (B)   All purchases shall be made in compliance with state law concerning
purchase orders.
   (C)   Unless otherwise specified, the City Manager shall serve as the
purchasing agent.
Statutory reference:
   Similar provisions, see 62 O.S. §§ 310.1 et seq.
§ 3-308 9-1-1 VoIP SERVICE FEE.
   (A)   A 9-1-1 service fee is hereby adopted and imposed by the City Council
upon interconnected voiceover internet protocol telephone service customers
whose businesses or residences are located within the city limits, at the rate
of $0.50 per month for each VoIP service user, pursuant to 63 O.S. §§ 2855 et
seq.
   (B)   In addition, all VoIP carriers having customers within the city shall
provide an annual census of customers to the city no later than 60 days after
the first day of each calendar year.
(Ord. 2006-05, passed 12-5-2006)
§ 3-309 FAIR HOUSING.
   (A)   Policy. It is the policy of the city to provide, within constitutional
limitations, for fair housing throughout the city.
   (B)   Definitions. For the purpose of this section, the following
definitions shall apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a
different meaning.
      DISCRIMINATORY HOUSING PRACTICES. An act that is unlawful under divisions
(D), (E) and (F) below.
      DWELLING. Any building, structure or portion thereof which is occupied as
or designed or intended for occupation as a residence by one or more families
and any vacant land which is offered for sale or lease for the construction or
location thereon of any such building, structure or portion thereof.
      FAMILY. Includes a single individual.
      PERSON. Includes one or more individuals, corporations, partnerships,
associations, labor organizations, legal representatives, mutual companies,
joint-stock companies, trusts, unincorporated organizations, trustees in
bankruptcy, receivers and fiduciaries.
      TO RENT. Includes to lease, to sublease, to let or otherwise to grant for
a consideration the right to occupy premises owned by the occupant.
   (C)   Unlawful practices.
      (1)   Subject to the provisions of divisions (C)(2) and (G) below, the
prohibitions against discrimination in the sale or rental of housing set forth
in this division (C) shall apply to all dwellings, except as exempted by
division (C)(2) below.
      (2)   Nothing in this section shall apply to:
         (a)   Any single-family house sold or rented by an owner; provided,
that such private individual owner does not own more than three such single-
family houses at any one time; provided further that, in the case of the sale
of any such single-family house by a private individual owner not residing in
such house at the time of such sale or who was not the most recent resident of
such house prior to such sale, the exemption granted by this division (C)(2)
shall apply only with respect to one such sale within any 24-month period;
provided, further, that such bona fide private individual owner does not own
any interest in, nor is there owned or reserved on his or her behalf, under any
express or voluntary agreement, title to or any right to all or a portion of
the proceeds from the sale or rental of any such single-family house shall be
excepted from the application of this title only if such house is sold or
rented:
            1.   Without the use in any manner of the sales or rental
facilities or the sales or rental services of any real estate broker, agent or
salesperson or of such facilities or services of any person in the business of
selling or renting dwellings or of any employee or agent of any such facilities
or services of any person in the business of selling or renting dwellings or of
any employee or agent of any such broker, agent, salesperson or person; and
            2.   Without the publication, posting or mailing, after notice, of
any advertisement or written notice in violation of division (D)(3) below.
However, nothing in this division (C)(2)(a) shall prohibit the use of
attorneys, escrow agents, abstractors, title companies and other such
professional assistance as is necessary to perfect or transfer the title.
         (b)   Rooms or units in dwellings containing living quarters occupied
or intended to be occupied by no more than four families living independently
of each other, if the owner maintains and occupies one such living quarters as
his or her residence.
      (3)   For the purpose of division (C)(2) above, a person shall be deemed
to be in the business of selling or renting dwellings if:
         (a)   He or she has, within the preceding 12 months, participated as
principal in three or more transactions involving the sale or rental of any
dwelling or any interest therein;
         (b)   He or she has, within the preceding 12 months, participated as
an agent, other than in the sale of his or her own personal residence, in
providing sales or rental facilities or sales or rental services in two or more
transactions involving the sale or rental of any dwelling or any interest
therein; and
         (c)   He or she is the owner of any dwelling designed or intended for
occupancy by, or occupied by, five or more families.
   (D)   Discrimination in the sale or rental of housing. As made applicable by
this section and except as exempted by divisions (C)(2) and (G) of this
section, it shall be unlawful:
      (1)   To refuse to sell or rent after the making of a bona fide offer or
to refuse to negotiate for the sale or rental of or otherwise make unavailable
or deny a dwelling to any person because of race, sex, color, religion,
national origin, disability, familial status, sexual orientation, gender
identity or any other characteristic protected by federal law;
      (2)   To discriminate against any person in the terms, conditions or
privileges of sale or rental of a dwelling on in the provision of services or
facilities in connection therewith because of race, sex, color, religion,
national origin, disability, familial status, sexual orientation, gender
identity or any other characteristic protected by federal law;
      (3)   To make, print or publish or cause to be made, printed or published
notice, statement or advertisement with respect to the sale or rental of a
dwelling that indicates any preference, limitation or discrimination based on
race, sex, color, religion, national origin, disability, familial status,
sexual orientation, gender identity or any other characteristic protected by
federal law, or an intention to make any such preference, limitation or
discrimination;
      (4)   To represent to any person because of race, sex, color, religion,
national origin, disability or familial status, sexual orientation, gender
identity or any other characteristic protected by federal law, that any
dwelling is not available for inspection, sale or rental when such dwelling is,
in fact, so available; and
      (5)   To induce or attempt to induce any person to sell or rent any
dwelling, for profit, by representations regarding the entry or prospective
entry into the neighborhood of a person or persons of a particular race, sex,
color, religion, national origin, disability, familial status, sexual
orientation, gender identity or any other characteristic protected by federal
law.
   (E)   Discrimination in financing or housing. It shall be unlawful for any
bank, building and loan association, insurance company or other corporation,
association, firm or enterprise whose business consists in whole or in part in
the making of commercial real estate loans to deny a loan or other financial
assistance to a person applying therefor for the purpose of purchasing,
constructing, improving, repairing or maintaining a dwelling or to discriminate
against him or her in the fixing of the amount, interest rate, duration or
other terms or conditions of such loan or other financial assistance because of
race, sex, color, religion, national origin, disability, familial status,
sexual orientation, gender identity or any other characteristic protected by
federal law, of such person or of any person associated with him or her in
connection with such loan or other financial assistance or the purposes of such
loan or other financial assistance or of the present or prospective owners,
lessees, tenants or occupants of the dwelling or dwellings in relation to which
such loan or other financial assistance is to be made or given, provided that
nothing contained in this section shall impair the scope or effectiveness of
the exception contained in division (C)(2) above.
   (F)   Discrimination in the provision of brokerage services. It shall be
unlawful to deny any person access to or membership or participation in any
multiple-listing service, rental or facility relating to the business of
selling or renting dwellings or to discriminate against him or her in the terms
or conditions of such access, membership or participation on account of race,
sex, color, religion, national origin, disability, familial status, sexual
orientation, gender identity or any other characteristic protected by federal
law.
   (G)   Exemption. Nothing in this policy shall prohibit a religious
organization, association or society or any nonprofit institution or
organization operated, supervised or controlled by or in conjunction with a
religious organization, association or society from limiting the sale, rental
or occupancy of dwellings which it owns or operates for other than a commercial
purpose to persons of the same religion or from giving preference to such
persons, unless membership in such religion is restricted on account of race,
sex, color, national origin, disability, familial status, sexual orientation,
gender identity or any other characteristic protected by federal law. Nor shall
anything in this policy prohibit a private club, not, in fact, open to the
public which, as an incident to its primary purpose or purposes, provides
lodgings which it owns or operates for other than a commercial purpose, from
limiting the rental or occupancy of such lodgings to its members or from giving
preference to its members.
   (H)   Administration.
      (1)   The authority and responsibility for administering this policy
shall be in the Chief Executive Officer of the city.
      (2)   The Chief Executive Officer may delegate any of these functions
duties and powers to employees of the city or to boards of such employees,
including functions, duties and powers, with respect to investigating,
conciliating, hearing, determining, ordering, certifying, reporting or
otherwise acting as to any work, business or matter under this policy. The
Chief Executive Officer shall, by rule, prescribe such rights of appeal from
the decisions of his or her hearing examiners to other hearing examiners or to
other officers in the city, to boards of officers or to himself or herself, as
shall be appropriate and in accordance with law.
      (3)   All executive departments and agencies shall administer their
programs and activities relating to housing and urban development in a manner
to affirmatively further the purposes of the policy and shall cooperate with
the Chief Executive Officer to further such purposes.
   (I)   Education and conciliation. Immediately after the enactment of this
policy, the Chief Executive Officer shall commence such educational and
conciliatory activities as will further the purposes of this policy. He or she
shall call conferences of persons in the housing industry and other interested
parties to acquaint them with the provisions of this policy and his or her
suggested means of implementing it and shall endeavor, with their advice, to
work out programs of voluntary compliance and of enforcement.
   (J)   Enforcement.
      (1)   Any person who claims to have been injured by a discriminatory
housing practice or who believes that he or she will be irrevocably injured by
a discriminatory housing practice that is about to occur (hereafter “person
aggrieved”) may file a complaint with the Chief Executive Officer. Complaints
shall be in writing and shall contain such information and be in such form as
the Chief Executive Officer requires. Upon receipt of such a complaint, the
Chief Executive Officer shall furnish a copy of the same to the person or
persons who allegedly committed or are about to commit the alleged
discriminatory housing practice. Within 30 days after receiving a complaint or
within 30 days after the expiration of any period of reference under division
(J)(3) below, the Chief Executive Officer shall investigate the complaint and
give notice in writing to the person aggrieved whether he or she intends to
resolve it. If the Chief Executive Officer decides to try to eliminate or
correct the alleged discriminatory housing practice by informal methods of
conference, conciliation and persuasion, nothing said or done in the course of
such informal endeavors may be made public or used as evidence in a subsequent
proceeding under this policy without the written consent of the persons
concerned. Any employee of the Chief Executive Officer who shall make public
any information in violation of this provision shall, upon conviction, be fined
not more that $100 or imprisoned not more than ten days.
      (2)   A complaint under division (J)(1) above shall be filed within 180
days after the alleged discriminatory housing practice occurred. Complaints
shall be in writing and shall state the facts upon which the allegations of a
discriminatory housing practice are based. Complaints may be reasonably and
fairly amended at any time. A respondent may file an answer to the complaint
against him or her and, with the leave of the Chief Executive Officer, which
shall be granted whenever it would be reasonable and fair to do so, may amend
his or her answer at any time. Both complaints and answers shall be verified.
      (3)   If, within 30 days after a complaint is filed with the Chief
Executive Officer, the Chief Executive Officer has been unable to obtain
voluntary compliance with this policy, the person aggrieved may, within 30 days
thereafter, file a complaint with the Secretary of the Department of Housing
and Urban Development. The Chief Executive Officer will assist in this filing.
      (4)   If the Chief Executive Officer has been unable to obtain voluntary
compliance within 30 days of the complaint, the person aggrieved may, within 30
days thereafter, commence a civil action in any appropriate court against the
respondent named in the complaint to enforce the rights granted or protected by
this policy insofar as such rights relate to the subject of the complaint. If
the court finds that a discriminatory housing practice has occurred or is about
to occur, the court may enjoin the respondent from engaging in such practice or
order such affirmative action as may be appropriate.
      (5)   In any proceedings brought pursuant to this section, the burden of
proof shall be on the complainant.
      (6)   Whenever an action by an individual shall come to trial, the Chief
Executive Officer shall immediately terminate all efforts to obtain voluntary
compliance.
   (K)   Investigations, subpoenas, giving of evidence.
      (1)   In conducting an investigation, the Chief Executive Officer shall
have access at all reasonable times to premises, records, documents,
individuals and other evidence or possible sources of evidence and may examine,
record and copy such materials and take and record the testimony or statement
of such persons as are reasonably necessary for the furtherance of the
investigation; provided, however, that the Chief Executive Officer first
complies with the provisions of the Fourth Amendment relating to unreasonable
searches and seizures. The Chief Executive Officer may issue subpoenas to
compel his or her access to or the production of such materials or the
appearance of such persons and may issue interrogatories to a respondent to the
same extent and subject to the same limitations as would apply if the subpoenas
or interrogatories were issued or served in aid of a civil action in the United
States District Court for the district in which the investigation is taking
place. The Chief Executive Officer may administer oaths.
      (2)   Upon written application to the Chief Executive Officer, a
respondent shall be entitled to the issuance of a reasonable number of
subpoenas by and in the name of the Chief Executive Officer to the same extent
and subject to the same limitations as subpoenas issued by the Chief Executive
Officer himself or herself. Subpoenas issued at the request of a respondent
shall show on their face the name and address of such respondent and shall
state that they were issued at his or her request.
      (3)   Witnesses summoned by subpoenas of the Chief Executive Officer
shall be entitled to the same witness and mileage fees as are witnesses in
proceedings in United States District Courts. Fee payable to a witness summoned
by a subpoena issued at the request of a respondent shall be paid by him or
her. Within five days after service of a subpoena upon any person, such person
may petition the Chief Executive Officer to revoke or modify the subpoena. The
Chief Executive Officer shall grant the petition if he or she finds that the
subpoena requires appearance or attendance at an unreasonable time or place,
that it requires production of evidence which does not relate to any matter
under investigation, that it does not describe with sufficient particularity
the evidence to be produced, that compliance would be unduly onerous or for
other good reason.
      (4)   In case of contumacy or refusal to obey a subpoena, the Chief
Executive Officer or other person at whose request it was issued may petition
for its enforcement in the municipal or state court for the district in which
the person to who the subpoena was addressed resides, was served or transacts
business.
      (5)   Any person who willfully fails or neglects to attend and testify or
to answer any lawful inquiry or to produce records, documents or other
evidence, if in his or her power to do so, in obedience to the subpoena or
lawful order of the Chief Executive Officer shall be fined not more than $100
or imprisoned not more than ten days, or both. Any person who, with intent to
mislead the Chief Executive Officer, shall make or cause to be made any false
entry or statement of fact in any report, account, record or other document
submitted to the Chief Executive Officer pursuant to his or her subpoena or
other order or shall willfully neglect or fail to make or cause to be made
full, true and correct entries in such reports, accounts, records or other
documents or shall willfully mutilate, alter or by any other means falsify any
documentary evidence shall be fined not more than $100 or imprisoned not more
than ten days, or both.
      (6)   The City Attorney shall conduct all litigation in which the Chief
Executive Officer participates as a party or as amicus pursuant to this
section.
   (L)   Enforcement by private persons.
      (1)   The rights granted herein by divisions (C), (D), (E) and (F) above
may be enforced by civil actions in state or local courts of general
jurisdiction. A civil action shall be commenced within 180 days after the
alleged discriminatory housing practice occurred; provided, however, that the
court shall continue such civil case brought pursuant to this section or
division (J)(4) above from time to time before bringing it to trial if the
court believes that the conciliation efforts of the Chief Executive Officer are
likely to result in satisfactory settlement of the discriminatory housing
practice complained of in the complaint made to the Chief Executive Officer and
which practice forms the basis for the action in court; and provided, however,
that any sale, encumbrance or rental consummated prior to the issuance of any
court order issued under the authority of this policy and involving a bona fide
purchaser, encumbrancer or tenant, without actual notice of the existence of
the filing of a complaint or civil action under the provisions of this policy,
shall not be affected.
      (2)   The court may grant as relief, as it deems appropriate, any
permanent or temporary injunction, temporary restraining order or other order
and may award to the plaintiff actual damages and not more than $1,000 punitive
damages, together with court costs and reasonable attorneys’ fees in the case
of a prevailing plaintiff, provided that said plaintiff, in the opinion of the
court, is not financially able to assume said attorneys’ fees.
   (M)   Interference, coercion or intimidation. It shall be unlawful to
coerce, intimidate, threaten or interfere with any person in the exercise or
enjoyment of or on account of his or her having exercised or enjoyed or on
account of his or her having aided or encouraged any other person in the
exercise or enjoyment of any right granted or protected by divisions (C), (D),
(E) or (K) above. This section may be enforced by appropriate civil action.
   (N)   Separability of provisions. If any provision of this policy or the
application thereof to any person or circumstance is held invalid, the
remainder of the policy and the application of the provision to other persons
not similarly situated or to other circumstances shall not be affected thereby.
   (O)   Prevention of intimidation in fair housing cases. Whoever, whether or
not acting under color of law, by force or threat of force, willfully injures,
intimidates or interferes with or attempts to injure, intimidate or interfere
with:
      (1)   Any person because of his or her race, sex, color, religion,
national origin, disability, familial status, sexual orientation, gender
identity or any other characteristic protected by federal law, and because he
or she is or has been selling, purchasing, renting, financing, occupying or
contracting or negotiating for the sale, purchase, rental, financing or
occupation of any dwelling or applying for or participating in any service,
organization or facility relating to the business of selling or renting
dwellings;
      (2)   Any person because he or she is or has been or in order to
intimidate such person or any other person or class of persons from:
         (a)   Participating without discrimination on account of race, sex,
color, religion, national origin, disability, familial status, sexual
orientation, gender identity or any other characteristic protected by federal
law, in any of the activities, services, organizations or facilities described
in division (O)(1) above; or
         (b)   Affording another person or class of persons opportunity or
protection so to participate.
      (3)   Any citizen because he or she is or has been or in order to
discourage such citizen or any other citizen from lawfully aiding or
encouraging other persons to participate, without discrimination on account of
race, sex, color, religion, national origin, disability, familial status,
sexual orientation, gender identity or any other characteristic protected by
federal law, in any of the activities, services, organizations or facilities
described in division (O)(1) above or from participating lawfully in speech or
peaceful assembly opposing any denial of the opportunity to so participate
shall be fined not more than $100 or imprisoned not more than ten days, or
both; and if bodily injury results, shall be fined not more than $100 or
imprisoned not more than ten days, or both; and if death results, shall be
subject to imprisonment for any term of years or for life.
(Ord. 19-03, passed 11-5-2019)
ARTICLE 4. ADDITIONAL DUTIES OF COUNCIL MEMBERS
§ 3-401 DUTIES.
   In addition to the other duties of the city, the City Council members shall
have the following objectives and duties.
§ 3-402 OBJECTIVES.
   (A)   To aid, assist and advise the city by investigation, suggestion and
planning concerning matters of paving, street maintenance, permits, building
and moving permits, operation of vehicles on streets, curbing, city
improvements, highways, rights-of-way, disposal plants, waterworks and any
other form of city improvements or convenience.
   (B)   All requests for building or moving permits, adding to any structures
or altering any structures, shall be submitted to the Council members with a
written application or request for approval, and the same shall be considered
in accordance with the restrictions in the dedication and plat and such city
ordinances as may be in existence or may be later passed, with a permit fee.
The permit fee shall be as determined by the City Council by motion and/or
resolution. The request shall be approved or disapproved by the City Council
members.
   (C)   Said Council members shall have the right and duty to make
recommendations if they so desire concerning any of the above-mentioned matters
for consideration.
§ 3-403 COUNCIL MEMBERS NOT OBLIGATED.
   The City Council members shall not be obligated in any way to enact or pass
or approve any recommendations made to the Council members, but only after
consideration of such as they deem necessary to the best interest of the city.
ARTICLE 5. PENALTY
§ 3-501 GENERAL PENALTY FOR VIOLATIONS OF CODE AND ORDINANCES; CONTINUING
VIOLATIONS.
   Whenever in this code or in any ordinance of the city, an act is prohibited
or is made or declared to be unlawful or an offense or misdemeanor, or whenever
in such code or ordinance, the doing of any act is required or the failure to
do any act is declared to be unlawful, and no specific penalty is provided
therefor, the violation of any such provision of this code or any such
ordinance shall be punishable by a fine in an amount not exceeding $100 and
payment of any costs. Each day on which any violation of this code or of any
ordinance shall continue shall constitute a separate offense and shall be
punishable as such.

ARTICLE 1. STATE ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGE CONTROL ACT
§ 4-101 STATE ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGE CONTROL ACT ADOPTED.
   The State Alcoholic Beverage Control Act, being 37A O.S. §§ 1-101 through 1-
168, is hereby adopted and incorporated in this code of ordinances, and all
provisions of the Act are hereby declared to be in force as if they were
written herein in complete detail.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012)
Statutory reference:
   Similar provisions, see 37A O.S. § 1-101
§ 4-102 DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.
   For the purpose of this article, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning. All
words, phrases and terms used in this chapter and not defined herein shall be
interpreted and construed in conformity with the definitions of the same set
forth in the State Alcoholic Beverage Control Act, being 37A O.S. §§ 1-101
through 1-168, with the same force and effect as if set forth in full herein,
and such definitions are made a part hereof by reference.
   ALCOHOL. Hydrated oxide of ethyl, ethyl alcohol, ethanol or spirits of wine
from whatever source or by whatever process produced. It does not include wood
alcohol or alcohol which has been denatured or produced as denatured in
accordance with acts of Congress and regulations promulgated thereunder.
   ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGE. Alcohol, spirits, beer and wine as those terms are
defined herein and also includes every liquid or solid, patented or not,
containing alcohol, spirits, wine or beer and capable of being consumed as a
beverage by human beings.
   BEER. Any beverage of alcohol by volume and obtained by the alcoholic
fermentation of an infusion or decoction of barley, or other grain, malt or
similar products. BEER may or may not contain hops or other vegetable products.
BEER includes, among other things, beer, ale, stout, lager beer, porter and
other malt or brewed liquors, but does not include sake, known as Japanese rice
wine.
   INTOXICATING BEVERAGES. Beverages containing more than 3.2% alcohol by
weight.
   MIXED BEVERAGE. One or more servings of a beverage composed in whole or part
of an alcoholic beverage in a sealed or unsealed container of any legal size
for consumption on the premises where served or sold by the holder of a mixed
beverage, beer and wine, caterer, public event, charitable event or special
event license.
   NONINTOXICATING BEVERAGES. Beverages containing more than 0.5% alcohol by
volume and not more than 3.2% alcohol by weight.
   SPECIAL EVENT. An entertainment, recreation or marketing event that occurs
at any single location on an irregular basis and at which alcoholic beverages
are sold.
   SPIRITS. Any beverage, other than wine or beer, which contains more than
0.5% alcohol measured by volume, and obtained by distillation, whether or not
mixed with other substances in solution and includes those products known as
whiskey, brandy, rum, gin, vodka, liqueurs, cordials and fortified wines and
similar compounds, but shall not include any alcohol liquid completely
denatured in accordance with the Acts of Congress and regulations pursuant
thereto.
   WINE. Any beverage containing more than 0.5% alcohol by volume and not more
than 24% alcohol by volume at 60°F obtained by the fermentation of the natural
contents of fruits vegetables, honey, milk or other products containing sugar,
whether or not other ingredients are added, and includes vermouth and sake,
known as Japanese rice wine.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012; Ord. 23-002, passed 5-2-2023)
ARTICLE 2. ALCOHOLIC OR INTOXICATING BEVERAGES
§ 4-201 OCCUPATION TAX.
   (A)   The city shall collect an annual occupational tax for the privilege of
operating as a retailer, mixed beverage, caterer or special event licensee,
bottle club, manufacturer, wholesaler or Class B wholesaler, within the city
limits, to be identical in amount to that collected by the state for such
licenses. The license tax shall be levied only if the licensee has his or her
principal place of business within the city municipal limits.
   (B)   The city shall not have the authority to determine or regulate the
issuance of the license but shall issue the license if the licensee has
obtained a license from the Alcoholic Beverage Laws Enforcement Commission.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012)
Statutory reference:
   Annual license fees, see 37A O.S. §§ 2-101v1 through 2-101v2
§ 4-202 ANNUAL REPORT.
   The city shall report annually all occupational taxes levied to the ABLE
Commission for the fiscal year showing the number and class of licensees and
the amount of money received therefrom.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012)
Statutory reference:
   Similar provisions, see 37A O.S. §§ 1-104 and 1-105
§ 4-203 LOCATION OF BUSINESS.
   (A)   The location of a retail package store, mixed beverage establishment
or bottle club shall be subject to the zoning ordinances of the city and is
specifically prohibited within 300 feet from any church property primarily and
regularly used for worship services and religious activities or public school;
provided, that if any such church or school, shall be established within 300
feet of any licensed premises after such premises has been licensed, this shall
not be a bar to continuous force and effect.
   (B)   The distance indicated in this section shall be measured from the
nearest property line of such church or school to the nearest public entrance
door of the premises of such package store, mixed beverage establishment or
bottle club along the street right-of-way line providing the nearest direct
route usually traveled by pedestrians between such points.
   (C)   For the purpose of determining measured distance, property situated on
the opposite side of the street from such church or school shall be considered
as if it were located on the same side of the street with such church or
school. Furthermore, a license shall not be issued for a location on any city
block where a school or church is located.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012)
§ 4-204 HOURS OF SALE.
   No alcoholic beverages shall be dispensed, served or consumed on the
premises between the hours of 2:00 a.m. and 10:00 a.m.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012)
Statutory reference:
   Similar provisions, see 37A O.S. § 3-124
§ 4-205 LICENSE REQUIRED.
   (A)   There is hereby levied upon each person, partnership, firm or
corporation holding a lawful license issued by the State Alcoholic Beverage
Control Board for a principal place of business located in the city an annual
occupation tax in the amount of $1,000 the first year and $900 for each renewal
year. The occupation tax shall be levied from July 1 to June 30 of the
following year. The amount of the tax shall increase or decrease to conform to
maximum allowed by any municipality due to any changes or amendments to 37A
O.S. § 4-104.
   (B)   No municipal license shall be issued to any retail dealer by the City
Clerk without a satisfactory showing that the applicant has obtained all state
and county permits required by law and has in all other respects complied with
the State Alcoholic Beverage Control Act, being 37A O.S. §§ 1-101 through 1-
168.
   (C)   All licenses shall expire on June 30 of the year following issuance;
provided, however, that any failure to continue operation of the business for
more than 30 days or issuance of a license to another party at the same
location shall void the license. A new license must thereafter be obtained by
any prior license holder without regard to the license year. A license fee
shall be paid in connection with each application. The license may not be
transferred.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012)
§ 4-206 NUDITY AND DRINK SOLICITATION PROHIBITED.
   No private club licensee, operator, partner or manager, employee or any
other person having supervisory control shall permit any person to remain in or
upon the licensed premises who exposes to public view any portion of his or her
pubic hair, anus, genitals or female breasts below a point immediately above
the top of the areola. Nor shall any such person permit any person to remain in
or upon the licensed premises who solicits drinks from any patron of the
business.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012)
§ 4-207 VIOLATIONS OF STATE LAWS PROHIBITED.
   No private club nor any officer, director, stockholder, owner or manager
thereof licensed pursuant to the provisions of this article shall violate any
of the provisions of the State Alcoholic Beverage Law, being 37A O.S. §§ 1-101
through 1-168, nor any of the gambling laws of the state, nor knowingly permit
the violation thereof on any premises subject to the control of said private
club.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012)
§ 4-208 INSPECTIONS AND ENFORCEMENT.
   The Police, Fire, Health and Sanitation Departments shall inspect all
private clubs regularly to enforce all the terms of this article and report any
violations to the City Council. The city shall enforce all of the provisions of
the Alcoholic Beverage Control Act, being 37A O.S. §§ 1-101 through 1-168, as
required by 37A O.S. § 5-115 and shall be entitled to initiate a license
suspension or revocation proceeding as allowed by state law.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012)
ARTICLE 3. NONINTOXICATING BEVERAGES
§ 4-301 DEFINITIONS.
   (A)   For the purpose of this article, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
      NONINTOXICATING BEVERAGES. All beverages containing more than 0.5%
alcohol by volume and not more than 3.2% alcohol by weight.
      RETAIL DEALER. Any person, firm, corporation, association or
concessionaire who sells, distributes or dispenses, at retail, any alcoholic
beverage within the corporate limits of the city, without regard to any place
where such beverages may be consumed or used.
   (B)   The provisions of 37A O.S. § 1-103 are incorporated herein by
reference, and all provisions contained therein are declared to be in force as
if they were written herein in complete detail.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012; Ord. 23-002, passed 5-2-2023)
§ 4-302 LICENSES.
   (A)   (1)   No person, association, firm or corporation shall maintain or
operate any private club in the city without first paying to the City Clerk the
license fee hereafter prescribed and making application for license therefor on
forms provided by the City Clerk and receiving a license from the City Council.
In addition to the receipt of the City Clerk, any applicant for a license for a
private club shall file with the City Clerk true copies, in duplicate, of the
articles of incorporation and bylaws, if the applicant be a corporation; true
copies, in duplicate, of any articles of association and bylaws, if the
applicant is an association; and a list of the officers, directors, owners and
managers of said club and any stockholders who receive a financial return on
their stock.
      (2)   The annual license fee shall be $200 and shall be due and payable
on or before July 1 of each year.
   (B)   No municipal license shall be issued to any retail dealer by the City
Clerk without a satisfactory showing that the applicant has obtained all state
and county permits required by law, and has in all other respects complied with
the state law. All such licenses shall expire on June 30 of the year following
reissuance. No license shall be transferable.
   (C)   The City Council shall have the power, after public hearings, to
revoke any license granted hereunder for violation of law or ordinance by the
license holder.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012)
§ 4-303 PERSONS UNDER 21 YEARS OF AGE.
   (A)   It is unlawful for any person firm, or corporation who holds a license
to sell and dispense any alcoholic beverage or any agent, servant or employee
of said license holder to sell, barter or give to any person under the age of
21 years any alcoholic beverage. It shall also be unlawful for any person who
holds a license to sell and dispense any alcoholic beverage for consumption on
the premises, or any agent, servant or employee of said licensee to permit any
person under 21 years of age to be admitted to or remain in a separate or
enclosed bar area of the licensed premises unless said person’s parents or
legal guardian is present, which has as its main purpose the selling or serving
of alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises.
   (B)   The provisions of this section shall not prohibit persons under 21
years of age from being admitted to an area which has as its main purpose some
objective other than the sale or serving of alcoholic beverages, in which sales
or serving of said beverages are incidental to the main purpose, as long as
persons under 21 years of age are not sold or served said beverages; however,
the incidental service of food in the bar areas shall not exempt a licensee,
agent, servant or employee from the provisions of this section.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012; Ord. 23-002, passed 5-2-2023)
§ 4-304 HOURS OF SALE.
   It is unlawful for such beverages as herein defined to be sold for
consumption on the premises between the hours of 2:00 a.m. and 7:00 a.m. on any
day or to sell such beverages on Sunday.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012)
Statutory reference:
   Similar provisions, see 37A O.S. § 3-124
§ 4-305 SALES PROHIBITED IN CERTAIN LOCATIONS.
   (A)   Sales of alcoholic beverages for on-premises consumption is
specifically prohibited within 300 feet from any public school or church
property primarily and regularly used for worship services and religious
activities; provided, that if any such church, or school, shall be established
within 300 feet of any licensed premises after such premises has been licensed,
this shall not be a bar to renewal of such license so long as there has not
been a lapse of more than 60 days. The distance indicated in this section shall
be measured from the nearest property line of such church or school to the
nearest public entrance door of the premises of any place licensed to sell
alcoholic beverages for on-premises consumption along the street right-of-way
line providing the nearest route usually traveled by pedestrians between such
points.
   (B)   For the purpose of determining measured distance, property situated on
the opposite side of the street from such church or school shall be considered
as if it were located on the same side of the street with such church or
school; provided, further, that the above restrictions shall not affect
premises already licensed to sell alcoholic beverages for on-premises
consumption on premises which may presently or in the future be licensed to
sell alcoholic beverages for on-premises consumption even though a school or
church is subsequently established within 300 feet of such licensed premises.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012; Ord. 23-002, passed 5-2-2023)
§ 4-306 PERSONS UNDER 21 CONSUMING NONINTOXICATING BEVERAGES.
   No person under the age of 21 years shall consume or possess with intent to
consume any alcoholic beverage in any public place. The provisions of this
section shall not apply when such persons are under the direct supervision or
control of a parent or guardian, but in no instance shall this exception be
interpreted to allow such persons to consume such beverages in any place
licensed to dispense alcoholic beverages.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012; Ord. 23-002, passed 5-2-2023)
Statutory reference:
   Similar provisions, see 37A O.S. § 3-124
§ 4-307 EMPLOYMENT OF PERSONS UNDER 18 YEARS.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for any person under 18 years of age to be
employed or permitted to work in any capacity whatsoever in a place where
alcoholic beverages are sold for consumption on the premises.
   (B)   It shall be unlawful for any person under the age of 18 years to be
employed or permitted to work, in any capacity whatsoever, in the separate or
enclosed bar area of a place where the main purpose of the area is the sale or
consumption of alcoholic beverages. The provisions of this division (B) shall
not apply to any area which has as its main purpose some objective other than
the sale or serving of alcoholic beverages, in which sales or serving of said
beverages is incidental to the main purpose; however the incidental service of
food in the bar area shall not exempt a holder of a license to sell alcoholic
beverages for consumption on the premises from the provisions of this section.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012; Ord. 23-002, passed 5-2-2023)
Statutory reference:
   Similar provisions, see 37A O.S. § 6-102
ARTICLE 4. PENALTY
§ 4-401 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person violating any provision of this chapter shall be guilty of
a misdemeanor and, upon conviction thereof, shall be fined not to exceed the
amount set forth in §
3-501.
   (B)   Each day upon which a violation continues shall constitute a separate
offense.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012)
§ 4-402 GROUNDS FOR SUSPENSION AND REVOCATION OF LICENSE.
   (A)   (1)   Conviction in any court of competent jurisdiction, including the
City Municipal Court, of violating any of the provisions enumerated in this
section or the omission of acts enumerated in this section shall constitute
grounds for the suspension or revocation of any private club license issued
pursuant to this article by the City Council, after reasonable notice has been
given to the licensee, and a public hearing held by the City Council.
      (2)   For the purpose of this division (A), the following definitions
shall apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different
meaning.
         REVOCATION. A permanent termination of a private club license and
requires application for a new license.
         SUSPENSION. The temporary cessation of the private club license for a
period of time which includes the cessation of all rights and privileges to
operate a private club.
   (B)   The following shall constitute offenses and shall be grounds for
suspension or revocation of a private club license.
      (1)   No private club licensee shall allow the private club to remain
open during prohibited hours established by state law and local ordinances.
      (2)   No private club licensee shall employ any person under the age of
18 years or permit any person under the age of 21 years to handle, distribute
or serve alcoholic beverages.
      (3)   No private club licensee shall knowingly serve or furnish any
alcoholic beverage to an insane or mentally deficient person.
      (4)   No private club licensee shall knowingly serve or furnish any
alcoholic beverage to a person under the age of 21 years.
      (5)   No private club licensee shall knowingly allow the distribution of
controlled and dangerous substances as defined in 63 O.S. within the areas
under the control of the private club.
      (6)   No private club licensee shall allow any person who shall become
disorderly or violent to remain upon the private club premises; nor shall any
firearms be carried into or used on the premises.
      (7)   No private club licensee shall knowingly allow solicitation for
prostitution to occur upon the private club premises or to knowingly permit any
person who shall make such solicitation to remain upon the private club
premises.
      (8)   No private club licensee shall knowingly allow gambling on the
private club premises.
      (9)   No private club licensee shall willfully provide any false
information in any application for a private club license or in application for
renewal of such license.
      (10)   No private club licensee shall allow any designated fire exit to
be locked, blocked or access to such exit impeded in any manner during hours of
operation of the private club.
      (11)   No private club licensee shall knowingly serve or furnish any
alcoholic beverage to an intoxicated person.
      (12)   No private club nor any officer, director, stockholder, owner or
manager thereof licensed pursuant to the provisions of this article shall
violate any of the provisions of the State Alcoholic Beverage Law, being 37A
O.S. §§ 1-101 through 1-168, nor any of the gambling laws of the state, nor
knowingly permit the violation thereof on any premises subject to the control
of said private club.
      (13)   No private club licensee, operator, partner or manager, employee
or any other person having supervisory control shall permit any person to
remain in or upon the licensed premises who exposes to public view any portion
of his or her pubic hair, anus, vulva, genitals or female breasts below a point
immediately above the top of the areola.
   (C)   Upon receipt of a verified complaint alleging violation or violations,
the City Council may instigate an investigation to determine if a license
holder has violated any of the provisions contained in division (B) above. Upon
determination by the Council that probable cause exists to believe that a
violation or violations have been committed, then it shall schedule a public
hearing within a reasonable period of time to determine whether the Council
shall suspend or revoke the license, giving written notice to the licensee of
the alleged violation or violations and informing the licensee of his or her
right to have counsel present at the hearing, his or her right to cross-examine
any complaining witness and his or her right to present evidence in his or her
behalf. After conducting a public hearing, the Council shall determine, based
upon the preponderance of the evidence, whether the license should, under the
evidence presented and circumstances, be revoked or suspended. In making its
determination, the Council shall prepare written findings of fact and
conclusions of law. If the Council finds that the license should be suspended
or revoked, the Council may suspend or revoke the private club license based on
the following standards.
      (1)   The Council may suspend the private club license for a period up to
five days for the first determination by the Council that the private club
license should be suspended.
      (2)   The Council may suspend the private club license for a period up to
ten days in cases where the Council has conducted a prior hearing and has
suspended the club’s license and has conducted a second public hearing and
determined that the license should again be suspended.
      (3)   In cases where the City Council has suspended a private club
license pursuant to divisions (C)(1) and (C)(2) above and has conducted a third
hearing and determined that the private club license should again be suspended,
the Council may revoke the private club license for the remaining period of the
license year and shall, upon such revocation, order the City Clerk’s office not
to accept an application for that club’s license until 12 months have elapsed
from the date of the revocation.
   (D)   Any person, partnership, corporation or association which has operated
or held an ownership interest, in excess of 30%, in any private club at the
time of the revocation shall be prohibited from being a manager, owner or
operator of any private club or stockholder or officer of any corporation,
partnership or association, owning or operating a private club for a period of
12 months from the date of revocation.
   (E)   Any partnership, corporation or association operating a private club
while the license thereof is under revocation shall be guilty of an offense
and, upon conviction thereof, shall be fined not more than $100. A separate
offense shall be deemed committed on each day during or on which a violation of
this section occurs or continues.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012)
ARTICLE 5. SPECIAL EVENTS
§ 4-501 SPECIAL EVENT LICENSE.
   (A)   A special event license may be issued to a business or restaurant
which is already authorized to sell alcoholic beverages doing business in the
city on behalf of an organization association, or nonprofit corporation
organized for political, fraternal, charitable religious or social purposes.
   (B)   The holder of the special event license is authorized to sell and
distribute alcoholic beverages for consumption on the property immediately
outside the building in which the business or restaurant is normally run but
still on the premises owned or leased by the business or restaurant.
   (C)   The special event license may include permission to sell and
distribute alcoholic beverages for consumption on city property, such as a
block on an adjacent street which has been blocked off from automobile traffic
by the city, or a city park. The license will specify the parameters of the
property to be used for the event and the length of time the event may last. No
persons may be excluded from city property during the event solely for the
reason that he or she is not a member of the group sponsoring the event.
   (D)   The special event license must be approved by the City Manager and the
City Attorney. The license may be granted or denied on a case by case basis,
giving due consideration to the inconvenience to the citizens of the city and
the amount of city property sought to be used and the length of time for which
the permit is sought.
   (E)   The license will allow the business or restaurant to continue to sell
and distribute any other food or beverages it normally offers for sale, and the
licensee must offer substantial food items at the event.
(Ord. 2005-02, passed 9-6-2005; Ord. 23-002, passed 5-2-2023)
§ 4-502 LICENSE FEE.
   (A)   No person shall operate a special event without first obtaining a
license from the City Clerk. No particular application form is required, but
the application must specify the property sought to be used, whether it be
property owned by the restaurant or business or city property, the nature of
the event, the number of people expected, the amount of noise expected and the
length of time it is expected to last.
   (B)   A $100 fee shall be required to obtain a license pursuant to the
provisions of this article.
(Ord. 2005-02, passed 9-6-2005)
ARTICLE 6. GATHERINGS WHERE MINORS MAY CONSUME ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES
§ 4-601 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this article, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   GATHERING. A party, gathering or event where a group of three or more
persons have assembled or are assembling for a social occasion or a social
activity.
   MINOR. Any person under 21 years of age.
   PARENT. Includes adoptive parent, foster parent, stepparent and guardian.
   PREMISES. Any residence or other private property, place or premises,
including any commercial or business premises.
   RESPONSE COSTS. The costs associated with responses by law enforcement, fire
and other emergency response providers to a gathering, including, but not
limited to:
      (1)   Salaries for the amount of time responding to a gathering in
violation of this article and the administrative costs attributable to such
response;
      (2)   The costs of any medical treatment for any responders;
      (3)   The costs of repairs or use of city equipment involved in response
to a gathering in violation of this article; and
      (4)   Any other costs directly related to the enforcement of this
article.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012)
§ 4-602 CONSUMPTION OF ALCOHOL BY MINORS.
   Except as permitted by state law, it is unlawful for any minor to consume an
alcoholic beverage at any public or private place unless said minor is being
supervised by his or her parent.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012)
§ 4-603 HOSTING, PERMITTING OR ALLOWING GATHERING WHERE MINORS CONSUME ALCOHOL
PROHIBITED.
   It is unlawful for any person having control of any premises to knowingly
host, permit or allow a gathering to take place at said premises where at least
one minor consumes an alcoholic beverage. This section does not apply to
conduct involving the use of alcohol by a minor when said minor is with his or
her parent.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012)
§ 4-604 PENALTIES.
   (A)   A person who violates the provisions of this article shall be deemed
guilty of an offense and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punished by a fine
of up to $200.
   (B)   The city reserves its right to sue a violator of this article for its
response costs in district court.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012)
