ARTICLE 1. SPECIAL PROVISIONS
§ 6-101 CITY INSPECTOR, OFFICE CREATED, APPOINTMENT.
   There is hereby created the office of City Inspector who shall be appointed
by the City Manager. The City Inspector may be removed, demoted, laid off or
suspended at any time by the City Manager. In case of absence or disability of
the City Inspector, the City Manager may designate some qualified person to
perform the duties of the office during such absence or disability.
(Ord. 23-008, passed 11-7-2023)
§ 6-102 GENERAL POWERS AND DUTIES OF CITY INSPECTOR; ASSISTANT INSPECTORS;
SALARY.
   (A)   The City Inspector shall serve in such capacity and perform such
duties as the City Manager shall from time to time designate. The City
Inspector shall be primarily responsible for all inspections required by city
ordinances and state statutes, including, but not limited to, electrical,
plumbing and construction inspections. In conjunction with the City Manager,
the City Inspector shall inspect construction of off-site improvements. The
City Inspector may serve either on a full-time or part-time basis, as the City
Manager may determine is necessary. The City Inspector shall not be interested
directly or indirectly in the profits or emoluments of any contract, job, work
or service with or performed within the city.
   (B)   The City Inspector shall receive such salary or pay as the City
Manager determines is appropriate.
(Ord. 23-008, passed 11-7-2023)
§ 6-103 BUILDING OFFICIAL, CITY INSPECTOR.
   (A)   The City Inspector shall have the powers, duties and functions
prescribed for the “Building Official” by the code adopted by this chapter. The
powers, duties and functions of the Building Official may be performed by
authorized representatives of the Building Official and under his or her
supervision and control. The authorized representatives may bear such titles as
“Building Inspector,” “Gas Inspector,” “Plumbing Inspector,” “Electrical
Inspector” and so on, as may be deemed appropriate to indicate their respective
areas of concern. The authorized representative shall be appointed by the
governing body.
   (B)   When any ordinance or provision of any code adopted by this chapter
prescribes any power, duty or function for any of the authorized
representatives of the Building Official, the Building Official shall also have
such power, duty or function in the absence of the designated representative of
the Building Official.
§ 6-104 BUILDING PERMITS REQUIRED.
   (A)   Except as otherwise provided in division (B) below, no person shall
engage in the following acts without having first obtained the necessary
permits from the City Clerk:
      (1)   The installation of any electrical, gas distribution or plumbing
systems, or the subsequent modification of existing systems by a builder or
contractor. Systems shall not include any electrical unit installed merely by
use of electrical plug;
      (2)   The alteration, construction, enlargement, removal, relocation or
repair of any building or other structure;
      (3)   The construction, alteration, cutting, mutilation or changing in
any manner for any purpose, any paved or traveled portion of any street or
alley, curb, gutter, catch basin or other appurtenance of a street or alley or
any sidewalk;
      (4)   The construction or repair of any off-site improvement within the
city limits; and
      (5)   The installation of any air conditioning, heating or refrigeration
system, or the subsequent modification of existing systems. System shall not be
deemed to include window units or freestanding units that are installed merely
by use of electrical plugs.
   (B)   No permit is required under the following circumstances:
      (1)   Where a public utility corporation installs electrical conductors
or equipment in the generation, transmission, sale or use of electrical energy
as outlined in their franchises with the city;
      (2)   Where the ordinary interior alterations or repairs of buildings or
structures do not exceed $1,000, such alterations or repairs do not include the
removal of any portion of a stone, concrete or brick wall, such alterations or
repairs do not include the removal, change or closing of any stairway or
opening in an exterior wall; or
      (3)   Where the construction, alterations, cutting and changing of a
portion of any street or alley, any curb, gutter, catch basin or other
appurtenance of a street or alley is under the direct supervision of the city
administration.
§ 6-105 BUILDING PERMIT APPLICATIONS.
   (A)   A person desiring a building permit shall submit an application
therefor to the City Clerk on forms provided by the City Clerk. All
applications must be accompanied with a scaled plat plan showing the actual
shape and dimensions of the lot or lots to be built upon, or improvements being
made. All easements, streets or alley rights-of-way must be shown, as well as
the exact size of the existing buildings or structures on the lot or tract of
land and their location thereon and the lines within which the proposed
building or structure is to be erected or altered either above or below the
ground.
   (B)   All new applications for building permits must be accompanied with
scaled, detailed plans and drawings or blueprints of the structure and shall
show all dimensions, lot lines, setbacks, easements, sewers, drains, plumbing,
gas, heating, air conditioning, electrical outlets, wiring diagrams and any
fixtures either above or below the ground.
§ 6-106 ISSUANCE OF PERMIT; PERMIT AND DEPOSIT FEES; PENALTY; AND APPEALS.
   (A)   The City Inspector and City Manager shall approve all building
permits. The proposed building plans and specifications shall comply with the
ordinances of the city. The City Clerk, after approval and compliance as
required herein, shall issue the permit after the applicant has paid to the
City Clerk a permit fee as follows.
      (1)   (a)   Building permit fees for new single-family residential
construction are as follows.
 
0 - 500 sq. ft.         $100
501 - 1,000 sq. ft.     $150
1,001 - 1,500 sq. ft.   $175
1,501 - 2,000 sq. ft.   $200
2,001 - 2,500 sq. ft.   $225
2,501 sq. ft. and above $250
 
         (b)   In addition to the building permit fee, in accordance with the
above calculations, a $79.50 plumbing permit fee shall be charged; a $79.50
mechanical permit fee shall be charged; and a $79.50 electrical fee shall be
charged, which shall include $4.50 charged by the State Construction Industries
Board.
      (2)   (a)   Building permit fees for remodel of existing single-family
structures where the cost of such remodel exceeds $2,000 shall be $50 per
structure. Building permit fees for remodel of existing commercial structures
where the cost of remodel exceeds $2,000 shall be $75.
         (b)   Remodel of residential or commercial structures where the costs
do not exceed the thresholds established immediately above do not require a
building permit.
         (c)   However, all plumbing, electrical or mechanical work shall still
require applicable permits.
      (3)   (a)   Building permit fees for new commercial construction are as
follows.
 
0 - 500 sq. ft.         $125
501 - 1,000 sq. ft.     $150
1,001 - 1,500 sq. ft.   $200
1,501 - 2,000 sq. ft.   $225
2,001 - 2,500 sq. ft.   $250
2,501 sq. ft. and above $275
 
         (b)   In addition to the building permit fee in accordance with the
above calculations, a $79.50 plumbing permit fee shall be charged; a $79.50
mechanical permit fee shall be charged; and a $79.50 electrical fee shall be
charged, which shall include $4.50 charged by the State Construction Industries
Board.
      (4)   A $50 fee shall be charged for residential and commercial
structures in the event a reinspection becomes necessary.
      (5)   In addition to the above, the following permit fees shall be
required as applicable.
 
Residential                 Commercial
Roof                    $50 Roof                    $75
Safe room/storm shelter $25 Safe room/storm shelter $25
Sign with electric      $50 Sign with electric      $50
Sign without electric   $25 Sign without electric   $25
Swimming pool           $35 Swimming pool           $50
 
   (B)   Each application for building permits must be accompanied with a
deposit of $10 per $1,000 of estimated cost. The deposit will be applied toward
the permit fee if obtained by the applicant within 30 days from application
date. Otherwise, the deposit will be forfeited and the applicant shall apply
for a new permit.
   (C)   Any person, firm or corporation who violates any provision of this
chapter shall be punished by a monetary fine of not less than $50 nor more than
$750, or by imprisonment for a period not to exceed 60 days, or both by such
fine and imprisonment for each such violation or failure to comply. Each day
that a violation or failure to comply exists shall constitute a separate and
distinct offense, and any one or more of such offenses may be set out in any
complaint or information filed. In addition, or as an alternative, to the
penalties set forth immediately herein, any person, firm or corporation who
violates any provision of this chapter may be charged as a permit fee an amount
equal to two times the amount of the regular fee levied in division (A) above.
   (D)   Prior to beginning construction on any off-site improvements, the
contractor shall submit a copy of the contract documents and the maintenance
bond required by the chapter on subdivision regulations of this code to the
City Clerk. Inspection fees as established by the City Council by motion or
resolution shall accompany the contract documents. Upon receipt of the permit
to construct from the Health Department, if required, the application of a
building permit, if deemed complete, will be processed.
   (E)   The property owner or his or her authorized agent shall have the right
to appeal a decision or determination made by the Building/Code Official
relative to the application and interpretation of the appropriate code as
adopted by this chapter to the City Council whenever such property owner
believes:
      (1)   The true intent of the adopted codes, or the rules legally adopted
thereunder, have been incorrectly or improperly interpreted;
      (2)   The provisions of those codes do not fully apply; and/or
      (3)   An equally good or better form of construction is proposed.
(Ord. 2003-06, passed 12-2-2003; Ord. 2022-07, passed 12-6-2022; Ord. 24-004,
passed 4-2-2024)
§ 6-107 AUTHORITY OF PERMIT; WORK TO BEGIN WITHIN SIX MONTHS.
   (A)   A building permit issued shall be construed to be a license to proceed
with the work and shall not be construed as authority to violate, cancel, alter
or set aside any of the provisions of this code, nor shall such issuance of a
permit prevent the city, through its authorized representatives, from requiring
a correction of errors in plans or in construction or of violations of this
code.
   (B)   Every permit issued shall automatically become invalid six months
after its issuance unless the work authorized by such permit is commenced
within the six-month period. Every permit issued shall automatically become
invalid if the work authorized by such permit is commenced but is thereafter
suspended or abandoned for a period of one year after the time the work is
commenced.
   (C)   For good cause shown, one or more extensions of time, for periods not
exceeding 90 days each, may be allowed in writing by the authorized
representative of the city if the extensions are applied for prior to the time
the permit becomes invalid.
§ 6-108 COMPLIANCE WITH CITY CODE AND INSPECTIONS.
   (A)   Approval of the plans does not relieve the owner or his or her agent
of responsibility in complying with any and all other ordinances or provisions
of this code. The fact that any such approved plan contains matter contrary to
any ordinance or provision is not a bar to its strict enforcement.
   (B)   When the framing of any building or structure is completed, when any
rough electrical wiring or electrical installation work is completed, when any
rough plumbing is completed, or when any air conditioning, heating or
refrigeration system is initially installed, an inspection of that work shall
be given by the Building Inspector.
      (1)   No plumbing work or electrical wiring, installed electrical or gas
fixtures, or electrical or gas equipment requiring a building permit, shall be
used in a building or on any premises until it has also had a final inspection.
This provision shall not apply to use for purposes of construction prior to
final occupancy.
      (2)   All work found to be faulty or incorrectly or defectively installed
shall be corrected before any rough or final approval shall be given by the
Building Inspector; and when such has been corrected, notification for a
reinspection shall then be given to the Building Inspector.
      (3)   All inspections shall be made by the Building Inspector within two
working days from the receipt of the notification for the inspection or
reinspection.
      (4)   No work which is required to be inspected shall be covered over or
covered up prior to that particular inspection, and any covering in place shall
be removed upon the order of the Building Inspector.
§ 6-109 MOVING BUILDINGS, BUILDING NOT TO DETRACT.
   No building of any kind shall be moved into the city or moved from one
location in the city to another, whether the location is within a business zone
or a residential zone, unless such building is of such materials, construction
and appearance as not substantially to detract from the value and enjoyment of
the property in the locality where such building is to be located.
§ 6-110 CERTIFICATES OF OCCUPANCY REQUIRED.
   No person shall occupy or use or permit the occupation or use of any
commercial, industrial or residential building or structure without having
first obtained a certificate of occupancy from the City Clerk under those terms
and requirements hereinafter provided.
§ 6-111 WHEN CERTIFICATE REQUIRED.
   (A)   A certificate of occupancy is required on all commercial, industrial
or residential buildings or structures when such buildings or structures:
      (1)   Are newly constructed;
      (2)   Are structurally altered;
      (3)   Are enlarged through addition;
      (4)   Are unoccupied for a period of two or more years;
      (5)   Undergo a change of occupancy or usage inconsistent with the last
occupancy or usage; or
      (6)   Are situated upon a tract of land abutting a private roadway
easement as described by 11 O.S. § 45-104.
   (B)   The city, if requested, shall supply a certificate to any buyer or
lessee who is then negotiating for the sale or lease of such building or
structure.
§ 6-112 APPLICATION FOR CERTIFICATE; INSPECTION.
   (A)   Upon receipt of a written application for a certificate of occupancy,
the City Inspector or other designated official of the city shall, within five
days, conduct an inspection of the building or structure. If the building or
structure complies with the requirements of this code, the certificate shall be
issued.
   (B)   Copies of the certificate shall be furnished at cost upon the request
of those persons having a proprietary interest in those buildings or
structures.
§ 6-113 TEMPORARY CERTIFICATES.
   The City Inspector or other designated official of the city may issue
temporary certificates for residential buildings or structures only under the
following conditions:
   (A)   The temporary occupancy or use would not jeopardize life or property;
   (B)   The applicants seeking a temporary certificate are in immediate need
of housing and are purchasing the particular residence;
   (C)   The temporary certificate shall be issued for a period of time not to
exceed 60 days; and
   (D)   The temporary certificate shall not be issued more than once to a
particular residential building or structure.
§ 6-114 INSPECTIONS.
   (A)   Inspections for the issuance of certificates of occupancy shall be
made by the City Inspector or other designated official of the city.
   (B)   Inspections shall seek to ascertain:
      (1)   The proper installation of site improvements;
      (2)   The proper installation and operation of all fixtures;
      (3)   The attachment of all hardware and trim;
      (4)   The completion of other items specifically designated by the
appropriate inspector so as to ensure a building’s or structure’s immediate and
full occupancy or usage; and
      (5)   Compliance with the provisions of the Building Code adopted and in
force in the city.
§ 6-115 FEE FOR INSPECTION, REINSPECTION.
   (A)   The cost of an initial inspection shall be as set forth in §
6-117 of this article.
   (B)   The cost of any reinspection shall be as set forth in §
6-117 of this article.
   (C)   The costs of inspection for certificate of occupancy shall be borne by
that person, individual, partnership, corporation or other association which:
      (1)   Has title to the particular building or structure; and
      (2)   Undertakes or permits the undertaking of those activities listed in
§
6-111 of this article.
   (D)   The fee for the occupancy certificate shall be collected by the City
Clerk prior to the issuance of a building permit when a building permit is
required, or by either the City Clerk or by the City Inspector when no building
permit is required.
§ 6-116 WATER AND ELECTRIC SERVICES DEPENDENT ON CERTIFICATE.
   No person who is required to obtain a certificate of occupancy shall be
entitled to water or electric services until such time as he or she has
obtained such certificate of occupancy or temporary certificate of occupancy as
authorized under this chapter.
§ 6-117 INSPECTION FEES.
   The fees for inspections of buildings, occupancies, electrical, plumbing
installations, gas, heating and air conditioning, mechanical and other
installations, shall be as set by the City Council by motion or resolution.
Presently the permit rates are as follows.
   (A)   City permits, new and remodeling. These charges are set forth in §
6-106 of this article.
   (B)   Electrical permits and inspections. Each dwelling, multi-family
dwelling or business, upon completion of the basic wiring, will obtain a rough-
in inspection before any wall coverings (sheetrock, paneling and the like) are
attached to the walls. The cost for a rough-in inspection will be charged to
the master electrician and will be as follows:
      (1)   Base fee for the service, $25;
      (2)   This fee may be included in the building permit fee, as set forth
in §
6-106 of this article; and
      (3)   Failure to receive the rough-in inspection will result in a $35
fine to the master electrician and the wall coverings will have to be removed
for the inspection. In addition, each dwelling, multi-family dwelling or
business must receive a final inspection before occupancy. There will be no
charge for this inspection. Failure to receive a final inspection before
occupancy will result in a $35 fine for each day occupied without a final
inspection and will be payable by the master electrician. Provided, that no
permit fee set forth in this section shall be charged on any structure in a
zoned agricultural area.
   (C)   Plumbing permits, water, sewer, gas.
      (1)   Generally, $25; where reinspection is necessary on any permit, $50.
      (2)   This fee may be included in the building permit, as set forth in §
6-106 of this article, for residential new construction.
   (D)   Grace period. A grace period of seven days after notification of
violation will be allowed for compliance, after which a $25 per day fine will
be imposed.
(Ord. 2003-06, passed 12-2-2003)
§ 6-118 INITIAL AND YEARLY LICENSE FEES FOR ELECTRICIANS, PLUMBERS AND
JOURNEYMAN; EXAMINATION OF ELECTRICIANS; BOND.
§ 6-118-1 QUALIFICATION FOR JOURNEYMAN ELECTRICIANS.
   (A)   Each person applying for a journeyman’s license shall have at least
two years of verifiable experience as an apprentice or hold a journeyman’s
license in the state, or may in lieu of taking an examination show proof that
they hold a license in the cities of Purcell, Norman or Oklahoma City,
Oklahoma. The latter may only be accomplished after the completion of an
application and with the approval of the Electrical Inspector.
   (B)   Each person applying for a journeyman’s license shall be employed at
the time of the application and during the time that the person holds the
license by a corporation or firm that holds a contractor’s license in good
standing with the city.
§ 6-118-2 FEES FOR EXAMINATION AND LICENSES FOR JOURNEYMAN ELECTRICIANS.
   (A)   The fee of $5 will be assessed before the taking of each electrical
examination, payable to the city, to the City Clerk, during the regular
business hours of City Hall.
   (B)   The fee of $10 will be assessed for the journeymen’s license upon
successful completion of the examination, and $10 each year that it is renewed.
§ 6-118-3 QUALIFICATIONS FOR MASTER ELECTRICIANS.
   Each person applying for a master’s license shall have at least three years’
experience as a journeyman electrician in the state, or notarized proof if out
of state, or may in lieu of the examination show proof of a master’s license in
the cities of Purcell, Norman or Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. The latter may only
be accomplished after completion of an application and with approval of the
Electrical Inspector.
§ 6-118-4 FEES FOR EXAMINATION AND LICENSES FOR MASTER ELECTRICIANS.
   (A)   The fee of $25 will be assessed before the taking of each master’s
examination, payable to the city, to the City Clerk during the regular business
hours of City Hall.
   (B)   The fee of $100 will be assessed upon successful completion of the
examination for the license and a fee of $40 for each year renewed.
   (C)   Fees for master’s and journeyman’s licenses will become due and
payable on July 1 of each year commencing the year of 1981 and each following
year. Failure to renew the license will result in having to take the
examination again.
§ 6-118-5 FAILURE TO PASS EXAMINATION.
   (A)   Failure to pass the examination (master or journeyman) by an
individual will allow that person to appeal to the Electrical Board the same
night of the test. If not satisfied with the decision, that person may appeal
to the City Council on its next meeting night. The appeal must be in writing
and presented to the City Clerk at least three working days prior to the next
City Council meeting and to be placed on the agenda.
   (B)   The City Council will appoint an Appeal Board to consist of one master
electrician and two journeymen. This Appeal Board shall decide on the meeting
time and place and contact all interested parties in writing. If the Appeal
Board upholds the decision of the Electrical Board, then the applicant may
retake the test on the next testing night. Failure to pass the second time will
require the applicant to wait 90 days before retaking the test again.
§ 6-118-6 BONDS REQUIRED OF MASTER ELECTRICIANS AND PLUMBERS.
   (A)   A corporate surety bond for licenses and permits in the sum of $1,000
payable to the city shall be required and shall be permanently deposited with
the City Clerk prior to the issuance of any master’s license.
   (B)   Said bond shall be executed by the applicant by a surety authorized to
do business in the state and shall be for a period coterminous with the
master’s license.
   (C)   Said bond will be conditioned upon all of the following conditions.
      (1)   The master and all his or her agents and employees shall faithfully
and properly conduct business in compliance with all provisions of this code.
      (2)   The master electrician or plumber shall pay all fines and/or
penalties imposed by the courts of competent jurisdiction for violations of
said applicable provisions.
      (3)   The master shall protect, save harmless and indemnify the city
against any liability imposed by law against said city for the negligence of
said master, his or her agents or employees, which arises from any act or
omission of said individuals engaged in work pursuant to this code.
      (4)   Any person aggrieved may bring action against said bond for the
recovery of the penalty thereof to the same extent and with equal rights as
though such aggrieved person had been named as the obligee in the bond.
§ 6-118-7 MASTER ELECTRICIAN’S AND PLUMBER’S LICENSE.
   (A)   No person shall install, alter, maintain or repair any electrical
conductors or equipment as a master or journeyman in either trade without first
obtaining a license as provided in this code.
   (B)   No corporation, partnership or business shall engage in the
installation or servicing, alteration or repairing of any electrical conductors
or equipment without an appropriate master as an active officer of the
corporation or an active member of the firm, and the name and address of such
master and the name and address of the corporation or firm shall be certified
and registered with the City Clerk.
§ 6-118-8 FEES FOR MASTER AND JOURNEYMAN PLUMBERS.
   (A)   Fees for master and journeyman plumbers shall be as follows:
      (1)   Master plumber: $100; renewal fee: $40; and
      (2)   Journeyman plumber: $10.
   (B)   Fees shall be due and payable on July 1 of each year commencing the
year of 1981 and each following year thereafter.
§ 6-118-9 PROHIBITED ACTS.
   No master shall employ or hire anyone to work at, or permit any person to
work at, installing, servicing, altering or repairing any electrical conductors
or equipment, unless that person be a licensed journeyman, or that person be an
apprentice performing such work under the personal supervision of the licensed
journeyman or master.
ARTICLE 2. PLUMBING CODE AND REGULATIONS
§ 6-201 ADOPTION OF PLUMBING CODE.
   A certain document, three copies of which are on file in the office of the
City Clerk, being marked and designated as the International Plumbing Code,
2009 edition, as published by the International Code Council, be and is hereby
adopted as the Plumbing Code of the city for regulating and governing the
design, construction, quality of materials, erection, installation, alteration,
repair, location, relocation, replacement, addition to, use or maintenance of
plumbing systems as herein provided; providing for the issuance of permits and
collection of fees therefor; and each and all of the regulations, provisions,
penalties, conditions and terms of said Plumbing Code on file in the office of
the City Clerk, are hereby referred to, adopted and made a part hereof, as if
fully set out in this article.
(Ord. 2012-10, passed 2-5-2013)
§ 6-202 ADDITIONS, INSERTIONS AND CHANGES TO PLUMBING CODE.
   (A)   The following sections are hereby revised as follows.
      (1)   Section P-100.1 (page 5, second line). Insert “the City of
Lexington.”
      (2)   Section P-104.1 (page 6, second line). Insert “April 11, 1989.”
      (3)   Section P-114.2 (page 12, third line). Insert “as provided in the
city’s code of ordinances.”
      (4)   Section P-117.4 (page 13, fifth, sixth and seventh lines). Insert
“offense and punished as provided in the city’s code of ordinances.”
      (5)   Section P-118.2 (page 14, fifth line). Insert “fine as provided in
the city’s code of ordinances.”
      (6)   Section P-303.2 (page 32, third line). Insert “a distance in feet
as determined by the city code.”
      (7)   Section P-308.3 (page 33, second and third lines). Insert “a depth
in feet as determined by the City Inspector.”
   (B)   The BOCA Building Code shall be amended to require that all water and
sewer lines be installed with schedule 40 PVC or comparable lines.
§ 6-203 PLUMBING PERMITS REQUIRED; CITY CLERK TO ISSUE.
   No plumbing work shall be undertaken without a permit from the City Clerk
after review and approval of the City Inspector and City Manager; therefore,
applications for plumbing permits shall be made to the City Clerk. The
applicant shall provide such plans, specifications and other data as may be
reasonably required. The fee to be charged for a plumbing permit shall be as is
set from time to time by the City Council. Currently, the fee is $25. This fee
is included in the cost of the building permit for new residential
construction.
(Ord. 2003-06, passed 12-2-2003)
§ 6-204 REGISTRATION REQUIRED.
   (A)   It is unlawful for any person to engage in the business, trade or
occupation of a plumbing contractor (otherwise known as a master plumber), or
of a journeyman plumber, or of a plumber’s apprentice, in this city unless he
or she is registered with the City Clerk and has a current and valid
certificate of registration issued by the City Clerk.
   (B)   Only persons who have current and valid licenses as plumbing
contractors or as journeyman plumbers issued by the State Commissioner of
Health may register as such with the City Clerk. Only persons who have current
and valid certificates of registration as plumber’s apprentices issued by the
State Commissioner of Health may register as such with the City Clerk.
   (C)   Upon application to the City Clerk and the payment of the required
fees to the City Clerk’s office, the City Clerk shall register such applicants
and issue to them certificates of registration. The city certificates shall not
be valid after the termination or expiration of the state licenses or
certificates. Registration certificates of plumbing contractors and journeyman
plumbers issued by the city shall expire on June 30 of each year. The city
certificates of plumber’s apprentices shall expire when their state
certificates expire.
   (D)   A qualified person may register as a plumbing contractor, a journeyman
plumber or a plumber’s apprentice, in the same manner as in the original
instance and upon payment of the required fees.
§ 6-205 REVOCATION OF REGISTRATION.
   The City Council, upon at least ten days’ notice and adequate opportunity
for a public hearing, may revoke the city registration of any plumbing
contractor or journeyman plumber for violating any provision of the ordinances
or regulations of the city relating to the installation of plumbing or for any
other cause specified in the State Plumbing License Law.
Statutory reference:
   Similar provisions, see 59 O.S. § 1010
ARTICLE 3. ELECTRICAL CODE AND REGULATIONS
§ 6-301 ELECTRICAL CODE ADOPTED.
   (A)   For the purpose of the safeguarding of persons and of buildings and
their contents from hazards arising from the use of electricity for light,
heat, power, radio, signaling and for other purposes; and providing for basic
minimum provisions considered necessary for safety, to protect the general
health and welfare of the public, the Electrical Code known as the National
Electrical Code, latest edition thereof, with all amendments, additions and
deletions made, of which at least one copy will be filed in the office of the
City Clerk, is adopted and incorporated hereby as fully as if set out at length
herein.
   (B)   From and after April 11, 1989, the provisions of the code and this
article shall be controlling in the use of electricity within the corporate
limits of the city.
Statutory reference:
   Similar provisions, see 59 O.S. §§ 1680 through 1696
§ 6-302 MODIFICATIONS OF NATIONAL ELECTRIC CODE.
   (A)   The City Inspector, who shall serve as the Electrical Inspector unless
another person is designated by the City Council, may modify any of the
provisions of the National Electric Code upon the written application of the
owner or the master electrician when:
      (1)   There are practical difficulties in the strict enforcement or
compliance with the letter of the National Electric Code;
      (2)   The spirit of the National Electric Code is nonetheless observed;
      (3)   Public safety is still secured; and
      (4)   The Building Official concurs.
   (B)   Any particular modification which is granted or allowed shall be
reduced to writing over the signature of the Chief Electrical Inspector, shall
be maintained in the Public Works Department and shall be furnished to the
applicant.
   (C)   The National Electric Code shall be amended to require that copper
wire of proper rating be used on all repair, remodel or new wiring, both
commercial and residential.
§ 6-303 PURPOSE OF ELECTRICAL REGULATIONS.
   The purpose of this article is the practical safeguarding of persons and
buildings and their contents from electrical hazards arising from the improper
use of electricity for light, heat, power and for other purposes.
§ 6-304 SCOPE.
   (A)   The provisions of this article shall apply to all installations of,
and work done on electrical conductors, fittings, electronic devices and signs,
within or on public and private buildings and premises with exceptions as
provided herein.
   (B)   On all installations of electrical conductors or equipment hereafter
made, and all existing installations which are altered, or for which the use
has changed, all work shall be done in a manner that will conform with the
requirements for sufficient and safe electrical structure and systems under
this article and the Electrical Code adopted by the city.
   (C)   Repair and maintenance work shall be such that if any “electrical
conductor or equipment” is removed and later replaced, same shall be replaced
in accordance with the provisions of this article.
   (D)   The words “this article” means this article and the National
Electrical Code adopted in this article.
§ 6-305 RESPONSIBILITY FOR SAFE WORK.
   The electrical regulations of this article and the Electrical Code shall not
be construed to relieve from or lessen the responsibility or liability of any
person, firm or corporation owning, operating or installing electrical
conductors, devices, appliances, fixtures, apparatus or equipment for damages
to persons or buildings caused by any defect therein by reason of the
inspection herein authorized or the certificate of approved inspection issued
by the Electrical Inspector as herein provided; nor shall the city be held
liable for any damages by reason of the enforcement of this article.
§ 6-306 ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR.
   There is hereby created the office of Electrical Inspector, whose duty it
shall be to inspect all electrical installations and to issue a certificate of
compliance upon completion of each inspection, along with such other duties as
set forth in this article. The Inspector shall have at least five years of
active experience in the electrical industry and shall have no interest, direct
or indirect, in any firm or corporation engaged in the electrical industry. The
Electrical Inspector may hold more than one office in the city and his or her
salary, if any, shall be as determined by resolution or motion of the City
Council. The Electrical Inspector shall possess such other additional
qualifications, abilities and knowledge as, in the opinion of the City Council,
are required to perform the duties, and shall hold office at the discretion of
the City Council.
§ 6-307 POWERS OF ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR.
   The Electrical Inspector shall have the power:
   (A)   To order the electric service disconnected where improper or defective
wiring exists or where electrical construction or equipment has been installed
without a permit as required herein; and
   (B)   To order compliance with provisions of this article where a change of
occupancy occurs in a building which required changes or alterations to
existing wiring.
§ 6-308 INSPECTION REQUIRED.
   It is unlawful for any person, firm or corporation to make connections from
a source of electrical energy to any electrical wiring, devices or equipment on
an installation for which a permit is required as set forth in this article
until a certificate of approval has been issued by the Electrical Inspector
authorizing such connection and the use of such wiring.
§ 6-309 ROUGH INSPECTION.
   When the rough wiring or installation work is completed on any premises, the
person responsible therefor shall notify the Electrical Inspector that the job
is ready for inspection, giving proper identification of the work and address.
The Electrical Inspector shall then make an inspection of the electric
installation within 24 hours from the time of notification, exclusive of
Sundays and legal holidays. If the wiring or installation work has been
installed in accordance with the terms and provisions of this article, the City
Electrical Inspector shall sign the inspection card, noting thereon the date of
approval of the work. More than one rough inspection may be made without charge
when the progress of construction requires such inspection.
§ 6-310 FAULTY WORK.
   If the electric wiring or installation of fixtures or equipment is found to
be faulty, incorrectly or defectively installed, the Electrical Inspector shall
notify the responsible person who installed such work of the changes necessary
to be made in order that the work may conform to this article.
§ 6-311 RECTIFICATION OF FAULTY WORK.
   The electrician shall make the changes ordered and shall proceed with the
work until the same is completed. Upon completion thereof and payment of the
reinspection fee, he or she shall notify the Electrical Inspector to the effect
that faulty work has been corrected. The latter shall then cause the
reinspection to be made, and if the work is found to comply with this article,
he or she shall sign the inspection card noting thereon the date of approval of
the work. If the Electrical Inspector shall again find the work incorrectly
installed, he or she shall notify the responsible electrician of the necessary
changes and shall collect an additional reinspection fee. If the responsible
electrician does not make the required changes within a reasonable time, the
Electrical Inspector shall refuse to issue to any such person any further
permits until the work in question is corrected and approved.
§ 6-312 FINAL INSPECTION.
   (A)   Upon the completion of all electrical wiring or installation of
fixtures or equipment in any building or on any premises, the electrician in
charge shall notify the Electrical Inspector, giving the address.
   (B)   The Inspector shall then make an inspection within 24 hours from time
of receipt of the notice (except Sundays and legal holidays).
   (C)   If any faulty wiring or equipment is found, the electrician in charge
shall be notified of the changes to be made in order that such work shall
conform to this article.
§ 6-313 WORK TO BE LEFT OPEN UNTIL INSPECTION COMPLETED.
   It is unlawful for any person to cover or cause to be covered any part of a
wiring installation with flooring, lath, wallboard or other material until the
Electrical Inspector shall have approved the wiring installation in part or as
a whole.
§ 6-314 FEES FOR REGISTRATION OF ELECTRICIANS.
   (A)   (1)   The fees for a certificate of registration to qualified persons
of each class shall accompany the application for registration. The
registration fee shall be paid to the Electrical Inspector or authorized city
employee before the issuance of a certificate of registration and only after
the person has been approved by the State Electrical Board.
      (2)   Fees for master electrician or contractor, journeyman electrician
or electrical apprentice shall be as follows.
 
Electrical apprentice            $10
   Renewal                    $5
Journeyman electrician           $10
   Renewal                    $10
Master electrician or contractor $100
   Renewal                    $40
 
   (B)   Fees are due and payable on July 1 of each year commencing on the year
of 1991 and each following year thereafter.
Statutory reference:
   Similar provisions, see 59 O.S. §§ 1680 through 1696
§ 6-315 REVOCATION OF REGISTRATION.
   The City Council, upon at least ten days’ notice and adequate opportunity
for a public hearing, may revoke the city registration of any electrical
contractor or journeyman electrician for violating any provision of the
ordinances or regulations of the city relating to electrical work, or for any
other cause specified in the State Electrical License Law.
§ 6-316 CERTIFICATE OF REGISTRATION; EXPIRATION.
   A certificate of registration shall not be transferable and shall be issued
to the person examined by the Board and named on the certificate and known as
the holder of the certificate. A certificate of registration shall expire June
30 of each year and new application shall be required for reinstatement if the
required annual renewal fee is not paid within 30 days from the expiration
date.
§ 6-317 REGISTRATION CARD; RENEWAL, REPLACEMENT.
   (A)   A registration certificate or card of identification shall be issued
to each electrician. Each such registration certificate or card shall expire at
12:00 a.m. of June 30 of each year and a new card shall be issued each year
upon receipt of the annual renewal fee.
   (B)   Registration certificates or cards lost or destroyed during the year
for which they are issued shall be reissued by the city, provided satisfactory
evidence has been presented by the registrant of such loss or destruction, and
provided the registrant pays the City Clerk the sum of $1.
§ 6-318 DISPLAY OF EVIDENCE OF REGISTRATION.
   It is required that all registrants fittingly display their certificates of
registration and that they display their registration cards upon request to the
Electrical Inspector.
§ 6-319 CLASSIFICATION OF REGISTRATION FOR ELECTRICIANS.
   There shall be three classes of electrical registration which shall be known
as follows:
   (A)   Electrical contractor;
   (B)   Journeyman electrician; and
   (C)   Electrical apprentice.
§ 6-320 METHOD OF REGISTRATION; CONDUCT OF BUSINESS.
   (A)   To secure a registration as a qualified and competent electrician in
any of the classes set out in this article, an application shall be made in
writing and addressed to the Council. The application shall show the
applicant’s name and address and such other information as may be prescribed by
the Council.
   (B)   In addition to submitting a properly executed application, the
applicant, if of contractual status as specified under classification of
registration, shall file with the application an affidavit setting forth the
name of the person who is the owner of the business, his or her address or the
place of business; if the business is a firm, partnership or corporation, the
names of the officers who own or operate the business, their addresses, the
address of the business and the name and address of the person who shall be
responsible for the conduct and in charge of the business for all work under
this article.
   (C)   If the applicant intends to conduct the business and complete the work
himself or herself of installing, repairing and the maintaining of the
electrical conductors and equipment, he or she shall file with the application
an affidavit setting forth that such applicant is a journeyman electrician and
has a license from the state.
   (D)   Applicants for a certificate of registration as an electrical
contractor shall file with the application an affidavit setting forth that such
applicant is not less than 21 years of age, and has had experience in the
installation, alteration and repair of electrical equipment and conductors, and
also has an electrical contractor’s license from the state.
   (E)   An applicant for registration as an electrical apprentice shall make
in the application affidavit a statement that:
      (1)   The applicant is registered as an electrical apprentice with the
state and under the provisions of this article;
      (2)   The applicant shall perform all installation, alteration and repair
of electrical wiring, fixtures and equipment in accordance with this article;
and
      (3)   The applicant will not independently engage in the business of
contracting such electrical work unless he or she is also a registered
electrical contractor.
§ 6-321 PERMITS REQUIRED FOR ELECTRICAL WORK.
   (A)   No person shall install or cause to be installed, or to permit any
person to install “electrical wiring” or to make any alterations, additions or
changes within the scope of this Electrical Code, including any new circuits
installed or to be installed from existing or newly installed distribution
points, panels or breakers, or any change of service or meter loops, without
first procuring a permit therefor issued by the Electrical Inspector.
   (B)   No permit shall be issued except to a licensed electrical contractor,
or the building owner of an existing building or buildings, on which such
electrical wiring work is to be performed. Permits are required for maintenance
work or for repair work where wiring is altered or rearranged.
   (C)   Prior to commencement of any electrical wiring installation, the
electrical contractor or the building owner shall call the building inspection
and permits office or he or she or his or her authorized employee shall visit
the office and obtain a permit listing the name of the owner and contractor,
job name and address, building permit number and scope of electrical wiring.
When the permit is issued by telephone, the contractor’s copy shall be mailed
to his or her business address. The permit covers only that work listed
thereon; any additions or changes shall be reported to the inspection and
permits office and addition to the permits taken prior to requesting final
inspection.
   (D)   The Electrical Inspector may, if he or she deems it necessary, require
or demand from the electrical contractor a set of plans and specifications of
any job, in order that the Electrical Inspector may check same to determine if
the plans and specifications comply with this article. All applications for
permits on work involving higher than 600 volts, or services or circuits of
1,000 amperes or over, shall be submitted together with detailed plans and
specifications. The Electrical Inspector must render a decision on such plans
and specifications within three working days after receiving same.
   (E)   When a building or portion of a building containing electric wiring is
moved from its foundation, the owner shall have the electric wiring and
equipment in the building inspected and repaired where necessary, including
proper grounding. The electrical contractor shall obtain a wiring permit and
request inspections.
   (F)   The fee to be charged for an electrical permit shall be as is set from
time to time by the City Council. Currently, the fee is $25. This fee may be
included in the building permit fee for new residential construction (reference
§ 6-106 of this chapter).
(Ord. 2003-06, passed 12-2-2003)
§ 6-322 EXEMPTIONS.
   The provisions of this article shall not apply to:
   (A)   Minor repairs, consisting of repairing or replacing outlets or minor
working parts of electrical fixtures;
   (B)   Maintenance work for state and federal institutions;
   (C)   The construction, installation, maintenance, repair and renovation by
a public utility regulated by the corporation commission;
   (D)   Public service corporations, telephone and telegraph companies, rural
electric associations or municipal utilities; or
   (E)   The construction, installation, maintenance, repair and renovation of
telephone equipment or computer systems by a person, firm or corporation
engaged in the telecommunications or information systems industry when such
activities involve work exclusively for communication of data, voice or for
other signaling purposes; except fire alarm systems, security systems and
environmental control systems that are not an integral part of a
telecommunications system.
§ 6-323 PERMITS REFUSED.
   The Electrical Inspector may refuse to issue a permit for the installation
of electric wiring as herein provided, or for any additions or extensions to
any electric wiring in or on any building where, in his or her judgment, the
wiring done or proposed to be done is unsafe or not in accordance with the
provisions of this article.
§ 6-324 APPEALS FROM DECISIONS OF INSPECTOR OR ELECTRICAL BOARD.
   (A)   Any person aggrieved by an Inspector or the Board exercising his, her
or their power and authority pursuant to this article must, before instituting
suit, appeal to the City Council.
   (B)   Any such appeal shall be made within ten days after the decision of
the Inspector or the Electrical Board, and shall be in writing, stating the
reason for the appeal. The date and place of all hearings shall be fixed by the
City Council and all interested parties shall be given written notice of the
hearings.
   (C)   The City Council may either affirm, modify or reverse the decision of
the Inspector or Electrical Board and shall issue a written decision within ten
days of the date of the final hearing.
ARTICLE 4. BUILDING CODE AND REGULATIONS
§ 6-401 BUILDING CODE ADOPTED.
   A certain document, three copies of which are on file in the office of the
City Clerk, being marked and designated as the International Building Code,
2009 edition, as published by the International Code Council, be and is hereby
adopted as the Building Code of the city for regulating and governing the
conditions and maintenance of all property, buildings and structures; by
providing the standards for supplied utilities and facilities and other
physical things and conditions essential to ensure that structures are safe,
sanitary and fit for occupation and use; and the condemnation of buildings and
structures unfit for human occupancy and use and the demolition of such
structures as herein provided; providing for the issuance of permits and
collection of fees therefor; and each and all of the regulations, provisions,
penalties, conditions and terms of said Building Code on file in the office of
the City Clerk are hereby referred to, adopted and made a part hereof, as if
fully set out in this article.
(Ord. 2012-04, passed 2-5-2013)
§ 6-402 ADDITIONS AND CHANGES TO BUILDING CODE.
   The following sections of the BOCA Basic Building Code are hereby revised.
   (A)   Section 100.1, insert: “City of Lexington.”
   (B)   Section 114.3.1, insert: “The fee schedule shall be as may be set or
amended by ordinance or resolution.”
   (C)   Section 117.4, insert: “Offense, punishable by fine and imprisonment
as provided in the city code of ordinances.”
   (D)   Section 118.2, insert: “fine as provided in the city code of
ordinances.”
   (E)   Section 123.3, insert: “as set by the City Council.”
   (F)   Section 501.2, insert: “the boundaries of the fire limits as provided
in the city code of ordinances.”
   (G)   Sections 1807.2.1 and 1807.22, insert: “a number of feet to be
determined by the City Council,” in both locations.
   (H)   Section 1906.1, insert: “Amount as set by the City Council.”
§ 6-403 VARIANCE FROM BUILDING CODE AND ORDINANCES.
   Under special circumstances, in order to prevent undue hardship on a
property owner or owners, provisions of the Building Code and ordinances may be
varied for a particular building by a majority vote of the City Council. No
variance shall be permitted when it would be detrimental to the public welfare.
§ 6-404 DISTANCE OF DWELLINGS FROM SIDE LINES.
   Dwelling houses shall be of such materials and of such design, arrangement
and appearance as not substantially to detract from the value and enjoyment of
adjoining property, whether such adjoining property is improved or not.
§ 6-405 BUILDING PERMITS.
   The fees to be paid to the City Clerk prior to the issuance of a building
permit are as set forth in §
6-106 of this chapter.
(Ord. 2003-06, passed 12-2-2003)
ARTICLE 5. MECHANICAL CODE AND REGULATIONS
§ 6-501 POLICY OF CITY.
   It is hereby declared to be the policy of the city to protect and promote
the safety and welfare of the citizens of this city by regulating the
construction, installation and maintenance of heat or refrigeration producing
appliances, chimneys, vents and gas piping.
§ 6-502 MECHANICAL CODE ADOPTED.
   A certain document, three copies of which are on file in the office of the
City Clerk, being marked and designated as the International Mechanical Code,
2009 edition, as published by the International Code Council, be and is hereby
adopted as the Mechanical Code of the city for regulating and governing the
design, construction, quality of materials, erection, installation, alteration,
repair, location, relocation, replacement, addition to, use or maintenance of
plumbing systems as herein provided; providing for the issuance of permits and
collection of fees therefor; and each and all of the regulations, provisions,
penalties, conditions and terms of said Mechanical Code on file in the office
of the City Clerk are hereby referred to, adopted and made a part hereof, as if
fully set out in this article.
(Ord. 2012-08, passed 2-5-2013)
§ 6-503 NEW CONSTRUCTION.
   The owner and general contractor or builder of any residential or commercial
building or buildings situated within the limits of the city, the construction
and remodeling of which is subsequent to the enactment of this article, shall
each be responsible for the construction and installation of heat or
refrigeration producing appliances, chimneys and vents and gas piping in the
building or buildings in the manner as required by this article. Further, any
person who installs or constructs a heat or refrigeration producing appliance,
chimney, vent or gas piping within the limits of the city shall, likewise, be
responsible for compliance with the provisions of this article.
§ 6-504 STANDARDS ADOPTED; STANDARD MECHANICAL CODE.
   The standards, specifications and requirements for the installation and/or
construction of heat and refrigeration producing appliances, chimneys and
vents, as provided in the Building Code, the latest edition thereof and any
amendments or revisions thereto, are hereby adopted and incorporated as part of
the ordinances of the city.
§ 6-505 UNSAFE APPLIANCES.
   All unsafe heat or refrigeration producing appliances shall be made safe or
removed. All unsafe chimneys, vents and gas piping shall be made safe or taken
down.
§ 6-506 RECORDS.
   The City Clerk shall have available at all times for inspection and copying
a true and correct copy of the latest edition of the Building Code and shall
furnish, upon request, a copy of any portion or all of same upon payment of a
charge determined by the City Clerk sufficient to cover the expense of the
copying.
§ 6-507 ENFORCEMENT, RIGHT TO ENTER.
   (A)   The City Inspector or other officer designated by the Council, along
with the Police Department, shall be responsible for the enforcement of this
article.
   (B)   The City Inspector shall be initially responsible for determining
whether any heat or refrigeration appliance, chimney, vent or gas piping is
unsafe. With respect to all heat and refrigeration producing appliances,
chimneys, vents and gas piping installed or constructed prior to the enactment
of this article, the Fire Chief shall use the requirements of the standards of
the Building Code as much as practicable under the particular circumstances of
each instance. The installation, construction and maintenance of all heat
producing appliances, chimneys, vents and gas piping subsequent to the
enactment of this article shall be governed by the Standard Mechanical Code.
   (C)   In the event the City Inspector or the designee shall have good cause
to believe a violation of this chapter exists as to any building, he or she
shall be entitled to enter the building for the purpose of inspection thereof.
§ 6-508 REGISTRATION REQUIRED FOR GAS FITTERS.
   No person shall install, service, alter or repair on consumer premises any
gas equipment, pipes or lines as a master or journeyman in the plumbing or
mechanical trade without being registered under this article.
§ 6-509 MECHANICAL CONTRACTOR’S LICENSE.
   (A)   It is unlawful for any person to engage in mechanical contracting
business as defined in 59 O.S. §§ 1850.1 et seq., in this city unless he or she
is registered with the City Clerk and has a current and valid certificate of
registration issued by the City Clerk.
   (B)   Only persons who have current and valid licenses as mechanical
contractors or as journeyman issued by the State Commissioner of Health may
register as such with the City Clerk. Only persons who have current and valid
certificates of registration as contractor’s apprentices may register as such
with the City Clerk.
   (C)   Upon application to the City Clerk and payment of the required fees,
the City Clerk shall register such applicants and issue to them certificates of
registration. The city certificate shall not be valid after the termination or
expiration of the state licenses or certificates. Registration certificates of
mechanical contractors and journeyman contractors issued by the city shall
expire on June 30 of each year. The city certificates of apprentices shall
expire when their state certificate expires as per the terms of 59 O.S. §
1850.9(B).
   (D)   The annual registration fee shall be as follows.
 
Apprentice            $10
Journeyman            $10
   Renewal         $10
Mechanical contractor $100
   Renewal         $40
 
   (E)   The City Council, upon at least ten days’ notice and adequate
opportunity for a public hearing, may revoke the city registration of any
mechanical contractor or journeyman for violating any provisions of the
ordinances or regulations of the city or for any other cause specified in the
State Mechanical Licensing Act, being 59 O.S. §§ 1850.1 through 1860.
§ 6-510 WORK TO BE LEFT OPEN UNTIL INSPECTION COMPLETED.
   It is unlawful for any person to cover or cause to be covered any part of a
mechanical installation with flooring, lath, wallboard or other material until
the City Inspector shall have approved the installation in part or as a whole.
§ 6-511 CERTIFICATE OF REGISTRATION; EXPIRATION.
   A certificate of registration shall not be transferable and shall be issued
to the person examined by the Board and named on the certificate and known as
the holder of the certificate. A certificate of registration shall expire June
30 of each year and new application shall be required for reinstatement if the
required annual renewal fee is not paid within 30 days from the expiration
date.
§ 6-512 REGISTRATION CARD; RENEWAL, REPLACEMENT.
   A registration certificate or card of identification shall be issued to each
mechanical contractor. Each such registration certificate or card shall expire
at 12:00 a.m. on June 30 of each year, and a new card shall be issued each year
upon receipt of the annual renewal fee.
§ 6-513 PERMITS REQUIRED FOR MECHANICAL WORK.
   (A)   No person shall install or cause to be installed, or to permit any
person to construct or install heat or refrigeration producing appliances,
chimneys, vents or gas piping or to make any alterations, additions or changes
within the scope of this Mechanical Code, without first procuring a permit
therefor issued by the City Inspector.
   (B)   No permit shall be issued except to a licensed mechanical contractor,
or the building owner of an existing building or buildings, on which such work
is to be performed. Permits are required for maintenance work or for repair
work where a heat or refrigeration system, chimney, vent or gas piping is
altered or rearranged.
   (C)   Prior to commencement of any mechanical installation, the mechanical
contractor or the building owner shall call the building inspection and permits
office, or he or she or his or her authorized employee shall visit the office
and obtain a permit listing the name of the owner and contractor, job name and
address, building permit number and scope of the work. When the permit is
issued by telephone, the contractor’s copy shall be mailed to his or her
business address. The permit covers only that work listed thereon; any
additions or changes shall be reported to the inspection and permits office and
addition to the permits taken prior to requesting final inspection.
   (D)   The City Inspector may, if he or she deems it necessary, require or
demand from the mechanical contractor a set of plans and specifications of any
job, in order that the Electrical Inspector may check same to determine if the
plans and specifications comply with this article. The City Inspector must
render a decision on such plans and specifications within three working days
after receiving same.
   (E)   The fee to be charged for an electrical permit shall be as is set from
time to time by the City Council. Currently the fee is $25. This fee may be
included in the fee for new residential construction (reference §
6-106 of this chapter).
(Ord. 2003-06, passed 12-2-2003)
§ 6-514 EXEMPTIONS.
   (A)   No person shall install, replace or repair any heat or refrigeration
producing appliance, chimney, vent or gas piping unless such person is
registered under this article or is registered as a plumbing contractor or
journeyman plumber pursuant to this article.
   (B)   The Mechanical Code shall not apply to:
      (1)   A person who is the property owner of record, or his or her
authorized representative, when performing minor repair which shall include,
but not be limited to, cleaning, adjusting, calibrating and repair of
mechanical system parts and the replacement of fuses and room thermostats and
other minor repairs which shall not include any repair which could violate the
safe operation of the equipment;
      (2)   The installation of portable, self-contained, ductless air
conditioners or heaters;
      (3)   The setting or connecting of detached air conditioning units which
utilize flexible ductwork on a manufactured home. The term “manufactured home”
shall have the same definition as such term is defined in 47 O.S. § 1102; or
      (4)   The installation of boilers which are subject to the jurisdiction
of the Commissioner of Labor pursuant to the provisions of 40 O.S. §§ 141.1
through 141.18.
   (C)   The registration requirements of the Mechanical Code shall not apply
to public utilities, public service corporations, rural electric associations
or municipal utilities and their subsidiaries during work on their own
facilities or during the performance of energy audits, operational inspections,
minor maintenance or minor repairs for their customers or on their own
equipment.
§ 6-515 PERMITS REFUSED.
   The Electrical Inspector may refuse to issue a permit for the installation
of a heat or refrigeration producing appliance, chimney, vent or gas piping as
herein provided, or for any additions or extensions in or on any building
where, in his or her judgment, the work done or proposed to be done is unsafe
or not in accordance with the provisions of this article.
