ARTICLE 1. FIRE PREVENTION
§ 10-101 GOVERNED BY STATE LAW.
   The City Fire Department shall be subject to and governed by the provisions
of the State Volunteer Firefighters’ Act, being 11 O.S. §§ 29-201 to 29-205.
§ 10-102 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   MUNICIPALITY. One who is qualified to participate in the Firefighters’
Relief and Pension Fund.
   PUBLIC STORM SHELTER. The storm shelter located at the city public school
campus or any other storm shelter constructed or wholly owned by the city, if
any, which is intended by the owner to be made available for use by the general
public during an emergency.
   SERVICE ANIMALS. Dogs that are individually trained to do work or perform
tasks for people with disabilities.
   VOLUNTEER FIRE DEPARTMENT. One which has in its employ not more than two
full-time firefighters.
   VOLUNTEER FIREFIGHTER. One who is enrolled as a member of the Fire
Department and who serves in said capacity without receiving a regular salary.
(Ord. 2022-004, passed 6-7-2022)
§ 10-103 VOLUNTEER FIRE DEPARTMENT.
   (A)   (1)   The volunteer Fire Department shall consist of not less than 12
and not more than 20 members. Members of the City Fire Department may continue
as members of the volunteer Fire Department established under this code of
ordinances without probation, but shall be subject to the bylaws authorized
under this article.
      (2)   All new members shall be on probation for one year after their
appointment to the Department and shall not become regular members of the
Department upon completion of their probation period until their approval by a
majority of the regular members of the volunteer Fire Department.
   (B)   The volunteer Fire Department shall adopt bylaws, a copy of which
shall be deposited with the City Clerk and shall include the following.
      (1)   All volunteer firefighters are required, when notified, to respond
to alarms of fire and other emergencies.
      (2)   All volunteer firefighters are required to be present at all
regular meetings, call meetings and schools and training classes presented for
the benefit of the firefighters.
      (3)   There shall be at least one regular business meeting each month.
      (4)   Any volunteer firefighter having two unexcused absences in
succession, or three unexcused absences in a period of three months, will be
expelled from the Fire Department rolls.
      (5)   Volunteer firefighters leaving the city for an extended period of
time will be required to notify the Fire Chief.
      (6)   Any volunteer firefighter refusing to attend training classes
provided for him or her will be dropped.
      (7)   Any volunteer member of the Fire Department shall be dropped from
the rolls for the following offenses:
         (a)   Conduct unbecoming to a firefighter;
         (b)   Any act of insubordination;
         (c)   Neglect of duty;
         (d)   Any violation of the rules and regulations governing the Fire
Department; or
         (e)   Conviction of a felony.
§ 10-104 FIRE DEPARTMENT TO ENFORCE REGULATIONS.
   The fire prevention regulations adopted by the City Council shall be
enforced by the Fire Department of the city, under the supervision of the Fire
Chief, who may appoint such members of the Fire Department as inspectors as
shall be necessary.
§ 10-105 RURAL FIREFIGHTING ASSESSMENT.
   There is hereby assessed a charge for each call the Fire Department has to
make outside the city limits, which said charge shall be paid by the owner and/
or occupant of the property on which the fire occurs. The charge shall be as
follows: $200 for the first hour and $50 per hour thereafter, to be determined
from the time of leaving the fire station and the time of return.
ARTICLE 2. FIREWORKS AND EXPLOSIVES
§ 10-201 SALE OR POSSESSION OF FIREWORKS PROHIBITED.
   It shall be unlawful and an offense for any person, firm or corporation to
sell or have in his, her or its possession or to discharge, ignite or in any
manner aid, assist or abet in the discharging or igniting of any firecrackers
of any size, type or description, skyrockets, pistols, torpedoes, Roman
candles, flash salutes, flash rockets, balloons or other fireworks or
substances designed and intended for pyrotechnic display, also other appliances
using caps containing chlorate or potash mixture within the city limits, unless
previously authorized by the City Council or its designee.
(Ord. 2018-03, passed 5-1-2018)
§ 10-202 EXPLOSIVES.
   It shall be unlawful for any person or persons to store, keep, to have on
their premises or in their possession any explosive articles in the nature of
dynamite, blasting powder or other explosive materials of any kind or nature
without first having complied with the laws of the state, for the purpose of
selling, storing or keeping such articles.
ARTICLE 3. PENALTY
§ 10-301 PENALTY.
   Any person, firm or corporation who violates any provision of this chapter,
including any code adopted by the city, shall be guilty of an offense and, upon
conviction, shall be fined in any sum not to exceed the sum set forth in §
3-501 of this code, including costs. Each day upon which a violation continues
shall be deemed a separate offense.
ARTICLE 4. RURAL FIRE MEMBERSHIP SERVICE
§ 10-401 ESTABLISHMENT.
   (A)   Establishment and direction. There is hereby established the “City
Rural Fire Membership Service,” to be operated by the City Fire Department, but
shall be under the direction of the City Manager and City Council.
   (B)   Operation for rural residents. The rural fire service shall be
operated primarily for the purpose of providing fire protection to rural
residents living outside the corporate limits of the city, but within the area
generally encompassed by the city mailing route or any other area recommended
by the Rural Fire Advisory Board and approved by the City Council.
   (C)   Annual membership fee. The service to be provided is unlimited fire
runs to any member’s property within the area referred to in division (B) above
upon the annual payment of a membership fee, as set by the City Council, by
each property owner or resident residing on another’s property. The initial
membership fee shall be $50.
   (D)   Due date. Payment of the membership fee is due on or before July 1 of
each year.
   (E)   Cost to members who have not paid membership fee by due date. The cost
of a fire run for a member whose dues are not current shall be as set forth in
§
10-105 of this chapter.
   (F)   Use of funds, payment of claims. The monies collected from the members
in payment of their annual dues shall be placed in a separate account in the
General Fund to be used for the purchase and maintenance of fire trucks and
equipment and to otherwise operate the Fire Department, including the payment
of claims and other financial transactions.
   (G)   Limitations of responsibility.
      (1)   In the performance of fire prevention or protection services
outside the corporate limits of the city, the City Fire Department shall not
assume responsibility for damages to structures or other casualty incurred
prior to the arrival of the Department, nor shall the Department assume
responsibility for damages to structures incurred as a result of late
notification of the members of the Department.
      (2)   The Fire Department must always keep the property within the city
limits as its first priority and may not be able to provide assistance if the
equipment and personnel needed to respond are also needed in the city. Weather
conditions may also prohibit the Fire Department from responding.
      (3)   The Fire Chief or his or her designee may decide not to respond or
to leave a scene if, in his or her discretion, lives would be endangered by
responding or remaining.
   (H)   Collection of dues. Unpaid fees, charges or annual memberships may be
subject to collection by the city in any manner normally employed by the city,
including the use of small claims procedures in the district court. A person
will be dropped from the membership roles for nonpayment of dues.
   (I)   Expenses to member’s insurer. The expense to a member’s fire insurance
company shall be based on the same rate as set forth in §
10-105 of this chapter.
(Ord. 2006-02, passed 6-6-2006)
§ 10-402 ADVISORY COMMITTEE.
   (A)   Establishment. There is hereby established a City Rural Fire Committee
for the purpose of advising the City Council concerning the operation of the
rural fire membership service.
   (B)   Composition. The Advisory Board shall consist of a city representative
and four additional members, who shall be appointed by the City Council from
the rural members of the rural fire membership service.
   (C)   Eligibility and terms. All paying members of the rural fire membership
service shall be able to serve on the Advisory Committee. The Committee members
shall serve for three-year staggered terms.
   (D)   Meetings.
      (1)   The Advisory Committee shall normally meet at least once each
quarter of the year, with more meetings as necessary.
      (2)   Their meetings shall comply with the Open Meeting Act, being 25
O.S. §§ 301 et seq., and their minutes comply with the Open Records Act, being
51 O.S. § 24A.1.
      (3)   They shall report to the City Clerk at least once each quarter.
   (E)   Submission of purchases and activities for Committee’s review.
      (1)   The Fire Chief shall be responsible for ensuring that proposed fire
protection related purchases and activities are submitted to the Advisory Board
for its recommendation and comment prior to final action by the City Council,
if in excess of $1,000.
      (2)   Failure to submit such proposals to the Advisory Board shall not
invalidate City Council action on any such proposal.
(Ord. 2006-02, passed 6-6-2006)
ARTICLE 5. PUBLIC STORM SHELTER
§ 10-501 AVAILABILITY.
   (A)   Any public storm shelter may only be available for utilization as is
more particularly set forth below upon approval of, and at such times, as the
owner of the public storm shelter may allow. Any public storm shelter owned by
a school district or located on a school campus may only be made available as
set forth below during such dates and times when school is not in session and,
in such case, all rules, laws and regulations pertaining to the school property
and grounds shall apply.
   (B)   In all cases, the provisions of this article shall be construed in
such a way as to ensure the liability exemptions of the Governmental Tort
Claims Act, being 51 O.S. §§ 151 through 200, apply.
(Ord. 2022-004, passed 6-7-2022)
§ 10-502 POWERS.
   (A)   The decision to open or utilize, including the decision to close, any
public storm shelter, as that term is defined in §
10-102, shall be vested solely with the Chief of the Fire Department for the
city, or in his or her absence, the designee of the Chief of the Fire
Department.
   (B)   (1)   Upon making a determination that a public storm shelter should
be opened to the public and that personnel qualified to such position, pursuant
to the training and/or licensure requirements of the public storm shelter
owner, is/are available, the Chief of the Fire Department shall designate not
less than one member of the City Fire Department to maintain a presence at the
public storm shelter at all times between the time it is opened to the time it
is closed.
      (2)   Such individual shall be referred to as the Shelter Supervisor.
   (C)   (1)   No individual may be selected as Shelter Supervisor who does not
qualify under the required terms of the public storm shelter owner.
      (2)   Furthermore, any individual selected must maintain in good standing
all training and/or licenses required by the owner of the public storm shelter.
   (D)   No public storm shelter shall be opened unless a Shelter Supervisor,
with such qualifications as required by the owner, is appointed and available
to remain present at the public storm shelter at all times between the time it
is opened to the time it is closed.
(Ord. 2022-004, passed 6-7-2022)
§ 10-503 PUBLIC STORM SHELTER REGULATIONS.
   (A)   Any public storm shelter shall only be opened and closed pursuant to
the direction of the City Fire Chief. When the Fire Chief directs any public
storm shelter to be closed, all individuals must immediately evacuate the
public storm shelter.
   (B)   Only certified service animals may accompany any individual into any
public storm shelter. No emotional support animals or pets of any kind are
permitted entrance into any public storm shelter.
   (C)   Except for law enforcement personnel, firearms are strictly forbidden.
No individual, except for the Shelter Supervisor, or other on-duty member of
law enforcement, possessed with any firearm will be permitted entrance into any
public storm shelter.
   (D)   Smoking, vaping or use of tobacco in any form is prohibited in any
public storm shelter and, in the case of a public storm shelter located on
school grounds, on all school property.
   (E)   Alcohol and drugs (other than those prescribed by a physician) are
prohibited in any public storm shelter and, in the case of a public storm
shelter located on school grounds, on all school property.
   (F)   Radios or music devices are permitted in any public storm shelter only
with individual earphones.
(Ord. 2022-004, passed 6-7-2022)
§ 10-504 NONCOMPLIANCE.
   Any public storm shelter occupants who do not adhere to the public storm
shelter regulations or, in the judgment of the Shelter Supervisor, are
disruptive to the orderly functioning of the public storm shelter will be
referred to security or local law enforcement personnel and may be removed from
the facility.
(Ord. 2022-004, passed 6-7-2022)
CHAPTER 11: GARBAGE AND OTHER REFUSE

ARTICLE 1. GARBAGE AND TRASH COLLECTION
§ 11-101 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   GARBAGE. Includes kitchen and table refuse, offal and every accumulation of
animal and vegetable matter which attends the preparation of, decay of, dealing
in or storage of meats, fruits, vegetables and other provisions for human
sustenance.
   SEWAGE. Includes water, human excrement and liquid refuse that should
properly be disposed of through the sanitary sewers of the city, but shall not
include rainwater, soil drainage or other drainage.
   TRASH and RUBBISH. Includes paper, rags, containers of paper, wood or tin,
tin cans, yard and house sweepings and all other household wastes, except tree
trimmings, building and manufacturing wastes, SEWAGE and GARBAGE as herein
defined, grasses, weeds, leaves and rocks.
§ 11-102 GARBAGE AND TRASH TO BE COLLECTED.
   Every person, firm or corporation using or occupying any building, house or
structure, within the city, shall be required to collect, separate and dispose
of all garbage, trash and sewage as provided in this article. It is unlawful
for any person, firm or corporation to collect, separate or dispose of garbage,
trash or sewage in any manner except as provided herein.
§ 11-103 GARBAGE CANS TO BE PROVIDED.
   Every person, firm or corporation using and occupying any building, house or
structure within the city shall maintain a garbage can or cans of sufficient
size to hold the garbage and trash which will ordinarily accumulate between the
times when the garbage is collected.
§ 11-104 REFUSE CONTAINERS; BUNDLES OF TRASH.
   (A)   Refuse cans or containers shall be portable, with handles, and
constructed of watertight plastic or galvanized metal or equivalent in such a
manner as to be strong, not easily corrodible, rodentproof, flyproof and shall
have a tightfitting lid. The cover shall not be removed except when depositing
or removing the contents of the receptacle.
   (B)   Such containers shall have a capacity of not less than 20 gallons and
not more than 30 gallons, and if one container is not sufficient to hold the
quantity of refuse that will accumulate between collections, a sufficient
number of containers shall be provided. Refuse container surfaces shall be kept
free of garbage accumulations by wrapping, in paper, all garbage placed in the
container, by washing the container or by other means.
   (C)   Business establishments may provide a box or other receptacle with a
tight cover for the accumulation of rubbish, and said container shall be of
such construction and design that it can be maintained in a sanitary condition.
Containers shall be located and maintained so as not to create a fire hazard or
provide harborage for rodents or the breeding of insects and shall be placed at
an easily accessible place on the premises.
§ 11-105 GARBAGE AND TRASH TO BE PLACED IN CANS.
   (A)   All garbage, as defined herein, shall be placed in the garbage cans
maintained for that purpose. Before placing garbage in the can, all the liquid
portion of the garbage shall be drained into the sanitary sewer. The lid or
cover must be kept on the can at all times and fastened so that flies and other
insects or animals may not have access to the contents therein and shall be
removed only while depositing additional garbage or trash, or while the city
employees are removing and unloading the contents of the can for disposal.
   (B)   All trash as defined herein, shall be placed in the can with the
garbage, but only to such extent as will permit the cover or lid of the can to
be properly placed on the can. All trash in excess of that placed in the can
with the garbage shall be placed in a separate container or bundle and securely
tied and fastened so that it may be safely carried without coming apart or
spilling.
   (C)   Cans containing other than garbage or trash, as defined herein will
not be collected until such prohibited materials have been removed by the
person responsible for placing them in the can, and the collector shall
promptly report such person to the head of his or her department.
§ 11-106 TREE TRIMMINGS AND BUILDING MATERIALS.
   (A)   Definitions. For the purpose of this section, the following
definitions shall apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a
different meaning.
      COMMERCIAL. Any business activity or use within the corporate limits of
the city.
      CURBSIDE SERVICE. Collection service provided by the city at the curb or
within the public street right-of-way.
      EXCESSIVE TREE TRIMMINGS. Anything above normal tree trimmings and the
load shall not exceed six feet wide by four feet high, by 12 feet in length,
and limbs shall not exceed ten inches in diameter.
      NORMAL TREE TRIMMINGS. Tree cuttings, debris or trimmings. Trimmings
shall be stacked, not to exceed two feet wide by three feet high, by six feet
in length, limbs shall not exceed three inches in diameter, and all limbs must
be piled in the same direction with the cut ends facing the roadway.
      RESIDENTIAL. Any resident living within the corporate limits of the city
having an active utility account.
   (B)   Free residential collection of normal and excessive tree trimmings.
The city shall conduct free limb and brush collection of normal and excessive
tree trimmings throughout the city during the third week of each month except
for the months of November and December. There will be no brush pick-up in
November and December. Brush and limbs shall not be placed for pickup prior to
the Saturday of the week it is to be picked up. All limbs must be piled in the
same direction with cut ends facing the roadway. The below stated fees shall be
charged for the collection of tree trimmings placed at curb side or alley that
fall outside the free limb and brush collection period set forth above.
   (C)   Additional residential and commercial collection and/or disposal
services of tree trimmings.
      (1)   Residential and commercial customers may request special curb side
collections of normal tree trimmings which fall outside the “free” collection
period set forth herein through the utility billing office. Tree trimmings to
be collected must be arranged so as to not constitute a safety hazard and
remains the resident’s responsibility, until removed by the city. Tree
trimmings to be collected through these additional services shall be placed at
curb side with the same rules and conditions set forth herein. No trimmings
shall be placed in the alley with the exception of those residences or
businesses whose property fronts upon a state or federal highway in which case
the trimmings will be placed in the alley.
      (2)   Any brush, limbs or trimmings piled at curbside or alley longer
than seven days shall be collected by the city at resident’s or businesses’
expense without any further notice. Cost will be assessed on-site.
      (3)   For residential and commercial curbside service for normal tree
trimmings, a fee of $15 per load will be assessed.
      (4)   For residential and commercial curbside service for excessive tree
trimmings, a fee of $50 per load will be assessed.
   (D)   General. Tree trimmings, building and manufacturing wastes, grasses,
leaves, weeds, rocks and other debris shall not be allowed to accumulate upon
any premises in the city so as to create a menace to health, a fire hazard or
an unsightly appearance and shall be removed at the expense of the person
responsible for the accumulation at the rates set forth in division (C) above.
(Ord. 2016-06, passed 8-2-2016; Ord. 2020-03, passed 9-1-2020)
§ 11-107 SEWAGE TO BE DRAINED OFF.
   All sewage, as herein defined, shall be drained off and disposed of through
the proper receptacles into the sanitary sewer.
§ 11-108 GARBAGE, RUBBISH AND TRASH TO BE COLLECTED BY CITY.
   All garbage, rubbish and trash in the city shall be collected by employees
of the city, and it is unlawful for any other person to collect or dispose of
or to haul or transport the same, or to molest or interfere with the contents
of any receptacle containing garbage, rubbish or trash; provided, however, that
in the event the waste materials are such that the city has no facilities to
properly collect and dispose of the waste matter or the collection or disposal
would create a hardship to the city, the city may license a private service to
dispose of the material. Collections by the city employees shall be made at
regular intervals, to be determined by the Council.
§ 11-109 GARBAGE OR TRASH NOT TO BE BURNED IN CITY.
   It is unlawful for any person or persons to burn garbage, rubbish or trash
within the city limits of the city.
§ 11-110 FEES FOR COLLECTION OF GARBAGE.
   (A)   The following fees shall be charged and collected per month by the
city for the disposition and collection of garbage, rubbish and trash:
      (1)   Residential. For each residence, occupied apartment or mobile home:
$7.50; and
      (2)   Commercial. For each commercial pick-up: $5.92 per each two-yard
dumpster per pick-up, plus 10%. Commercial customers not using dumpsters shall
be billed at the rate of one 1-yard dumpster per once a week pick-up, or $2.96
per pick-up, plus 10%.
   (B)   Following is a schedule indicating the monthly charges for various
kinds of commercial garbage service.

§ 11-111 COLLECTION OF FEES.
   (A)   The items mentioned in §
11-110 are charges for garbage service and shall be chargeable to the person or
persons, owner, occupant or lessee of all premises, and shall be collected by
and through the Water Department monthly in the same manner as charges for
water service are collected.
   (B)   A statement of the same shall be rendered on the water bill statement
and shall be due and payable at the same time as such bills for water service
and, in the event of the failure to pay the same, the garbage service shall be
discontinued, together with the water service, until such charges have been
paid, and the city shall have the right to discontinue the service or to file a
complaint against the occupant in the Municipal Court for his or her failure to
pay for such service and, upon conviction thereof, shall be fined in any sum
not to exceed $20, together with costs, and each day shall be considered as a
separate offense for nonpayment as long as payment is not made.
ARTICLE 2. PENALTY
§ 11-201 PENALTY.
   Any person who violates any provision of this article, either by doing that
which is prohibited or by failing or refusing to do that which is commanded,
shall be guilty of an offense and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punished
by a fine in any amount not exceeding the sum set forth in §
3-501, including costs. Each day of such violation shall be a separate offense.

ARTICLE 1. CONTAGIOUS DISEASES
§ 12-101 INTRODUCING DISEASES.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for any person infected with or exposed to any
contagious or infectious disease to appear upon the street or in any public
place in the city so as to expose other persons to such disease.
   (B)   It shall be unlawful for any parent, guardian or person having charge
of any child or children to allow, permit or suffer such child or children to
attend any classes, school or any gathering of people, or to appear upon the
street or in any public place in the city, while infected with or exposed to
any contagious or infectious disease, or in any manner so as to expose other
persons to such disease.
   (C)   No person suffering from, or infected with, a communicable form of a
venereal disease, shall engage in any occupation involving intimate contact
with children or in the occupation of nurse, domestic servant, barber,
hairdresser, chiropodist, manicurist, bath attendant, masseur or food handler.
§ 12-102 REPORT OF CONTAGIOUS DISEASES.
   (A)   Every practicing physician in the city shall report to the Public
Health Official within six hours after the diagnosis of any of the following
diseases:
      (1)   Diphtheria (including membranous croup);
      (2)   Scarlet fever;
      (3)   Smallpox;
      (4)   Yellow fever;
      (5)   Typhoid fever;
      (6)   Typhus fever;
      (7)   Asiatic cholera;
      (8)   Chickenpox;
      (9)   Tuberculosis;
      (10)   Undulant fever;
      (11)   Acute anterior poliomyelitis (infantile paralysis);
      (12)   Epidemic cerebrospinal meningitis;
      (13)   Whooping cough and mumps; and
      (14)   Any other pestilential, infectious or contagious disease.
   (B)   Syphilis, gonococcus infection and chancroid are hereby and
hereinafter recognized and declared to be contagious and infectious,
communicable and dangerous to the public health. For the purpose of this
article, the term VENEREAL DISEASE shall include all such diseases.
   (C)   The laws of the state governing the diseases stated hereinabove shall
apply to cases of this nature after said report is made.
§ 12-103 QUARANTINE.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for any person to enter or go upon any ground or
premises under quarantine without first having obtained permission of the
Public Health Official to do so.
   (B)   It shall be unlawful for any person whom the Public Health Official of
the city shall have ordered to be detained in quarantine to neglect or refuse
to be so detained, or willfully violate any quarantine regulation thereof;
every day of such neglect or refusal shall constitute a separate offense.
   (C)   It shall be unlawful for any person to tear down, remove, deface,
mutilate or destroy any order, notice or flag that may be posted or displayed
by the Public Health Official of the city.
   (D)   It shall be unlawful for any person to willfully violate or refuse to
comply with the lawful order, direction, prohibition, rule or regulation of the
Public Health Official or any officer charged with enforcement of such order,
direction, prohibition, rule or regulation.
§ 12-104 POLICE DUTIES.
   It shall be the duty of the City Police Chief and all peace officers to
apprehend all persons coming within the provisions of this article and to aid
and assist, in every way possible, the local, county and state health officials
in enforcing each and every provision in this article.
ARTICLE 2. TOILET FACILITIES
§ 12-201 SANITARY TOILET FACILITIES REQUIRED.
   (A)   Every residence and building equipped with toilet facilities, in which
humans reside or are employed or congregate, shall be required to have a
sanitary method for the disposal of human excreta, namely, a sanitary water
closet or closets or sanitary pit privy or privies. The sanitary toilets
required by this article shall be the sanitary water closet type when the
property is served by the sanitary sewer system.
   (B)   All privies not adjacent to a sanitary sewer line shall be of the
sanitary pit type as approved by the State Health Department or sanitary water
closets.
§ 12-202 PROPER DISPOSAL REQUIRED.
   It shall be unlawful for any person, firm or corporation owning or occupying
property within the city, to permit the disposal of human excreta on any
property owned or occupied by such person, firm or corporation, except in a
flush-type sanitary water closet or closets if the property is served by the
sanitary sewer system of the city; or in a sanitary pit privy or privies if the
property is not served by the sanitary sewer system of the city.
§ 12-203 SEPTIC TANKS.
   No septic tank, liquefying closet or chemical closet shall be constructed
within the corporate limits of the city, without a permit from the City Health
Officer, and same must comply with the requirements of the State Health
Department.
§ 12-204 COST TO BE BORNE BY OWNER.
   The cost of providing for a sanitary method of disposal of human excreta
shall be borne by the owner of the property upon which the sanitary pit privy
or privies are located in the city.
§ 12-205 COUNCIL TO CAUSE OFFICER TO MAKE INSPECTIONS.
   (A)   It shall be the duty of the Council to cause the Health Officer or
other duly authorized representative to make an inspection of the methods of
disposal of sewage within the city, within five days after the effective date
hereof and as frequently thereafter as is necessary to secure compliance with
this article.
   (B)   (1)   Written notification of any violation of this article shall be
given by the Health Officer or their duly authorized representative to the
owner and occupant of the property upon which the violation occurs.
      (2)   If the provisions of this article have not been complied with
within the period of five days following date of notice of violation, the owner
or owners of the property shall be prosecuted in accordance with the provisions
of this article.
§ 12-206 TOILET FACILITIES TO BE KEPT CLEAN; USE.
   (A)   All privies shall be kept clean at all times and the seat of the
privies shall be kept closed at all times when the privies are not being used.
   (B)   (1)   No wash water, kitchen slop or anything other than human excreta
and toilet paper shall be emptied into a privy.
      (2)   No excreta from any person suffering with typhoid fever, dysentery
or other serious bowel diseases shall be deposited in any sanitary pit privy or
sanitary water closet until the same shall be disinfected in such manner as may
be prescribed by the City Health Officer.
§ 12-207 TOILET FACILITIES; NUISANCE.
   All privies on any premises within the city, not constructed and maintained
in conformity with the provisions of this article and the Housing Code are
hereby declared to be a nuisance and a menace to public health.
§ 12-208 “HUMAN EXCRETA” DEFINED.
   For the purpose of this article, HUMAN EXCRETA shall be construed to mean
the bowel and kidney discharges of human beings.
§ 12-209 “SANITARY WATER CLOSET” DEFINED.
   For the purpose of this article, SANITARY WATER CLOSET shall be construed to
mean the flush-type toilet which is connected with a sewer line of sufficient
capacity and so constructed as to carry away the contents at all times.
§ 12-210 “SANITARY PIT PRIVY” DEFINED.
   For the purpose of this article, SANITARY PIT PRIVY shall be construed to
mean a privy which is built or constructed so as to conform to the
specifications approved by the State Health Department.
§ 12-211 “HEALTH OFFICER” AND “CHIEF OF POLICE” DEFINED.
   For the purpose of this article, HEALTH OFFICER and CHIEF OF POLICE shall be
construed to mean the persons appointed to said positions or the person or
persons authorized to act as their agents.
ARTICLE 3. CAFÉS AND RESTAURANTS
§ 12-301 SANITATION.
   All persons, firms or corporations operating a restaurant, café, drive-in
and/or beer parlor shall comply with the State Department of Health sanitation
requirements.
§ 12-302 HEALTH CERTIFICATE.
   (A)   All persons who handle food shall have a certificate of health or a
letter stating that such person is not a carrier of a communicable disease, and
such certificate shall be obtained each six months and signed by a doctor of
medicine or a doctor of osteopathy.
   (B)   The person shall comply with all state and health requirements.
ARTICLE 4. MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS
§ 12-401 ABANDONED ICEBOXES.
   It is unlawful for any person, firm or corporation to leave or permit to
retain outside of any dwelling, building or other structure or within any
unoccupied or abandoned building, dwelling or other structure under his or her
or its control, in a place accessible to children, any abandoned, unattended or
discarded icebox, refrigerator or other container which has an airtight door or
lid, snaplock or other locking device which may not be released from the
inside, without first removing the snaplock or other locking device from the
icebox, refrigerator or container.
§ 12-402 REMOVAL OF DEAD ANIMALS.
   No person shall permit any dead animal to remain on his or her premises for
a longer period than 24 hours. It shall be his or her duty, immediately upon
information that a dead animal is on his or her premises, to have the same
removed. He or she shall remove the same and make disposition of it as required
by the regulations of the State Health Department. No dead animals shall be
buried within the city.
§ 12-403 STAGNANT WATER.
   It is unlawful for any person, being the owner or occupant of any premises
in the city, to permit any stagnant water to stand or remain on any of his or
her premises so situated. All such places shall be drained, filled to a natural
level and kept in such condition that the water will flow away and not stand or
stagnate.
§ 12-404 WELLS.
   No person shall deposit any excrement, foul or decaying matter or other
deleterious substance in any public fountain, trough, watering place, well or
spring situated on any private or public property within the city or within
five miles of the corporate limits thereof.
§ 12-405 SPITTING.
   It is unlawful for any person to spit or expectorate upon any sidewalk,
crosswalk, floors of any church, public hall, theater, school, depot, railroad
or bus station or other public place of assembly, or waiting room or other
place of congregation.
ARTICLE 5. AMBULANCE SERVICE
§ 12-501 CITY MAY PROVIDE SERVICE.
   The city may provide ambulance service to the city and may, in its
discretion, discontinue ambulance service at any time. If the city provides
ambulance service, the cost shall be charged directly to the citizens as
follows.
   (A)   All residential users of either water, garbage, sewer or electricity
residing within the limits of the city shall be assessed a monthly fee of $4
per household or business. The fee may be changed by the Council by motion. The
fee shall be assessed for each rental unit or mobile home served through a
common meter. It shall also be assessed for each bed in a nursing home. The
landlord or lot owner or nursing home shall be liable for payment of the fee,
which shall inure to the benefit of the tenant occupying the home or rental
unit or bed for the period during which the fee is assessed. All persons who
are charged the fee shall receive the services provided for the residents of
the city by the city’s contract with Wadley Ambulance Service, a copy of which
is on file with the City Clerk for public inspection.
   (B)   The city shall have the right to collect for all charges by any means
available to the city.
ARTICLE 6. HOUSING CODE
§ 12-601 APPLICATION OF ARTICLE.
   No person shall occupy as owner-occupant, or permit a member of his or her
family to occupy, or let to another for occupancy any dwelling or dwelling unit
which does not comply with the provisions of this article.
§ 12-602 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this article, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   APPROVED. Authorized by the Health Officer, who, in addition to the City
Council, shall be authorized to determine whether or not a dwelling or dwelling
unit complies with this article.
   BASEMENT. A portion of a building located partly underground but having less
than one-half of its clear floor to ceiling height below the average grade of
the adjoining ground.
   CELLAR. A portion of a building located partly or wholly underground and
having one-half or more than one-half of its clear floor to ceiling height
below the average grade of the adjoining ground.
   DWELLING. Any building or structure, or part thereof, which is used or
intended to be used for living or sleeping by human occupants. Mobile temporary
housing, as hereinafter defined, shall not be regarded as a DWELLING.
   DWELLING UNIT. Any room or group of rooms located within a dwelling and
forming a single habitable unit with facilities which are used or intended to
be used for living, sleeping, cooking and eating.
   EXTERMINATION. The control or elimination of insects, rodents or other pests
by elimination of their harboring places; by removing or making inaccessible
material that may serve as their food; by poisoning, spraying, fumigating,
trapping or blocking their access to a dwelling; or by any other recognized and
legal pest elimination methods approved by the Health Officer.
   HABITABLE FLOOR AREA. The square footage in a habitable room, which shall be
used in computing maximum permissible occupancy. At least one-half of the
HABITABLE FLOOR AREA shall have a height of at least seven feet, and the floor
area of that part of any room where the ceiling height is less than five feet
shall not be considered in computing HABITABLE FLOOR AREA.
   HABITABLE ROOM. A room or enclosed floor space used or intended to be used
for living, sleeping, cooking or eating purposes, excluding bathrooms, water
closet compartments, laundries, pantries, foyers, communicating corridors,
closets and storage spaces.
   HABITATION. A dwelling, dwelling unit, rooming house, rooming unit, mobile
home and premises, or any part thereof.
   HEALTH OFFICER. The County Health Official or his or her authorized
representative.
   INFESTATION. The presence, within or around a dwelling or anywhere on the
premises, of insects, rodents or other pests, in such numbers as to constitute
a hazard to health.
   OCCUPANT. Any person living, sleeping, cooking, eating in or having
possession or use of a dwelling unit or rooming unit. For the purpose of this
definition, a person under one year of age shall not be counted as an OCCUPANT.
   OPERATOR. Any person who has charge, care or control of a building or part
thereof in which dwelling units are let.
   OWNER. Any person who, along or jointly or severally with others:
      (1)   Has legal or equitable title to any dwelling or dwelling unit with
or without actual possession thereof; or
      (2)   Has charge, care or control of any dwelling or dwelling unit, as
owner or agent of the owner, or an executor, executrix, administrator,
administratrix, trustee or guardian of the estate of the owner. Any such person
thus representing the actual owner shall be bound to comply with the provisions
of this article, and with rules and regulations adopted pursuant thereto, to
the same extent as if he or she were the owner.
   PLUMBING. All of the following supplied facilities and equipment: gas pipes,
gas burning equipment, water pipes, mechanical garbage disposal units, waste
pipes, water closets, sinks, installed dishwashers, lavatories, bathtubs,
shower baths, installed clothes washing machines, catch basins, drains, vents
and any other similar supplied fixtures, together with all connections for
water, sewer or gas lines.
   PUBLIC SPACE. Space within a residential building for public use, such as
lobbies, lounges, reception halls, meeting, lecture and recreation rooms, and
dining rooms and their kitchens, and swimming pools.
   REFUSE. All waste substances other than garbage, including, but not limited
to, the following trash or waste material: paper, rags, cartons, boxes, wood,
excelsior, rubber, leather, tree branches, yard trimmings, tin cans, metals,
mineral matter, glass, crockery, plastics, ceramic material and dust.
   ROOMING HOUSE. Any dwelling or part thereof in which a rooming unit is let
by the owner or operator to three or more persons who are not related to the
owner or operator by blood or marriage; or any dwelling or part thereof
containing two or more rooming units.
   ROOMING UNIT. Any room or group of rooms in a rooming house or dwelling
forming a single habitable unit used or intended for use for living or sleeping
but not for cooking or storing food for eating purposes.
   SUBSTANTIAL REPAIR OR REMODEL. Any repair or remodel work exceeding in cost
the sum of $500 involving any installation of electrical, plumbing, heat and
air conditioning equipment or appliances.
   SUPPLIED. Paid for, arranged for or furnished or provided by or under
control of the owner or operator.
§ 12-603 ELECTRICITY.
   Dwellings shall be supplied with electricity and shall meet the following
requirements.
   (A)   Every habitable room shall contain at least two separate wall type
electric convenience outlets or one such convenience outlet and one supplied
ceiling type light fixture.
   (B)   Every water closet compartment, bathroom, laundry room or public hall
shall contain at least one ceiling or wall type electrical light fixture.
   (C)   Every public hall or stairway in or leading into every multiple
dwelling shall have a minimum of one foot-candle of illumination measurable
with a standard light meter at floor level in halls and at tread level on
stairways when the structure is occupied.
§ 12-604 HEATING.
   Every dwelling unit shall have properly installed heating facilities which
are maintained in safe and good working condition, and are capable of safely
and adequately heating all habitable rooms, bathrooms and water closet
compartments therein to a temperature of 70°F at a distance three feet above
floor level at an outside temperature of 0°F. The heating equipment shall be
operated as is reasonably necessary to maintain a temperature in all habitable
rooms at not less than 70°F.
§ 12-605 LIGHT, VENTILATION.
   Every habitable room shall have at least one window or skylight facing
directly to the outdoors. The minimum total window area, measured between
stops, shall be 10% of the habitable floor area of such room. If the only
window in the room is a skylight type window in the top of the room, the total
window area of the skylight shall equal at least 15% of the habitable floor
area of the room it serves.
   (A)   In every habitable room, at least 40% of the window or skylight
required shall be easily opened unless one of the following methods of
ventilating the room is approved.
      (1)   For inside habitable rooms, a wall area equivalent to 20% of the
floor area must open into a room with adequate light and ventilation. In such
cases, the window area shall be at least 8% of the total floor area to be
served by such windows.
      (2)   Kitchens may be equipped with a ventilation system capable of
continuous operation.
   (B)   Bathrooms and waste closet compartments may be equipped with a
ventilation system which is capable of continuous operation.
   (C)   Whenever walls or other portions of structures face a window of any
room and such light obstructing structures are located less than three feet
from the window and extend to a level above that of the ceiling of the room,
the window shall not be deemed to face directly to the outdoors and shall not
be included as contribution to the total required window area.
§ 12-606 MAINTENANCE.
   (A)   Every foundation, floor, wall, ceiling and roof shall be reasonably
weathertight, watertight and rodentproof; shall be capable of affording
privacy; and shall be kept in good repair.
   (B)   Every window, exterior door and basement hatchway shall be reasonably
watertight, weathertight and rodentproof; and shall be kept in good repair.
   (C)   Every inside and outside stair, every porch and every appurtenance
thereto shall be so constructed as to be safe to use and capable of supporting
the load that the normal use may cause to be placed thereon; and shall be kept
in sound condition and good repair.
   (D)   Every plumbing fixture and water and waste pipe shall be properly
installed and maintained in good sanitary working condition, free from defects,
leaks and obstructions.
   (E)   Every water closet compartment floor surface and bathroom floor
surface shall be constructed and maintained so as to be reasonably impervious
to water and so as to permit such floor to be easily kept in a clean and
sanitary condition.
   (F)   Every supplied facility, piece of equipment or utility which is
required by this article shall be so constructed or installed that it will
function safely and effectively, and shall be maintained in satisfactory
working condition.
   (G)   No owner, operator or occupant shall furnish or use any cooking
equipment which does not comply with the following minimum standards.
      (1)   Every piece of cooking equipment shall be so constructed and
installed that it will function safely and effectively and shall be maintained
in sound working condition.
      (2)   Portable cooking equipment employing flame and cooking equipment
using gasoline or kerosene as fuel for cooking are prohibited.
   (H)   No owner, operator or occupant shall cause any service, facility,
equipment or utility which is required under this article to be removed from or
shut off from or discontinued for any occupied dwelling let or occupied by him
or her, except for such temporary interruptions as may be necessary while
actual repairs or alterations are in process, or during temporary emergencies
when discontinuance of service is approved by the Health Officer.
   (I)   No owner shall occupy or let to any other occupant any vacant dwelling
unit unless it is clean and in a sanitary condition.
§ 12-607 SANITATION.
   (A)   Every dwelling unit shall contain the following facilities:
      (1)   A kitchen sink in good working condition and properly connected to
hot and cold water lines and a sewage disposal system;
      (2)   A flush water closet, located within the building and in a room
affording privacy, and which is properly connected to a water line and sewage
disposal system;
      (3)   A bathtub or shower, located within the building and in a room
affording privacy, and which is properly connected to a water line and sewage
disposal system; and
      (4)   A lavatory which shall be supplied by both hot and cold water lines
and connected to a sewage disposal system.
   (B)   Upon application and after hearing, the Council may grant its approval
and permission for the occupants of not more than two dwelling units occupying
the same building to share a flush water closet, a lavatory basin and a bathtub
or shower. In no event shall a total of more than six persons occupy the
dwelling units sharing such sanitary facilities.
   (C)   Where both city water supply and sanitary sewer are available, no
septic tank shall be installed. When a sanitary sewer is not available, a
septic tank may be installed which is in compliance with the rules and
regulations of the State Health Department and the provisions of this code.
   (D)   Every dwelling shall have the proper garbage and refuse containers.
   (E)   Every owner of a dwelling containing three or more dwelling units
shall be responsible for maintaining in a clean and sanitary condition the
shared or public areas of the dwelling and the premises thereof.
   (F)   Every occupant of a dwelling or dwelling unit shall be responsible for
maintaining in a clean and sanitary condition that part of the dwelling,
dwelling unit and premises thereof which he or she occupies and controls.
   (G)   Every occupant of a dwelling unit shall dispose of all his or her
garbage and rubbish in a clean and sanitary manner, by placing it in garbage
disposal facilities or in proper containers. It is the responsibility of the
owner to supply such facilities or containers for all dwelling units in a
dwelling containing four or more dwelling units and for all dwelling units
located on premises which four or more dwelling units share. In all other
cases, it shall be the responsibility of the occupant to furnish such
facilities or container.
§ 12-608 SPACE AND LOCATION.
   (A)   (1)   Every dwelling unit shall contain at least 150 square feet of
habitable floor space for the first occupant thereof and at least 100
additional square feet of habitable floor space for every additional occupant.
A dwelling unit, exclusive of mobile homes, shall contain at least one
habitable room having a minimum horizontal dimension of ten feet. The amount of
area allowed as habitable floor area for the purpose of complying with these
regulations shall not be in excess of 80% of the gross floor area.
      (2)   For the purpose of this division (A), GROSS FLOOR AREA includes all
of the area encompassed by measuring from the outside face of the exterior
walls.
   (B)   In every dwelling unit of two or more rooms, every room occupied for
sleeping purposes by the occupant shall contain at least 70 square feet of
floor space; and every room occupied for sleeping purposes by more than one
occupant, including buildings operated as clubs, shall contain at least 50
square feet of floor space for each occupant thereof.
   (C)   No dwelling or dwelling unit containing two or more sleeping rooms
shall have such room arrangement that access to a bathroom or water closet
compartment intended for use by occupants of more than one sleeping room can be
had only by going through another sleeping room; nor shall room arrangement be
such that access to a sleeping room can be had only by going through another
sleeping room, a bathroom or water closet compartment.
   (D)   No basement or cellar space shall be used as a habitable room or
dwelling unit unless:
      (1)   The floor and walls are impervious to leakage of underground and
surface runoff water and are insulated against dampness;
      (2)   The total of window area in each room is equal to at least the
minimum window area sizes as required in this article; and
      (3)   The total area of window which can be opened in each room is equal
to at least the minimum required in this article, except where there is
supplied some other device affording adequate approved ventilation.
   (E)   No temporary housing shall be used without the written permission of
the Health Officer.
§ 12-609 VERMIN.
   The owner and occupant are responsible for extermination of any insects,
rodents or other pests.
§ 12-610 WATER.
   Every dwelling shall have supplied water heating and storage facilities
which are properly installed, maintained in safe and good working condition,
and properly connected to furnish hot water to every sink, lavatory, bathtub or
shower required therein.
   (A)   Water heating facilities shall be capable of delivering at every
required outlet at a temperature of not less than 120°F.
   (B)   Hot water storage facilities shall be provided and shall be able to
store amounts at least equal to or greater than the amounts given in the
following schedule:
      (1)   Minimum per dwelling unit: 20 gallons; and
      (2)   Minimum per occupant: four gallons.
§ 12-611 CARE OF PREMISES.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for the owner or occupant of a residential
building, structure or property to utilize the premises of such residential
property for the open storage of any derelict motor vehicle, icebox,
refrigerator, stove, glass, building material, building rubbish and similar
items.
   (B)   It shall be the duty and responsibility of every such owner or
occupant to keep the premises of such residential property clean and to remove
from the premises all such items as listed above, including, but not limited
to, weeds, dead trees, trash, garbage and the like upon notice from the Housing
Official.
§ 12-612 CERTIFICATE OF OCCUPANCY, WHEN REQUIRED.
   (A)   A certificate of occupancy is required of all residential buildings or
structures when such buildings or structures:
      (1)   Are newly constructed;
      (2)   Are structurally altered;
      (3)   Are enlarged through addition; and
      (4)   Are substantially repaired or remodeled.
   (B)   Inspections shall be made by the City Building Inspector or any
official designated by the City Council. Inspections shall seek to ascertain
compliance with this article and the building code. Upon approval, a
certificate will be issued by the City Clerk.
§ 12-613 MOBILE HOMES/TRAVEL TRAILERS MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   Except as hereinafter provided, every mobile home shall meet the
provisions of this article and comply with all zoning laws.
   (B)   The provisions of this article, pertaining to floor area, flush
toilet, bath or shower, and ceiling height shall not apply to travel trailers.
   (C)   Every mobile home shall contain the following minimum gross floor area
of habitable space:
      (1)   One hundred fifty square feet for one or two occupants;
      (2)   One hundred additional square feet for three occupants; and
      (3)   Seventy-five square feet additional for each additional occupant
thereafter.
   (D)   Habitable space in a mobile home shall have a minimum ceiling height
of seven feet over 50% of the floor area; and the floor area where the ceiling
height is less than five feet shall not be considered in computing minimum
gross floor area.
   (E)   A mobile home shall have a safe and unobstructed primary exit and an
emergency exit located remote from the primary exit.
   (F)   Rooms occupied for sleeping purposes must contain at least 60 square
feet of floor space, if used by more than one person, and at least 40 square
feet, if used by one person.
   (G)   Dependent mobile homes shall not be required to have a flush toilet or
a bath or shower.
ARTICLE 7. NOISE CONTROL
§ 12-701 DECLARATION OF POLICY.
   (A)   The making and creation of excessive, unnecessary or unusually loud
noises within the limits of the city, is a condition which has existed for some
time and the extent and magnitude of such noises is increasing.
   (B)   The making, creation or maintenance of such excessive, unnecessary or
unusually loud noises which are prolonged, unusual or unreasonable in their
time, place and use affect and are a detriment to public health, comfort,
convenience, safety and welfare of the residents of the city.
   (C)   The necessity in the public interest for the provisions and
prohibitions hereinafter contained and enacted is declared as a matter of
public policy, and the provisions and prohibitions hereinafter contained and
enacted are in pursuance of and for the purpose of securing and promoting the
public health, comfort, convenience, safety, welfare and the peace and quiet of
the inhabitants of the city.
§ 12-702 DEFINITIONS AND STANDARDS.
   Terminology used in this article may be found in this article and, if not
defined therein, shall conform with applicable “American Standards National
Institute Publication.”
§ 12-703 USE DISTRICT NOISE LEVELS.
   (A)   Maximum permissible sound levels.
      (1)   It shall be a violation of this article for any person to operate
or permit to be operated any stationary source or sound which either:
         (a)   Creates a sound level greater than 15 dBA above the ambient
sound level (L90) within any land use district during any measurement period;
or
         (b)   Creates a ninetieth percentile sound level (L90), a tenth
percentile sound level (L10) or a first percentile sound level (L1) for any
measurement period which exceeds the limits set forth for the following
receiving land use districts when measured at the boundary or at any point
within the property affected by the noise.
 
            L90                 L10                     L1
