ARTICLE 1. WATER SERVICE
§ 19-101 READING OF METERS.
   It shall be the duty of the Water Superintendent to read or cause to be read
all water meters connected to the municipal properties, once in each calendar
month, the same being done on or before the twentieth day of each month. He or
she shall make a record of such readings for each and every meter and report
the same to the Utilities Clerk, showing in each case the amount of water
currently consumed during the month as recorded by such meters.
§ 19-102 DISCONNECTIONS.
   It shall be the duty of the Water Superintendent to disconnect any premises
connected to the water system upon notice from the Utilities Clerk and to keep
the same disconnected until ordered by such Utilities Clerk to reconnect the
same.
§ 19-103 PREPARE MAP.
   The Water Superintendent of the city shall prepare a map of the city on
which shall be exhibited the location of all main and lateral line pipes,
junctions, tap positions, manholes, main valves and the size and condition of
each.
§ 19-104 METER RECORD.
   The Water Superintendent shall keep a record of all meters by number,
showing the capacity, location, person in possession and any repairs made on
the same.
§ 19-105 CUSTODIAN.
   The Water Superintendent shall be the lawful custodian of all properties
belonging to the municipal water system and shall preserve the same in good
condition and prevent its use for any other purpose. It shall be his or her
duty to keep all machinery and plant equipment clean and in good operation.
§ 19-106 METERS; CITY TO SUPPLY; DUAL CONNECTIONS.
   (A)   All water meters shall be owned and provided by the city. No person
shall obtain any water from the city water system except when the same shall
pass through a properly installed and approved meter, and water thereby
obtained shall not thereafter be resold to regular consumers.
   (B)   Dual connections consisting of more than one household or business, or
other establishment per meter, shall not be permitted. Consumers shall be
billed for any and all damage to meters or fittings not caused by the city, the
City Public Works Authority, its agents or employees.
§ 19-107 METERS; LOCATION.
   Water meters shall be placed as near as possible and convenient to the curb
or property line of the property served thereby. Residence property meters may
be placed between the curb and the sidewalk or between the sidewalk and the
property line. Meters serving stores or business property shall be placed under
the floor or stairway, or in some place approved by the Water Superintendent.
All locations shall be approved by the Superintendent.
§ 19-108 FREEZING.
   Every water meter shall be protected at all times from freezing or other
injury. In case an injury shall occur, the Water Department will make the
necessary repairs at its own cost except in cases of neglect by the owner or
occupant, in which cases the city will make the repair at the cost of the owner
or occupant of the premises served. A failure to keep the water box covered
shall not be the neglect of the city but of the user, and freezing due to same
shall be at the cost of the user.
§ 19-109 YARD HYDRANTS.
   No yard hydrant shall be placed nearer than ten feet to any water meter and
in no case shall a yard hydrant be so placed that the drainage therefrom will
run toward or into the meter pit.
§ 19-110 TAMPERING WITH CURB BOXES.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to tamper with any curb box or any of
the contents within the same, or to throw, leave or deposit any matter, dirt or
material of any kind in the same.
§ 19-111 TAMPERING WITH METERS.
   (A)   It is unlawful for any person, other than a duly authorized officer of
the city, to alter, change, bridge over or around, disconnect, injure or damage
in any manner or otherwise to interfere with any water meter or connection to
the same which is installed for use in connection with the city waterworks
system. Provided, that licensed plumbers shall have the right to temporarily
turn off the water when the same is necessary to make repairs on the plumbing
attached to the same. No plumber shall leave any meter turned off except in
cases of such repairs and only for the time necessary to make the repairs.
   (B)   In the event any customer causes or suffers to be caused any tampering
or interfering with the meters, pipes and fittings of the system, the authority
may immediately disconnect the customer’s connection to the system and may
require reasonable security prior to reconnection.
§ 19-112 THEFT OF WATER.
   (A)   Any person who, by fraud or stealth, in any way obtains water from the
municipal waterworks system of the city, or who turns on the water service
without authority of ordinance or duly authorized official, shall be guilty of
an offense and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punished by a fine not
exceeding $100, plus the cost. Each day of such violation shall be a separate
offense. The amount of water that has been obtained by any person by fraud or
stealth or without permission from a proper city official, as provided by
ordinance, shall be estimated by the amount used by such person during the last
month previous that the meter operated and registered correctly all water; and
such person shall pay for the same at the rate fixed by the city for the
particular class of service obtained, before any further water connection is
made.
   (B)   In all cases of fraud or stealth, the city shall have the right to
install apparatus, locks and instruments which are necessary to prevent theft
at the expense of the consumer and shall maintain the same so long as deemed
necessary by the city, not exceeding one year from such installation.
§ 19-113 FAILURE OF WATER SUPPLY.
   In case water is limited, whether from natural causes or accidents of any
kind, the city shall not be liable for any damage of any kind for such reason
of failure. In all cases where the size of the service pipe and the amount of
water used is such that the main pressure in the immediate vicinity is
perceptibly affected, it shall be the duty of such person to install a storage
tank of sufficient capacity to enable them to operate entirely without water
direct from the mains. In such cases, it shall be the duty of such persons to
keep a storage of water on hand to meet the demands of such business without
reducing the water pressure in the immediate vicinity. The City Council
reserves the right and power, in cases of emergency, to govern and regulate the
use of water to all consumers, by resolution or proclamation, as it deems
proper for the public health and safety.
§ 19-114 MANDATORY CONNECTIONS; TAPPING FEE.
   (A)   Connection to water supply required. All houses, buildings or
properties used for human occupancy, employment, recreation or other purposes
situated within the city, except as excluded hereinbelow, shall connect with
the water supply of the city, and the owner of such property shall continue
that water supply to the farthest property line from the point where the supply
first reaches his or her property, at his or her expense. Private wells shall
be permitted for irrigation purposes only.
   (B)   Cost for connection.
      (1)   The cost for connection to the city water supply shall be
determined as follows.
         (a)   If an existing water main abuts the property of a parcel one
acre or more, the owner shall pay to the city an amount equal to the number of
acres in his or her development multiplied by the prevailing cost per mile of
installation of water mains (as determined by the City Clerk) divided by 640.
         (b)   If the city water main does not abut the property, the owner
shall extend the water main to his or her property and shall not be charged for
the connection. In such event, the city shall return to the owner any amounts
paid for subsequent connections to the line so installed for a period of 15
years or until the owner has been paid 80% of the cost of the installation of
the line from city supply to his or her nearest property line, whichever shall
sooner occur. In no event shall the cost of a six-inch, four-inch, two-inch or
smaller pipe be allowed for reimbursement by the city to the owner/developer.
         (c)   All construction must conform to specifications approved by the
City Council and on file in the office of the City Clerk. Fire hydrants shall
also be installed by the developer in accordance with minimum requirement of
the National Board of Fire Underwriters.
      (2)   The total cost to the city of all repair and maintenance to said
distribution system for a period of three years from date of approval and
acceptance of distribution by the city shall be deducted from those amounts
determined in accordance with this section.
   (C)   Extensions and connections by city. The city shall have the right to
make any connections or cross-connections deemed necessary by city between the
water pipelines of the owner constructed pursuant to this agreement and any
other existing or future water line which may be constructed, without the
payment of any sum to the owner; provided, however, that said right shall be
restricted to water pipe lines owned or operated by the city. It is further
understood and agreed that the city shall have the right to make any extension
of the owner’s system deemed necessary by the city without the payment of any
sum to the owner when such extension is constructed by the city with public
funds.
   (D)   Connections or extensions by others. The city shall have the right and
privilege to permit the connection of other water pipe lines to be constructed
by others than the city to the water pipe lines constructed pursuant to this
agreement upon the following terms and conditions.
      (1)   In the event such connection is made to the water pipe line of the
owner, the city will require any such applicant so desiring to connect to the
owner’s system to pay to the city for the use and benefit of the owner in
accordance with the following schedule for each and every connection of any
line having a diameter of eight inches and larger:
         (a)   Twelve-inch diameter and larger: $2,000;
         (b)   Ten-inch diameter: $1,750; and
         (c)   Eight-inch diameter: $1,500.
      (2)   It is further understood and agreed that the charges provided for
in division (D)(1) above shall not be required if such applicant constructs
such extension at the applicant’s sole expense and, upon completion thereof,
conveys by appropriate instruments all of the applicant’s right, title and
interest in and to all the water pipe lines in the system so constructed, in
which event said system so constructed by such applicant shall become part of
the owner’s system.
      (3)   Any and all sums collected by the city under the terms of this
section shall be placed by the city in a special trust account and shall be
paid to the owner within 30 days after the completion and acceptance by the
city of the water system for which such payments have been received.
      (4)   The city shall have the right to permit the connection of water
pipe lines constructed by others without charge when such connections shall be
to pipe lines of the owner having a diameter less than ten inches.
      (5)   The city shall not be liable for fees.
   (E)   Final plan. Within a period of 30 days after the completion of the
construction of said distribution system, the owner shall furnish, in
triplicate, a plan (exhibit C), showing the correct location, sizes and length
of all lines, hydrants, valves and other accessories thereof, said plan being
drawn to scale by a competent draftsman; and after approval by the City Council
and acceptance by the city, one copy shall be returned to the owner, one copy
shall be filed in the City Clerk’s office and one copy shall be attached to and
form a part of the agreement.
   (F)   Costs. Within 30 days after the completion of the construction, the
owner shall furnish to the city, in triplicate, a certified, itemized statement
of cost of the distribution system herein described, and as shown on the plan
per division (C) above; said statement to be in form specified by the city, and
shall show separately itemized costs for each size water pipe line and
appurtenances. The total cost of said installation shall include cost of
materials, excavations, backfill and all other work incident thereto, including
engineering fees of not to exceed 5%; but said statement shall not include
attorneys’ fees, charges for installing water service connections and meters
thereof, or any other charge not hereinabove mentioned. Said itemized statement
shall be approved by City Council.
   (G)   Exception to connection requirement. The provisions of divisions (A)
and (B) above shall not apply to:
      (1)   A single-family residence constructed after April 7, 1981, unless a
water main is located within 100 feet of the property line along a street,
alley or right-of-way, in which case the owner shall connect to the public
water supply;
      (2)   Any structures existing as of April 7, 1981; and
      (3)   A residence constructed in a previously platted subdivision which
provided for private water wells in lieu of public water supply for the
subdivision as of April 7, 1981.
§ 19-115 METER DEPOSIT.
   Each and every person receiving water from the city waterworks shall deposit
and maintain a service deposit with the Utilities Clerk which shall remain with
the city to the credit of the depositor so long as service is continued at such
connection and shall be the subject to any charge for water service which is
unpaid or for repairs done by the city to such person’s water service. In all
cases where a charge is made against such deposit, it shall be the duty of the
person to pay the Utilities Clerk an amount equal to the charge and thereby
maintain the deposit equal to the required amount at all times until service is
discontinued. The deposit shall be returned to such depositor upon
discontinuance of service after all water rents and other service charges are
first paid. The amount of the deposit shall be as set forth in §
19-401 and as may be subsequently changed by motion or resolution by the City
Council.
§ 19-116 SERVICE LIABILITY.
   Each and every person using water from the city water system shall be liable
to the city for all water used according to the established rates and minimum
charges and according to the rates promulgated by the City Council.
§ 19-117 DELINQUENT WATER BILLS.
   (A)   All bills for utility services shall be rendered to consumers in
accordance with the established policy on file in the office of the City
Utilities Clerk, a copy of which is incorporated herein by reference, or in
accordance with any other applicable policies or ordinances of the city. The
amount billed shall be due and payable by the consumer upon receipt of the
statement and in accordance with the due dates, late dates, penalties and late
charges established in existing policies and ordinances.
   (B)   (1)   It is the policy of the city to discontinue utility service to
customers by reason of nonpayment of bills only after notice and a meaningful
opportunity to be heard on disputed bills. The city's form for application for
utility service and all bills shall contain, in addition to the title, address,
room number, and telephone number of the official in charge of billing, clearly
visible and easily readable provisions to the effect:
         (a)   That all bills are due and payable on or before the date set
forth on the bill;
         (b)   That if any bill is not paid by or before that date, a second
bill will be mailed containing a cutoff notice that if the bill is not paid
within ten days of the mailing of the second bill, service will be discontinued
for nonpayment; and
         (c)   That any customer disputing the correctness of his or her bill
shall have a right to a hearing at which time he or she may be represented in
person and by counsel or any other person of his or her choosing and may
present orally or in writing his or her complaint and contentions to the city
official in charge of utility billing. This official shall be authorized to
order that the customer's service not be discontinued and shall have the
authority to make a final determination of the customer's complaint.
      (2)   Requests for delays or waiver of payment will not be entertained;
only questions of proper and correct billing will be considered. In the absence
of payment of the bill rendered or resort to the hearing procedure provided
herein, service will be discontinued at the time specified, but in no event
until the charges have been due and unpaid for at least 30 days.
      (3)   When it becomes necessary for the city to discontinue utility
service to a customer for nonpayment of bills, service will be reinstated only
after all bills for service then due have been paid, along with a turn-on
charge in the sum of $20.
§ 19-118 WATER RATES.
   (A)   Each customer shall pay for water service on a monthly basis according
to the following rates.
 
First 1,000 gallons           $8    (minimum charge)
All usage after 1,000 gallons $2.70 per 1,000 gallons
 
   (B)   The water rates may be increased or decreased by motion or resolution
of the City Council.
(Ord. 2003-06A, passed 11-4-2003)
§ 19-119 REREADING METERS.
   In the event a consumer requests that a water meter be reread, and in the
event the meter reading is correct, a $10 charge for rereading shall be
assessed and added to the next month’s utility bill. In the event the rereading
reveals that the utility billing is in error, an adjustment shall be made as
appropriate and no charge shall be assessed for the rereading of the meter.
§ 19-120 WATER BILL ADJUSTMENT.
   In the event that a customer requests an adjustment of his or her water bill
because a leak or some other factor has caused the bill to be unusually high,
the City Manager, in his or her discretion, shall have the authority to adjust
the water bill by splitting the difference between the amount of the
extraordinary bill and the amount of the customer’s average bill; provided,
however, that this authority shall not be exercised more than once each year
for any one customer.
ARTICLE 2. ELECTRIC SERVICE
§ 19-201 SCOPE OF RULES, REGULATIONS; AUTHORITY TO AMEND.
   Until otherwise provided by ordinance, all electric current or energy
furnished by the city shall be furnished by it at the rates and upon the terms
herein prescribed and established and any valid rules and regulations
heretofore prescribed by it. The city hereby reserves the right to amend or
repeal this article or any other rule or regulation for the furnishing by it of
electric current or energy.
§ 19-202 RATES.
   (A)   Rates.
      (1)   The following electric utility rate charge increases are approved
for implementation as of the effective date specified within the table set
forth immediately below:
Commercial Service  Effective Date
Commercial Service                                       Effective Date
   Minimum monthly charge                 $20.71      6-1-2024
   Energy charge                          $0.1437/kwh 6-1-2024
   Energy charge                          $0.1520/kwh 11-1-2024
Large Commercial Service
   Minimum monthly charge                 $869        6-1-2024
   Energy charge - over 10,000 kwh per mon$0.9020/kwh 6-1-2024
Residential Service
   Minimum monthly charge                 $10.36      6-1-2024
   Energy charge                          $0.1388/kwh 6-1-2024
   Energy charge                          $0.1469/kwh 11-1-1-2024
 
      (2)   The following fuel cost adjustment formula shall be implemented
effective June 1, 2024: Total OMPA Invoice + Total SWPA Invoice/Total kWh -
0.06 = Fuel cost adjustment per kWh.
      (3)   The fees established herein may be reviewed and changed by motion
or resolution of the Board of Trustees of the Lexington Public Works Authority
at least annually or more often as it deems appropriate.
   (B)   Definition. For the purpose of this section, the following definition
shall apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different
meaning.
      LARGE COMMERCIAL SERVICE. Nonresidential use over 10,000 kWh per month.
   (C)   Additional provisions.
      (1)   A variable fuel adjustment will be added to all of the above
charges for each kind of service.
      (2)   The electric rates may be increased or decreased by motion or
resolution of the City Council.
(Ord. 2003-06A, passed 11-4-2003; Res. 24-020, passed 5-7-2024)
§ 19-203 CHARGES TO BUILDING CONTRACTORS.
   (A)   The following rates and charges (for the furnishing of electric
current or energy) shall be charged by the city to building contractors or
others requesting the service herein specified, in addition to other charges
that may be levied:
      (1)   If the building contractor or other person furnishes his or her own
pole, and sets the same in place at their own expense, the following fees shall
be owing by the contractor to the city:
         (a)   For installing the drop wire to one pole and meter: $50; and
         (b)   For each additional span of wire required between multiple
poles: $10.
      (2)   If the city shall furnish and install a pole or poles on the
building site and also install the drop wire and meters, or shall remove the
same, then the city shall receive the following fee:
         (a)   One pole: $75;
         (b)   Two poles: $125;
         (c)   Three poles: $150; and
         (d)   Each pole beyond three: $20.
   (B)   The fees set forth in division (A)(2) above shall be for the
installation of poles, drop wire and meters only and shall not be deemed as a
purchase price for poles set.
   (C)   (1)   The fees set forth in division (A)(2) above apply to poles that
are required to provide service to the site and do not apply if service will
remain after construction has been completed.
      (2)   If service will remain after construction, the fees set forth in
division (A)(2) above will apply.
§ 19-204 READING METERS.
   The Light and Power Superintendent shall cause all electric meters on the
city electric system to be read on or before the fifteenth day of each calendar
month and a record of the same to be made and reported to the City Utilities
Clerk.
§ 19-205 DISCONNECTIONS.
   It shall be the duty of the Light and Power Superintendent to disconnect any
premises connected to the city electric system upon notice to do so from the
Utilities Clerk and to keep the same disconnected until ordered by said
Utilities Clerk to reconnect the same.
§ 19-206 METER RECORD.
   The Light and Power Superintendent shall keep a record of all electric
meters by number showing capacity, location, person in possession and any
repairs made on the same.
§ 19-207 CUSTODIAN.
   The Light and Power Superintendent shall be the lawful custodian of all
properties belonging to the city electric system and shall preserve the same in
good condition and prevent its use for any other purposes. He or she shall keep
the system clean and in good operation.
§ 19-208 METERS; CITY TO SUPPLY.
   (A)   The city will supply all electric meters and keep the same in a good
state of use; provided, that the user shall be liable for all damage and costs
of making repairs arising from his or her neglect or wrongful use.
   (B)   No person shall obtain any electricity from the city except when the
same shall pass through a properly installed and approved meter, and no
electricity shall thereafter be resold to any regular consumer.
§ 19-209 TAMPERING.
   It is unlawful for any person to tamper with, remove or change any meter
installed for electric service or any of its working parts or any wires
connected therewith, or to connect any other wires thereto, or to bridge over
or around or to establish or maintain any loop or conductor of electric current
around any duly installed electric meter.
§ 19-210 THEFT OF ELECTRICITY.
   (A)   It is unlawful for any person to use any electric current or power
from the city electric system which has been obtained by fraud or theft. Theft
shall consist of taking or using any electric current from the city light and
power system without the knowledge or consent of the City Council or in any
manner contrary to the provisions of the city ordinances.
   (B)   In all cases of theft of electric current, the amount so taken shall
be determined in the same manner as set for theft of water, and the premises
shall be disconnected until the charges therefor are paid in full.
   (C)   In prevention of such cases, the city shall have the right to install
such equipment for the prevention of theft at the expense of the owner as in
its judgment may be necessary, and to require the same to remain installed for
a period of not longer than one year.
§ 19-211 FAILURE OF SERVICE.
   (A)   The city undertakes to render an efficient and adequate electric power
and light service for the inhabitants of the city, but shall not be responsible
for any damages arising from inadequate supply of power for unexpected needs
and beyond its potential capacity or ability to serve.
   (B)   All service is contingent upon the exercise of skill, good faith and
the means at hand.
§ 19-212 DELINQUENT BILLS.
   (A)   All bills for electric service shall be based on meter readings made
by the Light and Power Superintendent on the same conditions and at the same
time as in the case of water meters, to which shall be applied the fixed rates
of service as established by the City Council.
   (B)   (1)   All such bills shall become due and be paid within the period of
time allowed for water bills.
      (2)   If not so paid, they shall become delinquent as in the case of
water bills, and all such delinquent electric bills shall be collected and
service disconnected and reconnected upon the same terms within the same
periods of time allowed for water bills and with the same reconnection charges.
§ 19-213 UTILITIES CLERK TO COLLECT.
   The City Utilities Clerk shall collect all electric light and power bills
and give receipt for same showing consumption, person paying the same and date
of payment. All bills shall be on meter readings by the Light and Power
Superintendent, to which shall be applied the rates as prescribed by ordinance,
resolution or motion.
§ 19-214 METER DEPOSITS.
   (A)   Each and every person receiving electricity from the city electrical
system shall deposit and maintain an electricity service deposit with the
Utilities Clerk which shall remain with the city to the credit of the depositor
so long as service is continued at such connection and shall be subject to any
charge for electric service which is unpaid or for repairs done by the city to
such person’s electric service.
   (B)   In all cases where a charge is made against such deposit, it shall be
the duty of the person to pay the Utilities Clerk an amount equal to the charge
and thereby maintain the deposit equal to the required amount at all times
until such service is discontinued. The deposit shall be returned to such
depositor upon discontinuance of service after all electrical rents and other
service charges are first paid. The meter deposit shall be as set forth in §
19-401 of this chapter and shall be subject to change hereafter by the City
Council by motion or resolution.
§ 19-215 METERING REQUIRED.
   Each dwelling, multi-family dwelling, business or multi-business must have a
separate service for each occupancy mounted on the outside of the building
accessible by the city meter reader, and each meter will have a separate
deposit paid by either the landlord or tenant as deemed necessary in §
19-214.
§ 19-216 INJURY OR DAMAGE.
   It is unlawful for any person to injure or damage, in any manner, any of the
poles, wires or electric installations of the municipal electric light and
power plant or any of its streets or alley line construction, or to throw
objects at the insulators, wires or other appurtenances with intent to injure
the same.
§ 19-217 COLLECTION OF CHARGES.
   The City Manager and the City Clerk-Treasurer are conjointly and directly
responsible for collections and payment charges for electric energy and water.
§ 19-218 LATE CHARGES.
   Any consumer who does not pay his or her electric bill on or before the
tenth day of each month shall be charged a 10% penalty.
§ 19-219 ELECTRICAL BOARD.
   (A)   Members. The Electrical Board shall consist of three members, the
Electrical Inspector, one master electrician and one resident of the city. The
master and the resident will be appointed and approved by the City Council.
   (B)   Duties. The Electrical Board shall:
      (1)   Periodically review and recommend modifications in the application
and administration of all electrical ordinances;
      (2)   Prepare and conduct the local examinations for those applicants
desiring electrical licenses and grade those examinations;
      (3)   Assist the City Clerk in the official duties of licensing;
      (4)   The Electrical Board shall neither collect nor disburse any
examination or licensing monies; and
      (5)   The Electrical Board shall meet the third Tuesday of each month at
7:00 p.m., and, at this time, all electrical applications shall be reviewed and
examinations given and graded the same night.
ARTICLE 3. SEWER SERVICE
§ 19-301 CITY TO MAINTAIN SEWER CONNECTIONS.
   The city shall inspect and maintain all connections to its sewer lines upon
the payment to the city by the user or beneficiary thereof of the charge or
charges prescribed by the city.
§ 19-302 MANDATORY SEWER CONNECTIONS.
   (A)   The owners of all houses, buildings or property used for human
occupancy, employment, recreation or other purposes situated within the city
and abutting on any street, alley or right-of-way in which there is located a
public sanitary sewer of the city are hereby required, at their expense, to
install suitable toilet facilities therein, and to have such facilities
connected directly with the proper public sewer within 60 days after the date
of official notice to do so; provided, that such public sewer is within 150
feet of the property line.
   (B)   Such notice (see division (A) above) shall be served by any member of
the City Police Department by delivering a true and correct copy to the
property owner or leaving the same at his or her usual place of residence with
a member of his or her family over the age of 15 years; or, if such owner
cannot be found, by posting a copy of such notice at the front entrance of the
building involved.
   (C)   Any person who shall fail, neglect or refuse to comply with the terms
of this section after having been notified so to do as provided herein shall be
guilty of an offense, and each 24-hour period thereafter shall constitute a
separate offense. In the event of a continuous violation of this section by any
property owner, the city shall discontinue the furnishing of water to such
property owner until such time as a proper sewer connection has been made.
   (D)   No person shall discharge or cause to be discharged into the municipal
sanitary sewer system any cistern water, groundwater, roof runoff, foundation
drainage or other subsurface drainage.
§ 19-303 PRIVATE SEWAGE DISPOSAL FACILITIES.
   (A)   Except as herein provided in this section, it shall be unlawful for
any person to construct or maintain any privy, privy vault, septic tank,
cesspool or other facility intended to be used for the disposal of sewage
within the limits of the city.
   (B)   Where a connection to a public sanitary sewer line is not required
under the provisions of §
19-302 of this article, a private septic tank or cesspool facility for sewage
disposal may be constructed and maintained, provided it is constructed and
maintained under the rules and regulations of the city Health Officer or other
duly appointed city agency or employee and in compliance with the
recommendations and requirements of the State Department of Health. No septic
tank or cesspool shall be permitted to discharge to any public sewer or natural
outlet.
   (C)   The owner of private septic tanks or cesspools shall operate and
maintain the same in a sanitary manner at all times, at no expense to the city,
and no statement contained in this article shall be construed to interfere with
any additional requirements that may be imposed by the Health Officer of the
city, county or state.
   (D)   At such times as a public sewer becomes available to a property served
by a septic tank or cesspool, a direct connection shall be made to such public
sewer in compliance with §
19-302 of this article, and the septic tank or cesspool shall immediately be
abandoned and filled with suitable material.
§ 19-304 CONNECTION AND TAP FEES AND SEWER SERVICE FEE.
   (A)   For each sewer tap made in the city, there shall be paid to the city a
fee of $25, and said tap shall be made and inspected by a city employee or
employees.
   (B)   For each dwelling, trailer house, business or other establishment of
any kind connected to the city sewer system, there shall be assessed a sewer
service fee in the amount of $7 and $1.60 per 1,000 gallons for all usage. The
sewer service charge shall be collected by and paid to the Utilities Clerk of
the city, and the collection procedure shall be the same as for electric or
water service. Service may be discontinued for failure to pay said sewer
service charge, even though charges for electric energy or water have been paid
and are not in arrears in respect to the premises for which the sewer service
charge is delinquent.
   (C)   The sewer tap fee and sewer service charge set forth in divisions (A)
and (B) above may be increased or decreased by motion or resolution of the City
Council.
(Ord. 2003-06A, passed 11-4-2003)
§ 19-305 CERTAIN SUBSTANCES PROHIBITED; DUTIES OF SEWER INSPECTOR; PERMITS FOR
SEWER CONNECTIONS FOR INDUSTRIAL WASTES; NOTICE TO OWNERS IN EVENT OF
NONCOMPLIANCE.
   (A)   No person shall discharge or cause to be discharged the following
substances if it appears likely, in the opinion of the Sewer Inspector, that
such wastes can harm the sewers, the sewage treatment process or equipment;
have an adverse effect on the receiving stream; or can otherwise endanger life,
limb or public property, or otherwise constitute a nuisance. The prohibited
substances are:
      (1)   Flammable or explosive materials;
      (2)   Water or waste containing fats, wax, grease or oils in excess of
one hundred milligrams per liter (100 mg/l) or containing any substance which
may solidify or become viscous at temperatures higher than 32°F;
      (3)   Any liquid or vapor having a temperature higher than 150°F;
      (4)   Any garbage or food waste not properly shredded. The installation
and operation of any grinder or shredder equipped with a motor of three-fourths
horsepower or greater shall be subject to review and approval by the Sewer
Inspector;
      (5)   Any waters or wastes containing the metals listed below or other
toxic substances in quantities determined by the Sewer Inspector to be harmful:
         (a)   Antimony;
         (b)   Arsenic;
         (c)   Barium;
         (d)   Beryllium;
         (e)   Bismuth;
         (f)   Boron;
         (g)   Cadmium;
         (h)   Chromium;
         (i)   Cobalt;
         (j)   Copper;
         (k)   Iron;
         (l)   Lead;
         (m)   Manganese;
         (n)   Mercury;
         (o)   Molybdenum;
         (p)   Nickel;
         (q)   Rhenium;
         (r)   Selenium;
         (s)   Silver;
         (t)   Strontium;
         (u)   Tellurium;
         (v)   Tin;
         (w)   Uranium; and
         (x)   Zinc.
      (6)   Any water or waste containing iron pickling wastes or plating
solutions;
      (7)   Any waters or wastes containing phenols or other taste- or odor-
producing substances;
      (8)   Any radioactive wastes of a half-life or concentration determined
by the Sewer Inspector to be harmful;
      (9)   Any water or wastes having pH lower than 5.5 or having any
corrosive property capable of damaging installations, equipment or personnel of
the sewage works;
      (10)   Solid or viscous substances of such size or in such quantities
capable of causing obstruction of sewers or interference with operation of
sewage works, such as ashes, cinders, mud, straw, shavings, metal, glass, rags,
feathers, tar, plastics, wood, unground garbage, whole blood, paunch manure,
hair, fleshings, entrails and paper containers;
      (11)   Wastes containing unusual concentrations of suspended solids, such
as fuller’s earth, lime or clay;
      (12)   Wastes containing unusual concentrations of dissolved substances,
such as sodium chloride or sodium sulfate;
      (13)   Water or wastes containing excessive coloration, such as that
caused by dye wastes and tanning solutions;
      (14)   Wastes containing unusual concentrations of organic material, such
as whey, milk, yeast, blood or unusual biochemical oxygen demand (BOD),
chemical oxygen demand (COD) or chlorine requirement, constituting a
significant load on the sewage treatment facilities; and
      (15)   Materials which cause unusual volume of flow or concentration of
wastes constituting slugs which adversely affect the sewage treatment process.
   (B)   If any waters or wastes are discharged or proposed to be discharged
which contain the substances described in division (A) above, the Sewer
Inspector may prohibit their discharge; require the responsible party to
pretreat the waste before discharge; limit the quantity, rates and time of
discharge; require the installation of a control manhole for observation,
sampling and metering of the wastes; and assess a surcharge based on the
quantity and strength of the wastes. If pretreatment is to be accomplished, the
design, installation and operation of the plant and equipment shall be subject
to the review and approval of the Sewer Inspector.
   (C)   Application for permits for sewer connections for industrial wastes
shall show the following information:
      (1)   A plat of the property showing all existing sewers and storm
drains;
      (2)   Plans and specifications covering any work proposed to be done
under the permit;
      (3)   A schedule of all process waters and industrial wastes produced or
to be produced, a description of the character of each waste, the daily volumes
and maximum rates of discharge and representative analyses; and
      (4)   The name of the firm or person who will perform the work covered by
the application.
   (D)   The Sewer Inspector shall cause to be served on the owner or occupant
of any establishment having sewer connections which do not conform to the
provisions hereof at the effective date hereof a notice in writing advising
that 30 days from the day of service of the notice, if the proper measures have
not been taken, enforcement action may be initiated as set forth elsewhere in
this chapter.
   (E)   The Sewer Inspector shall cause samples of wastes from industrial
establishments to be obtained and tested periodically to determine the quantity
and composition thereof.
§ 19-306 PRIVATE SEWER LINE CONNECTIONS; LIMITING LIABILITY.
   (A)   Private sewer line connections.
      (1)   All private service lines connected to the city public sewer system
from and after the date of this section shall include a pop-off device or other
city approved backflow prevention device connected to the sanitary sewer
cleanout to protect against backflow.
      (2)   Said device shall be of sufficient size and quality to prevent
backflow to individual residences or businesses.
      (3)   All installed pop-off devices and other city approved backflow
prevention devices shall be registered with the city and properly maintained
and secured by said property owner.
      (4)   For those service lines already connected to the city’s public
sewer system, the city shall provide a sewer inspection fee and waiver in the
form attached to the ordinance codified herein to allow those who are already
connected to the city’s public sewer system an opportunity to install a pop-off
device or other approved backflow prevention device.
   (B)   Limiting liability. Failure to meet the conditions of this section
effectively limits the city’s liability in the event of a sanitary sewer backup
to the cost of the pop-off or other backflow device.
(Ord. 2014-03, passed 8-5-2014)
ARTICLE 4. DEPOSITS
§ 19-401 DEPOSIT REQUIRED; AMOUNT.
   (A)   Any customer desiring utility service shall make application to the
City Utilities Clerk on forms provided for that purpose. The application shall
state the name of the customer, including spouse, the premises to be served,
the size of piping and such other information as may be required by the Water
or Electrical Superintendent. The application shall be accompanied by a deposit
in the following amounts:
      (1)   Commercial property: one and one-half times the average bill for
the previous six months;
      (2)   Rental property with electric service: $200 ($100 if letter of good
credit from previous utility);
      (3)   Rental property or owner occupied without electric service: $60;
and
      (4)   Owner occupied: $50.
   (B)   (1)   The amount of deposit required shall hereafter be regulated by
the City Council by motion or resolution.
      (2)   Upon payment of all fees required and making of the application,
the city will make the connection as required by the application.
      (3)   Subject to any applicable provision of Article 5 of this chapter,
no connection shall be made or service provided on any premises for any
customer who is in arrears on the payment of any utility bill at any location
within the city.
      (4)   For the purpose of this division (B), CUSTOMER shall include any
partners, a spouse or adult persons, excluding dependent children, living at or
occupying the premises.
ARTICLE 5. UTILITY SERVICE TERMINATION POLICY
§ 19-501 DELINQUENT BILLS.
   (A)   All bills for utility service shall be based on meter readings to
which shall be applied the fixed rates of service as established by the City
Council. All bills shall be due and payable on the first day of each month for
the service rendered in each month after maturity or be considered delinquent.
Those bills paid after the fifteenth and on or before the twenty-third of each
month shall incur a penalty of 10% of the total amount due. Any person
delinquent in payment past the twenty-third of each month shall have service
discontinued.
   (B)   On the sixteenth of each month, the Utility Billing Clerk shall mail
out courtesy notices giving the customer seven days from the date of the notice
to pay the delinquent balance or service will be disconnected. Courtesy notices
shall contain the following:
      (1)   Balance due, including any late charge;
      (2)   Termination date;
      (3)   Customer’s right to have a hearing before the Utility Hearing
Board; and
      (4)   Procedure for requesting a hearing.
(Ord. 2002-03, passed 7-2-2002)
§ 19-502 DISCONNECTION PROCEDURE.
   If no hearing is requested by the customer, the following procedure shall be
used to disconnect service.
   (A)   Hours. Disconnections will be made only during regular business hours
from 8:00 a.m. until 5:00 p.m.
   (B)   Days. Disconnections will be made only Monday through Thursday, except
that no disconnection will be made on the day before a holiday.
   (C)   Cut-off date. The cut-off date shall be on or after the nineteenth day
of each month.
   (D)   Notice of termination. Immediately after, or simultaneously with, the
termination of service, the Light and Power Superintendent shall post a “Notice
Of Termination” at the location where service has been disconnected. The notice
of termination shall contain the following:
      (1)   Notice that service has been terminated;
      (2)   Balance due, including all additional charges; and
      (3)   Procedure for reconnection.
§ 19-503 HEARING PROCEDURE.
   (A)   A hearing prior to disconnection of utility service is required only
if the customer requests a hearing prior to the eighteenth day of the month and
only if the customer pays one-third of the amount due. Once a hearing has been
requested and the money paid, the actual date of the hearing shall be set
within three business days. The hearing shall be conducted by the Utility
Hearing Board. This Board shall consist of the Light and Power Superintendent,
the City Manager, Utility Billing Clerk, City Clerk and one member of the City
Council, any two of whom may conduct the hearing. The Utility Hearing Board
shall have the authority to grant a ten-day extension to pay the remaining two-
thirds of the bill. If the customer has been a long-time resident and has a
good payment history, the Utility Hearing Board may arrange a deferred payment
plan extending the time to pay that month’s bill, up to 90 days from the
original due date. No customer may be eligible for a deferred plan (either ten-
day or 90-day) who is not current on his or her bill prior to the month in
which the deferment is requested. The full amount shall be due immediately in
the event the customer becomes delinquent on a subsequent bill.
   (B)   A written record of the hearing shall be maintained and signed by both
the customer and at least two members of the Utility Hearing Board. A clear
disposition of the dispute should be made at the hearing and the written record
should reflect how the matter was resolved.
   (C)   The Utility Hearing Board shall present to the City Council, at the
next regularly scheduled meeting, a copy of the written record of all hearings
conducted during the preceding month.
   (D)   If adequate payment is not arranged at the time of the hearing, or a
deferred payment plan is not arranged, the utility service shall be
disconnected within three days of the hearing. No additional “Final Notice”
shall be required prior to actual disconnection. If payments pursuant to the
deferred payment plan are not made when due, the utility service shall be
disconnected immediately without further notice.
§ 19-504 RECONNECTION PROCEDURE.
   Once utility service has been disconnected, restoration of service shall not
be had until all accounts are paid in full. Any person whose utility service
has been discontinued for an unpaid utility bill may have the same reconnected
upon the payment of all utility bills due and the further sum of $20 to cover
the costs. In the event the city has applied the customer’s deposit to the
bill, the customer shall be required to make a new deposit as set forth in §
19-401 of this chapter.
§ 19-505 TRANSFER FEE.
   Residents who transfer utility service from one location to another shall
pay a fee to the City Clerk of $20 per transfer to cover the costs of the
transfer.
§ 19-506 LIFE-THREATENING SITUATION COLLECTION POLICY AND PROCEDURES.
   (A)   The City Public Works Authority and the city will suspend collection
activity when a consumer certifies that the consumer or a permanent member of
the household has a medical condition where the discontinuance of electrical
service would be life-threatening.
   (B)   For the purpose of this section, a LIFE-THREATENING CONDITION is
defined as one where the consumer or other permanent resident of the household
is dependent upon electric-operated equipment that is prescribed by a physician
and is needed to sustain the person’s life.
   (C)   Examples of life-sustaining equipment include: kidney dialysis
machine; iron lung; oxygen concentrator and certain other oxygen machines;
cardiac monitor; heating and air conditioning equipment; other equipment that
is prescribed by a licensed medical doctor. If a battery backup is normally
available for the life-sustaining equipment, then the medical condition is not
considered life-threatening. The following equipment is not considered to be
life-sustaining equipment: hot water heater; refrigerator; range/stove;
nebulizer that is battery-driven or hand-driven or self-contained; battery-
driven sleep apnea monitor; battery-driven cardiac monitor.
   (D)   The consumer may initially certify the condition, but further
verification of the condition by a licensed medical or osteopathic doctor is
required within ten days of initial notification. Completion of a form provided
by the City Public Works Authority and a payment plan worked out between a
customer service representative and the consumer will suspend disconnection of
electrical service to a specified residence for a period of 30 days from the
initial notification. Electric service may be suspended immediately if the
physician’s certification is not received within ten days of initial
notification. The 30-day period may be extended by the City Public Works
Authority at the request of the consumer for one additional contiguous 30-day
period, but only if necessitated by the life-threatening condition as indicated
by doctor verification. The request for the additional 30-day extension must be
made before the end of the initial 30-day period. The City Public Works
Authority is not required to furnish service to the consumer beyond a total of
60 days for life-threatening condition without full payment of the account or
acceptable payment arrangements on any unpaid balance.
   (E)   Failure of the consumer to fully comply with this policy may result in
denial of life-threatening status and renewed collection activity by the City
Public Works Authority, including termination of service to the residence.
(Ord. 2010-3, passed 11-2-2010)
ARTICLE 6. PUBLIC WORKS INSPECTORS
§ 19-601 INSPECTORS’ DUTIES.
   Inspectors of the Public Works Department shall have the authority to:
   (A)   Delay construction of any building or structure, or the repair or the
wrecking thereof, if such is being done in a careless or reckless manner, or in
violation of effective codes;
   (B)   Call upon the Police Department in enforcing violations of this
chapter, or for violation committed in the presence of the Inspector;
   (C)   Order the discontinuance of water service to any building, structure
or premises being constructed, used or occupied in violation of this chapter,
and such water service shall remain discontinued until such time as the
violations have been remedied to the satisfaction of the Inspector;
   (D)   Order the discontinuance of electric service where improper or
defective wiring exists or where electrical construction or equipment has been
installed without the proper license or permit;
   (E)   Enter upon or in any building, structure or premises at all reasonable
times so as to inspect all electrical wiring, electrical equipment, plumbing,
air conditioning systems, heating systems or refrigeration systems which are
now or may hereinafter be installed, or to ascertain the sanitary conditions,
damage or structural soundness of that building, structure or premises;
   (F)   Revoke any permit where it is found there has been a misrepresentation
of facts or in violation of any ordinance or any code adopted by the city; and
   (G)   Require an owner or agent who is constructing with reenforced concrete
or structural steel, to supply a non-city inspector satisfactory to the Public
Works Department, such inspector to oversee all work during the construction.
§ 19-602 APPEALS FROM INSPECTOR’S DECISIONS.
   (A)   Any person aggrieved by an inspector exercising his or her power and
authority pursuant to §
19-601 of this chapter must, before instituting suit, appeal to the Public
Works Appeals Board, which shall consist of the Public Works Director, the City
Attorney and a designee of the Mayor.
   (B)   (1)   Any such appeal shall be made within five working days after the
decision of the inspector and shall be in writing, stating the reasons for the
appeal.
      (2)   The date and place of all hearings shall be fixed by the Appeals
Board, and all interested parties shall be given written notice of the hearing.
   (C)   The Appeals Board shall give written decision within ten working days
of the hearing and, if accepted by the appealing party, the Board shall take
necessary steps to give effect thereto.
ARTICLE 7. CABLE TELEVISION
§ 19-701 GRANT OF FRANCHISE.
   The city hereby grants to T.C.I. Cablevision of Oklahoma, Inc., the right,
privilege and authority to provide services, facilities and equipment necessary
to meet the present and future cable related needs of the community.
§ 19-702 EFFECTIVE DATE; TERM.
   The franchise hereby granted shall be effective from and after the effective
date hereof and shall remain in full force and effect for a period of 15 years
unless otherwise terminated as allowed by law.
§ 19-703 AGREEMENT.
   The franchise hereby granted shall be in accordance with the franchise
agreement, §§ I through IX, and attached schedules, a copy of which is on file
with the City Clerk.

§ 19-706 EFFECT OF SUBPART N.
   Said Subpart N, as supplemented herein and as applicable to any cable rate
regulation proceeding before the City Council as a “franchising authority”
under 47 U.S.C. § 543, shall govern such proceeding.
§ 19-707 FURTHER DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this article, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   CABLE OPERATOR. Any “grantee” under this article.
   COMMISSION. The Federal Communications Commission.
   FCC. The Federal Communications Commission.
   FRANCHISING AUTHORITY. The City of Lexington.
§ 19-708 PROCEDURE FOR CONSIDERATION OF VIEWS OF INTERESTED PARTIES; 47 C.F.R.
§ 76.935.
   (A)   Any basic service, equipment or installation rate filing by a cable
operator on the franchising authority under Subpart N shall contain a brief
summary or description for publication purposes, and shall include appropriate
FCC forms and/or worksheets.
   (B)   A cable operator shall make Subpart N filings with the City Clerk.
   (C)   Upon such filing, the City Clerk shall forthwith place on the agenda
for the next regular scheduled meeting of the City Council an agenda item
conforming to the requirements of the Open Meeting Act (25 O.S. §§ 301 et seq.)
for the Council to set a public hearing on said basic service, equipment or
installation rate request.
   (D)   Said hearing shall then be set by Council on a date at least seven,
but not more than 14, days thereafter.
   (E)   Notice of the date, time and place of such hearing, together with a
brief summary or description of the rate request, shall be published by the
City Clerk in a newspaper of general circulation at least five days prior to
said hearing.
   (F)   In the event additional days are taken under 47 C.F.R. § 76.933, said
hearing shall be deemed continued until final regulatory action is taken by the
Council, which shall be in open meeting under the notice and agenda requirement
of the Open Meeting Act (25 O.S. §§ 301 et seq.).
§ 19-709 EFFECT OF AMENDMENTS.
   Any amendments to Subpart N, as adopted by reference in § 19-704 of this
article shall be deemed effective as published by the FCC, including, but not
limited to, effective dates; provided, that said amendments will not be
enforced hereunder absent ratification by the Council; provided further, that
no 47 C.F.R. § 76.943 fines shall be levied thereunder absent adoption by the
Council; and provided further, that no gap in rate regulation authority shall
be implied by or inferred from any failure of the Council to anticipate or
simultaneously adopt revisions as contemplated at 47 U.S.C. § 543(b)(2).
§ 19-710 POLE CHARGE.
   (A)   The City Public Works Authority hereby grants to CATV a franchise for
the right to construct communication lines and necessary drop and electrical
equipment on the city’s power pole communication spacing, moreover, 17,010 feet
to 21.10 feet.
   (B)   The franchise is to maintain proper National Safety Code ethics as
spelled out in the franchise agreement on file with the City Clerk. In
consideration therefor, the franchisee must pay to the city the sum of $4 per
pole per year for the life of the franchise.
