      (5)   When any vehicle is left abandoned upon public right-of-way in
excess of two days from the date it was first reported or observed by officers;
      (6)   When officers recover a vehicle reported stolen and the owner
cannot be located, or is unable or unwilling to effect the removal of the
vehicle within a reasonable amount of time not to exceed one hour, or the
preservation and collection of evidence requires removal;
      (7)   Where the vehicle has any evidentiary value, has directly or
indirectly been involved in the commission of a crime, has been used to
transport any person who has committed any offense involving the use of a
firearm, or was directly or indirectly associated with a drive-by shooting;
      (8)   When a police officer effects the arrest of the owner or operator
of a vehicle out of said vehicle, and no person immediately present can
lawfully or reasonably be given custody of such vehicle;
      (9)   When a vehicle bears a license plate which has expired for a period
in excess of 90 days, bears a license plate which has been altered or tampered
with, or bears a temporary paper tag which has been expired for a period in
excess of 90 days, or bears no license plate which could be in conformance with
the State Vehicle License Act (47 O.S. § 1101);
      (10)   Any place, including place of residence when a police officer
effects the arrest of the operator of the vehicle, out of said vehicle, and the
operator is found to have operated the vehicle under any of the following
violations: reckless driving; careless driving; driving under the influence of
drugs and alcohol; driving while impaired; driving under a suspended, revoked
or denied license; driving with no state driver’s license; eluding a police
officer, duty to give information and render aid or otherwise involved in a hit
and run accident; or
      (11)   When a vehicle is not compliant with the State Vehicle Compulsory
Insurance Law (47 O.S. § 7-606).
   (C)   Impound fee. Any vehicle impounded under the authority granted herein
shall be stored and held until a written order for its release, signed by an
authorized officer of the city, has been issued. The proper city authority to
authorize the release of an impounded vehicle shall be any of the following:
Police Chief, City Manager, City Judge, City Attorney or City Clerk. Such order
of release shall be conditioned upon the payment of an impound fee in the
amount of $50 by the person to whom the release is issued. This impound fee
shall be independent of any fines, costs or fees which may be assessed from
citations issued to any person for violation of traffic laws or other ordinance
violations involving the impounded vehicle. This fee is also independent of any
costs associated with the individual wrecker services used by the city and
independent of any fees charged by the impoundment facility.
   (D)   Redemption of impounded vehicle. Presentation of the order of release
at the place of impoundment, together with payment or tender of payment of all
impoundment costs and accrued storage charges due, shall entitle the person
presenting such release to obtain possession of such vehicle.
(Ord. 2013-01, passed 4-2-2013)
ARTICLE 20. PARKING METERS
§ 22-2001 PARKING METERS.
   [Reserved.]
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012)
ARTICLE 21. SECURITY VERIFICATION
§ 22-2101 REQUIREMENT TO CARRY SECURITY VERIFICATION.
   Every operator of a motor vehicle registered in this state shall, while
operating or using such vehicle, carry either an operator’s or owner’s security
verification form issued by a carrier, providing the operator is not excluded
from coverage thereon; or an equivalent form issued by the Department of Public
Safety, reflecting liability coverage, which shall be produced by any driver
thereof upon request for inspection by any law enforcement officer of the city,
and, in case of a collision, the form shall be shown upon request to any person
affected by the collision.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012)
§ 22-2102 DISMISSAL.
   Any person producing proof in court that a current security verification
form or equivalent form which has been issued by the Department reflecting
liability coverage for such person was in force at the time of the alleged
offense shall be entitled to a dismissal of such charge.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012)
§ 22-2103 COURT CLERK TO FORWARD ABSTRACT.
   Upon conviction, bond forfeiture or deferral of sentence, the court clerk
shall forward an abstract to the Department of Public Safety within ten days
reflecting the action taken by the court.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012)
ARTICLE 22. SEAT BELTS
§ 22-2201 OPERATORS AND FRONT SEAT PASSENGERS REQUIRED TO WEAR SAFETY BELTS.
   Every operator and front seat passenger of a passenger car operated in this
state shall wear a properly adjusted and fastened safety seat belt system,
required to be installed in the motor vehicle when manufactured pursuant to
Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard 208. For the purpose of this section,
PASSENGER CAR shall mean AUTOMOBILE, as defined in state law, except that
PASSENGER CAR shall not include trucks, pickup trucks, truck-tractors,
recreational vehicles, vans, motorcycles or motorized bicycles.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012)
§ 22-2202 APPLICATION.
   This section shall not apply to an operator or passenger of a passenger car
in which the operator or passenger possesses a written verification form from a
physician licensed in this state that he or she is unable to wear a safety seat
belt system for medical reasons; provided, that the issuance of such
verification by a physician, in good faith, shall not give rise to, nor shall
such physician thereby incur, any liability whatsoever in damages or otherwise,
to any person injured by reason of such failure to wear a safety seat belt
system. This section shall not apply to an operator of a motor vehicle who is a
route carrier of the U.S. Postal Service.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012)
§ 22-2203 REPEALED.
   This section was repealed by Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012)
§ 22-2204 VIOLATION AND PENALTIES.
   Any person convicted of violating §
22-2201 of this article shall be punished by a fine of $10 and shall pay court
costs of $15; provided, that the Department of Public Safety shall not assess
points to the driving record of any licensed or unlicensed person convicted of
a violation of §
22-2201 of this article.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012)

ARTICLE 24. VEHICLES EXCEEDING A GROSS CARRYING CAPACITY OF FIVE TONS
§ 22-2401 RESTRICTIONS FOR VEHICLES EXCEEDING GROSS CARRYING CAPACITY OF FIVE
TONS WITH EXCEPTIONS.
   It shall be unlawful to operate any vehicle in that portion of the city,
zoned for residential use, when the carrying capacity of said vehicle exceeds
five tons. It shall be unlawful to operate a vehicle in excess of such carrying
capacity rating in such areas except for the following:
   (A)   School buses;
   (B)   Recreational vehicles going to and from a specific residence;
   (C)   Any vehicle operated by the city, the county, the state and/or the
United States of America and/or the affiliates of such agencies carrying out
specific governmental functions; and
   (D)   Ambulances or other, similar emergency vehicles.
(Ord. 2012-09, passed 12-4-2012)
ARTICLE 25. VALIDITY AND PENALTY
§ 22-2501 VALIDITY.
   The invalidity of any section or provision of this chapter shall not
invalidate other sections or provisions thereof.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012)
§ 22-2502 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person, firm or corporation who violates any provision of this
chapter shall be guilty of a traffic offense and, upon conviction thereof,
shall be fined in any amount not exceeding $200, plus costs. Each day upon
which a violation continues shall be deemed a separate offense.
   (B)   The fine for any other ordinance violation not otherwise specifically
addressed in these ordinances (whether in this chapter or elsewhere) shall be
$200, plus costs.
   (C)   (1)   The costs to be imposed in each Municipal Court case in which
there is a finding of guilt or a plea of guilt or no contest, or in which the
defendant does not make an appearance shall be as follows:
         (a)   City of Lexington: $22;
         (b)   CLEET: $9;
         (c)   Forensics: $5;
         (d)   AFIS: $5; and
         (e)   Police and fire training: $3.
      (2)   Total cost in each case to be assessed: $44.
(Ord. 2012-02, passed 7-10-2012; Ord. 2016-05, passed 8-2-2016)

§ 23-203 FEES FOR PROCEEDINGS PERTAINING TO ANNEXATION.
   A fee of $50 is set for all proceedings pertaining to annexation. Any person
desiring to annex any property to the city shall pay to the City Clerk a fee of
$50 concurrent with the filing of the petition for annexation.
§ 23-204 PETITION FOR ANNEXATION SUBMITTED TO PLANNING COMMISSION FOR APPROVAL
PRIOR TO ACTION BY CITY COUNCIL.
   It is hereby required that any petition for annexation be submitted to the
Planning Commission as soon as practical after the filing of the petition. The
Planning Commission shall either approve or disapprove of the petition by
majority vote. In the event the petition is approved, it may be set before the
City Council at a regularly scheduled meeting. In the event the petition is not
approved, the applicant may appeal the decision to the City Council.

ARTICLE 4. VACATING LOT
§ 23-401 LOT 7 BLOCK 25.
   (A)   Background. Lot 7, Block 25, City of Lexington, was deeded to the city
on October 28, 1968, by quitclaim deed from Robert F. Calonkey. The property is
in a residential area and has never been used by the city, is not suitable for
any current or future use, and should be sold to allow full utilization of such
land by private owners to the ultimate advantage of the public.
   (B)   Sale recommended. After careful consideration of possible land use by
the city, the City Council has determined that the public interest of the city
is best served by a sale of said property.
   (C)   Certification. It is hereby certified that Lot 7, Block 25, has not
been improved or used for any public purposes to date; nor can any future use
for same for public purposes be reasonably anticipated.
   (D)   Sale. A sale of Lot 7, Block 25, is hereby authorized and directed,
the same to be done by a sale to the highest bidder after publication of the
notice of such sale.
CHAPTER 24: DISCRIMINATION
Section
Article 1. Grievance Procedure
24-101 Filing complaint

ARTICLE 1. GRIEVANCE PROCEDURE
§ 24-101 FILING COMPLAINT.
   (A)   Any person who feels that he or she has been discriminated against on
the basis of handicapped status in admission to, or access to, or treatment in
any of the city’s programs and activities, or in employment, shall make a
formal complaint in writing to the Civil Service Board of the city. Components
of the written complaint should include:
      (1)   Statement of the complaint;
      (2)   Names of person and/or persons involved; and
      (3)   Documentation of facts.
   (B)   The formal complaint and all supporting documentation shall be filed
with the City Clerk, who shall be the person responsible to coordinate efforts
to comply with all prohibitions applicable to the city concerning
discrimination against qualified individuals because of handicapped status.
   (C)   The grievance procedure included in this chapter is adopted to comply
with the requirements of §§ 51 through 55 of the revenue sharing regulations as
published in the Federal Register on October 17, 1983, and shall apply to all
persons included within the scope of said federal revenue sharing regulations.
§ 24-102 HEARING ON COMPLAINT.
   The City Clerk shall notify the Civil Service Board of the complaint, and
the Board shall then set a hearing on the complaint. The City Clerk shall give
the complaining party not less than 15 days’ notice of the hearing date. At
said hearing, the complaining party shall have the burden of proof. Any oral or
documentary evidence may be received by the Board. Each party shall have the
right to present, in person or by counsel, his or her case or defense, by oral
or documentary evidence, to submit rebuttal evidence, and to conduct such
examination and cross-examination as may be required for a full and true
disclosure of the facts.
§ 24-103 FINDINGS AND RECOMMENDATION.
   Within 30 days after the hearing date, the Civil Service Board shall file
its written findings and recommendation for disposition of the complaint with
the City Clerk.
§ 24-104 RIGHT TO APPEAL BOARD DECISION.
   (A)   If the complaining party is not satisfied with the outcome of the
hearing, he or she may appeal the decision of the Civil Service Board to the
City Council. The appeal must be filed in writing with the City Clerk within
ten days following the adverse decision.
   (B)   The City Council shall then set a review hearing and shall give the
complaining party not less than ten days’ notice of said hearing. The City
Council shall have the right to review the evidence presented at the prior
hearing and may make any reasonable inquiry it feels necessary to resolve the
matter. The decision of the City Council shall be final.
§ 24-105 CIVIL SERVICE BOARD ESTABLISHED.
   There is established a Civil Service Board comprised of three members to be
appointed by the City Council. Said Board members shall serve for a term of one
year.
